The Independent reacts to Crawford's masterful win over Canelo in Vegas

Tonight, Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli will square off in a world-title fight in Riyadh, despite deadly attacks on the Saudi city in recent weeks.

Alvarez will fight for the first time in 13 months, having undergone elbow surgery after his points loss to Terence Crawford last year, and the Mexican icon will enter this bout as the challenger.

Mbilli was the interim WBC super-middleweight champion until Crawford retired in December, at which point the unbeaten Cameroon was elevated.

The 31-year-old and Canelo, 36, will headline at ANB Arena tonight, despite recent strikes on Riyadh by the Yemen-aligned Houthis – attacks that have injured more than 300 people and killed at least 21, per Saudi authorities.

A loss for Canelo here could signal the start of the end, for a fighter who has long been the face of boxing. How much does he have left? Follow live updates and results below:

News.title: Canelo vs Mbilli: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight tonight
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this evening, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh.

Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks, Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months, after he was outpointed by fellow great Terence Crawford in Las Vegas.

• FOLLOW LIVE: All the build-up to Canelo vs Mbilli

Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record.

open image in gallery Canelo Alvarez (right) at the weigh-in for his fight with Terence Crawford ( Getty )

Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired.

Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know.

When is the fight?

Canelo vs Mbilli will take place on Saturday 31 October at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card is expected to begin at 4pm GMT (9am PT / 11am CT / 12pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at 8.30pm GMT (1.30pm PT / 3.30pm CT / 4.30pm ET).

How can I watch it?

The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view at a cost of £24.99 ($79.99 in the US), and on DAZN Ultimate Tier – which is priced at £24.99 per month. You can purchase the fight or an Ultimate Tier subscription here.

Will the event go ahead, and why is this a question?

The organisation of this fight card had been the subject of intense speculation in recent weeks, due to numerous deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airports. Per Saudi authorities, more than 300 people have been left injured and at least 21 dead, due to strikes by the Yemen-aligned Houthis.

The international airport was reopened, but the US Department of State urged citizens to “reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting”, while areas near the Yemen border were listed as such: “do not travel due to terrorism”.

However, one undercard bout was cancelled, as first reported by journalist Dan Rafael, who said Lindolfo Delgado would “probably not” face Arthur Biyarslanov; Delgado and his team had reportedly not made travel plans, although Biyarslanov had already arrived in Riyadh. News.title: Princess Kate shares Halloween picture of Prince Louis for first time
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Princess of Wales has shared a glimpse of her Halloween festivities as she shared a never seen before picture of Prince Louis on Saturday.

In the picture taken by Catherine in Norfolk, the young prince can be seen about to put his arms around a large pumpkin. Dressed in a blue raincoat and red wellies he shares a cheeky smile as he looks down at the seasonal favourite.

The caption shared on Kensington Palace’s official Instagram reads: “Happy Halloween [pumpkin emoji] Prince Louis, aged 1, photographed by The Princess of Wales.”

The Princess of Wales shared the picture on her Instagram account ( princeandprincessofwales on Instagram )

Fans praised the picture as of the one-year-old as “adorable” as one wrote: “Aw the pumpkin is nearly as big as Prince Louis. Cute photograph.”

Another added: “He's adorable! Happy Halloween to W,C,G,C and L!!”

Others noted the similarities to Louis’ older brother George, writing: “Adorable! Wow looks so much like George here!” and “So cute. I thought it was Prince George.”

Some also pointed out the young prince’s likeness to his mum and dad, commenting: “Such a beautiful boy. 99 per cent Middleton” and “Looks so like Prince William at that age!”.

The Royal family does not formally celebrate Halloween, but the Wales’ have been known to enjoy the festivities with their children privately.

It comes after Kate made a private visit to mental health support charity Dose Of Nature in west London last week, meeting staff and people helped by the organisation, which provides clinically-led "nature prescriptions" to boost wellbeing.

Visiting Pensford Field, the charity’s site near Kew, she met with clinicians to learn more about their pioneering mental health support and meet with those who had benefitted.

News.title: Tottenham ease to win over Crystal Palace and pile more pressure on Pierre Sage
News.content:
For the first time in more than 600 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off after just 13 minutes, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two, and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

More to follow...

News.title: Northampton’s brilliant comeback win over Gloucester marred by Mitchell injury
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

News.title: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot
News.content:
David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

News.title: Trump administration loses grip on bird flu, experts warn
News.content:
The Trump administration has been criticised for losing control of a bird flu outbreak that has spread among mink and cattle farms across the United States.

The H5N1 virus has infected around 1,000 people since it was first detected in the late 1990s, killing roughly half of them. While it currently does not spread among humans, scientists have long worried that it could trigger a pandemic, and that each human infection raises the risk of the virus mutating.

A new variant emerged in 2020 and has since spread to millions of birds and hundreds of animal species across the globe, leading to devastating losses in both wildlife and farmed livestock and poultry.

While some countries have introduced tough measures to curb its spread, including mandatory culls of infected animals, “flockdowns” (where birds are kept indoors) and vaccination of farm workers who handle at-risk livestock, experts say the US is allowing the virus to run rampant.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged unchecked on a Utah farm that raises thousands of mink for fur, news outlet ProPublica reported last week.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

Mink have very similar respiratory systems to humans, increasing the risk that a virus can spread between the animals and people, and undergo a process known as “reassortment”, when two or more viruses mix together to make a new, more dangerous strain.

Sports.title: Bizarre moment fan hurls a CRUTCH at referee during heated EFL clash as three red cards dished out in first half alone
Sports.content:
Next

AN EFL referee had a CRUTCH thrown at him as tempers flared at the end of the game.

Oldham Athletic suffered a 1-0 loss at home to Crawley Town and the hosts’ fans were not happy.



As the referee, David Rock, left the pitch, a video has surfaced of an angry fan throwing his crutch at the official.

The club is yet to make a comment about the incident but the supporter is sure to be in trouble if he can be identified.



It’s not the first time refs have felt the brunt of supporters’ frustrations, but they might have a case this time.

There were two red cards for Oldham in just the first half.

The referee dismissed both players for straight red cards and that led to rock-bottom Crawley getting just their second win in 11 games.

Oldham had their numbers reduced as early as the 14th minute, with Kai Payne first shown a straight red card for a late challenge on Danilo Orsi.

Kane Drummond then followed on the half hour mark when he raised his boot to control a high ball and met Kai Jennings head.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Oldham boss Micky Mellon, though disappointed, insisted he would not play the victim after the two red cards.



He said: “I’m really proud of my players, really proud of the football club, the supporters for an unbelievable response under unbelievably trying circumstances and we will look at the positives that come out of it.

“We remained a threat the whole game and we’ll be disappointed that a few things don’t fall for us there.

“But only pride, and I mean that, I’m not going to play the victim in how everybody with an Oldham connection – fans, players, staff – responded to a very trying afternoon with real guts and a lot of real

good character from everybody concerned, and we will take that forward with us.”

Sports.title: Meet footballer’s model wife who ‘just missed the Wag era’ after marrying retired former Tottenham star
Sports.content:
Next

THE WIFE of a former Spurs star has made a playful jab about missing out on a glitzy WAG lifestyle.

Rhianne Starbuck is a glamorous entrepreneur and former actress and model.



But she doesn’t reckon she can add Wag to that list despite her marriage to former Tottenham and Norwich midfielder Paul McVeigh, 48.

The pair tied the knot in 2021, more than a decade after the former Northern Ireland international hung up the boots.



But that did not stop Starbuck from making a playful reference to his playing days, as she shared a video of the couple to her 5,000 Instagram followers.

The video also included moments from McVeigh’s matches as part of a Spurs legends team, despite making just three league appearances for the side.



She captioned the video: “Married a former pro footballer just after he retired.

“Missed the Wag era and skipped straight to the Spurs legend era.”

Starbuck has former acting credits in British shows like Emmerdale and Fresh Meat.

She has also modelled between acting jobs as she continued to audition for roles.



But she has taken a step back from the small screen as her family with McVeigh grew.

Now a new career endeavour has brought her closer than ever to her husband – after the pair co-founded a business together.

The duo are the mastermind behind Speakify, a platform through which people can book celebrity speakers to attend events.

Stars listed on the platform include former F1 team principal Geunther Steiner, Ex-NFL star Justin Forsett and footballing icons like Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic and Hugo Lloris.

Sports.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta sees red as Palace striker wipes out TWO Tottenham stars in horror challenge after just 12 minutes
Sports.content:
Next

JEAN-PHILIPPE MATETA saw a red card after a horror tackle that took out TWO Spurs players.

The Crystal Palace forward was sent off just 12 minutes into his side’s trip to the Tottenham Hotspur stadium.



The Frenchman was at full pelt as he tried to beat Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky Van de Ven to a ball in behind.

But he was not quite quick enough as Van de Ven tipped the ball away right as he slid to reach it.



Instead his extended studs made grisly contact with the defender’s Achilles, while Van Hecke’s momentum took him tumbling on top of the pair on the floor.

Referee Michael Oliver originally deemed the challenge to be worthy of a yellow card.



But a brief trip to the VAR monitor was enough to convince him of the contact’s severity, and he quickly upgraded the caution to a red card.

It was far from a dream start for under-pressure boss Pierre Sage, with the Eagles entering the fixture 18th in the league.

And Archie Gray was on hand to compound that misery barely ten minutes after Mateta’s sending off.

The 20-year-old appeared unmarked at the back post to head home a Mohammed Kudus corner delivery and open the scoring.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Palace elected not to make any substitutions in the immediate wake of the red card, with Yeremy Pino and Dwight McNeil left as the most advanced players on the pitch in red and blue.

It was a disappointing end to just the forward’s third start in the Premier League this season, having been eased back in recent weeks from a hamstring injury sustained after Palace’s opener against Everton.

Sports.title: Hull 2 Ipswich 2: Oli McBurnie and Julio Enciso on target again as plucky pair trade timely blows to share points
Sports.content:
Next

HULL showed fight to avoid another fright and pick up a fifth Premier League draw in seven winless games.

It looked to be another horror show for the Tigers when Florentino’s first goal in English football put Ipswich ahead.



With 13 defeats on Halloween they have the most of any side in Football League history.

But Hull rose from a hellish start with a battling second-half display as goals from Tim Iroegbunam and Oli McBurnie – his second in successive games – put them in front.



Julio Enciso’s screamer, though, gave Gary O’Neil’s men a point their first-half efforts deserved.

Tigers keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis was lucky in the 16th minute when he was slow to clear in his box and got into a right muddle and just managed to nudge the ball away before Emersonn could take advantage.

And there was another reprieve for the hosts in the 34th minute when a corner caused problems and Enciso nodded in from close range, but the goal was ruled out for a foul just beforehand by Abdul Fatawu on McBurnie.

Summer signing Florentino – who left relegated Burnley after a permanent move following a season-long loan from Benfica – paid a chunk of his £16 million fee with his 22nd-minute strike.

Abdoul Ouattara picked out the Portuguese midfielder, who smashed his finish inside Konstantinos Tzolakis’ near post.

Hull failed to have a first-half shot on target for the third time this term.

But when they finally did in the 58th minute, midfielder Iroegbunam netted his own first Prem goal to level in fine style.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Boss Sergej Jakirovic had sacrificed centre-back John Egan for Matt Crooks to provide some muscle in midfield.

And the trick worked a treat as Town were finally tested and Iroegbunam collected a McBurnie pass into space on the right and was allowed to saunter forward without pressure and lash past visiting keeper Christian Walton.

That meant no clean sheet for Town again as their wait for a top-flight shutout extended to 28 games – since December 2024 at Chelsea.

And they led ten minutes later when Florentino fouled Mohamed Belloumi and up stepped McBurnie, who struck against Brentford last weekend, to fire into the corner.



But a fine fourth goal of the game followed when Enciso scrapped 30 yards out and showed neat footwork before whipping a fabulous curling finish into the top corner.

Only a touch by a stretching Walton denied Brooke Norton-Cuffy as Hull almost snatched a first win since August.

Sports.title: Brentford 2 Nottingham Forest 0: Pressure grows for Oliver Glasner as new club suffer fourth defeat in five outings
Sports.content:
Next

NIKOLA MILENKOVIC became only the sixth different Nottingham Forest player to score a Premier League goal this season – but sadly it was into his own net.

And the Serbian defender’s day went downhill from there as he also got the final touch before Brentford sealed a precious home win that keeps them in touch with the top six.



Milenkovic’s ghastly own-goal heralded yet another miserable performance with new boss Oliver Glasner’s position surely now coming under pressure.

His predecessor Vitor Pereira lasted less than six months in the job and much of that was during the close season.



What battling spirit Glasner’s side was hoping to display fizzled out after just half an hour when Milenkovic turned the ball past his own keeper.

Goals have been like gold dust at the City Ground this season so it’s something you guess that at least one Forest name was on the scoresheet.

If Glasner can now only persuade his players to kick in the right direction things will soon turn around. That is assuming he gets that long to do it.

Forest have been largely considered unlucky this season and given the benefit of the doubt that their ability to create chances would eventually pay off.



They boast the lowest goals scored tally in the division with six – even lower than bottom club Sunderland.

And record signing Liam Delap did not get anywhere near adding to his solitary strike since signing for a club-record £45million in the summer.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Another miserable and frustrating day ended for the former Chelsea man with 35 minutes left, replaced by veteran Chris Wood.

Even when opportunities did arise, such as James McAtee finding himself in yards of space with the home side backing off in the first half, Forest could not follow through and tuck the ball away with the midfielder skewing a shot hopelessly wide.



Brentford should have been out of sight but were dragged down by Forest’s sleepwalking style.

The breakthrough came on the half hour with a low-level goal kick by Caomihn Kelleher spearing through the midfield to find Dango Outtara on the right wing and catching his marker Murillo on the hop.

The Brentford forward charged to the by-line and hit a low cross which cannoned off the outstretched defensive foot of Milenkovic and deceived keeper Matz Sels from close range to gift the Bees a goal.

Milenkovic then committed a foul right on the edge of his own area that enabled Mathias Jensen to smack the Forest bar with a free-kick.

And with 14 minutes left, Bees’ sub Jaidon Anthony burst down the right wing then squared for Igor Thiago to hammer the ball home via Milenkovic’s sticking out leg to make it 2-0.



It ends a run of four games without a win for Brentford and the win keeps them two points above seventh-placed Bournemouth.

Sports.title: James Trafford makes horror error as England keeper left red-faced in Leeds’ painful 2-0 loss to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Next

WEREWOLF costumes are in short supply at this time of year – but James Trafford served up an even bigger Halloween howler.

The Leeds goalkeeper’s short pass out towards Ao Tanaka in the 31st minute truly was a shocking misjudgment.

And he was powerless to prevent interceptor Justin Kluivert squaring the ball for Evanilson to slot into an open goal, setting the Cherries up for a sixth consecutive win to nil, with Amine Adli adding a second late on.



Trafford’s stock has been rising this season but this was a reminder of why Pep Guardiola demoted him to deputy behind Gianluigi Donnarumma at Manchester City.



It was almost a carbon copy of the slack pass that was picked off by Pape Sarr and punished by Joao Palhinha in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham during Trafford’s brief run in the City side last year.

And it was the catalyst for a dramatic momentum shift in a game which, up to that point, had been Leeds’ for the taking.

Dan James was out to impress on his first Premier League start of the season, and banked early credit with travelling fans by skinning ex-Leeds man Tyler Adams with a crafty turn.



He then skipped past James Hill and rolled a low ball into the box, which was inches away from the end of Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s sliding boot.

It all came together for the visitors in the 11th minute when Jayden Bogle, Harry Wilson and James Justin combined in a flowing team move to tee up Calvert-Lewin, who bundled in.

But a VAR review showed that Calvert-Lewin’s arm got the final touch. The fact it was completely accidental counts for nothing when it leads directly to a goal.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Trafford’s gaffe followed, and Bournemouth are the last team you’d want to be chasing in this form.



AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa were all steamrollered 3-0 in the three games leading into this one.

And by the second half they had shaken off their stiffness, having played in midweek while Leeds kicked their feet up.

In-form Marcus Tavernier curled a free-kick around the wall which needed saving by Trafford, before Rayan fizzed a half-volley wide from a narrow angle.

Substitute Eli Kroupi then produced with a dazzling nutmeg and reverse pass in stoppage time to set up Adli for his third goal in four games.

Sports.title: Angulo dodges VAR red after HAIR pull on Coventry’s Sakamoto as Sunderland sink further into relegation mire in 3-1 loss
Sports.content:
Next

SUNDERLAND star Nilson Angulo avoided a red card despite pulling Coventry man Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s hair on Saturday afternoon.

The Ecuadorian might well have got away with one, as his side lost 3-1.



With new rules forbidding players from pulling hair, some might have assumed that Angulo being sent off was a given.

But even after a VAR check Angulo got away with it and didn’t suffer the same fate as team-mate Dan Ballard, who was sent off for pulling Wolves man Tolu Arokodare’s hair last season.



Coventry took advantage of a Black Cats Halloween horror show to cruise past Sunderland and lift themselves out of the relegation zone.

Strikes by Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni sunk Sunderland despite Enzo Le Fee’s consolation penalty kick.



The result piles pressure on boss Regis Le Bris amid the visitors’ dire start to the campaign.

This time last year, Le Bris’ side had picked up 17 points already and were sitting in the Champions League spots.

This season they have managed just one win and are rock bottom of the pack on five points.

This match had been dubbed as a relegation six-pointer, which felt a little premature given the league is not even a quarter of the way done.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But both sides knew how important three points could be, with Coventry 19th in the table and Sunderland propping up the rest of the league ahead of kickoff.

Despite that, only one side looked like they wanted to fight for survival.

Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues were a level above their old Championship foes for the majority, showing more technical nous, fight and character from the off.

It took the hosts 17 minutes to make the most of Sunderland’s calamitous defending.

Trai Hume attempted a clearance from a looping Milan van Ewjik cross, only for his lacklustre efforts to bounce off Luke O’Nien and directly into the path of Sakamoto.



The Japan international lashed home the loose ball first time, delightfully curling it into the bottom corner to start Sunderland’s afternoon of misery.

Awoniyi added a second in the 37th minute when he caught O’Nien napping on the ball, dispossessing the midfielder in the final third before carving his way into the box and lashing home.

His effort deflected off the backside of Omar Alderete, who would soon suffer the same fate for Cov’s third.

Just after the break, Rudoni let fly with a driven effort from distance and Alderete’s attempted block wrong-footed goalkeeper Robin Roefs to put Coventry three up and out of sight.

Not even a second half penalty, given after the ball struck the hand of Ethan Pinnock from an O’Nien effort, could change Sunderland’s fortunes.



Despite Le Fee slotting it past Carl Rushworth from 12 yards, Cov were already out of sight.

Any potential for a dramatic late comeback was further extinguished when Alderete received two yellow cards in nine added minutes, earning his marching orders.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Coventry have now won three of their last five games and finally look to be finding their feet in the top flight.



Sunderland, meanwhile, seem unable to cope with their European schedule and are already staring down the barrel of a shock relegation back to the Championship.

Sports.title: Norris pips Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying
Sports.content:
McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.001s in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix to set up a thrilling qualifying.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc had topped both of Friday's practice sessions but McLaren and Mercedes showed their hand to outpace the Monegasque driver by one tenth of a second.

Antonelli is likely to become world champion in Sunday's race as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the Formula 1 drivers' title.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was fourth while Red Bull appear to be out of the pole position battle as Max Verstappen was 0.351s off the pace, but there seems to be a genuine three-team fight at the front for qualifying later on Saturday at 9pm (build-up from 8pm), live on Sky Sports F1.

Regardless of what he does in qualifying, Verstappen cannot start on pole position as he and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson have a one-grid place penalty for colliding in second practice on Friday.

The stewards called the incident "unacceptable", with both drivers admitting the clash was "unnecessary and clumsy".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP - the clash would eventually lead to both drivers receiving a grid penalty

More drama took place before final practice on Saturday as Haas made the shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the remainder of the weekend.

The team provided no reason for replacing Ocon, but confirmed the Frenchman was not suffering from illness.

Haas recently confirmed that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad, with Brazilian youngster Rafael Camara signed as his replacement.

Hirakawa, a 24 Hours of Le Mans winner, has taken part in several practice sessions for Haas over the last two years and was 19th in final practice, six tenths down on team-mate Oliver Bearman.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Esteban Ocon used team radio to question Haas’ decision to change his run plan during second practice in Mexico City

Is anyone favourite for pole in Mexico?

Nobody delivered their best lap at the first time of asking in final practice on the soft tyre runs, leaving things even more open for qualifying given the teams usually optimise their setup and tyre characteristics to be quick on their first flying lap.

Leclerc visibly was sliding his car on most of his flying laps and it still feels Ferrari have more pace in the car, which neither driver showed in final practice as Lewis Hamilton languished in sixth ahead of Mercedes' George Russell in seventh.

"I think they can still be in the fight but it looked challenging [for Ferrari]," said Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick.

"Both drivers, Charles in particular, those first few laps on the soft tyre is where it didn't really happen for them. I think that's the challenge, you have to be able to put the lap in when it counts.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Anthony Davidson explained why Ferrari could be strong this weekend

"I think Ferrari's potential is higher, but it didn't feel like they managed to get the potential out of it early on the soft-tyre runs.

"I think they're still the dark horse favourites, or maybe not such dark horses, but I think it's gong to be so close between those top three teams."

Ferrari topped all three practice sessions last week in Austin before fading away in qualifying as Antonelli took pole position.

The Scuderia will hope a similar scenario does not repeat itself in Mexico City, with the added threat of McLaren being a force at the front for the first time in over a month.

Sports.title: St Johnstone fight back from Steward dismissal to take point at Kilmarnock
Sports.content:
St Johnstone battled to a terrific 2-2 draw with 10 men as Kilmarnock's woes continued.

Simo Valakari's side were at a disadvantage from the 13th minute following the dismissal of goalkeeper Toby Steward for handling outside of his area.

Yet despite going behind immediately after the red card to Cathal McCarthy's first goal, Saints were never out of the game.

They levelled through Danny Schmidt after 40 minutes, only for Djenairo Daniels to restore the home lead before half-time.

However, a breakaway goal from Joel Cotterill after 65 minutes was enough to claim an unlikely point.

The game was turned on its head after just 10 minutes when Steward was sent off following a costly error. The on-loan Portsmouth goalkeeper came rushing out of his penalty area to deal with a long ball, with Joe Hugill bearing down on goal.

Steward appeared to have time to take a step back before gathering the ball, but VAR advised referee Matthew MacDermid to review the incident for a denial of a goalscoring opportunity. The goalkeeper was shown a red card.

Sinclair, brought on in place of Taylor Steven, was immediately thrown into the action and had to pick the ball out of his net with his first touch.

From the resulting set-piece, Kilmarnock worked the ball for Greg Kiltie to deliver an inswinging cross, which McCarthy met six yards out with a header to score the first goal of his loan spell from Hull City.

Image: Kilmarnock's Cathal McCarthy celebrates with team-mates after scoring to make it 1-0

Daniels thought he had doubled the lead after 31 minutes from a tight angle before an offside flag foiled him.

Kilmarnock's defensive problems first came back to bite them, even with the personnel advantage, five minutes before half-time.

Josh Fowler was denied by an excellent fingertip stop by German keeper Nico Mantl but, from the corner, Enes Alic's delivery was headed into the far corner by an unmarked Schmidt.

Kilmarnock did not dwell on their misfortune and hit straight back. Hugill scampered up the left flank and his cutback was buried by a brilliant backheel flick from Daniels.

Image: Kilmarnock's Cathal McCarthy celebrates with team-mates after scoring to make it 1-0

Aaron Tshibola missed a golden opportunity to put Saints to bed after 63 minutes. Hugill's brilliant backheel sent the DR Congo international through on goal, but his weak effort was straight at Sinclair.

Saints stunned Killie just two minutes later to level the scores once more.

The equaliser came after Kilmarnock's corner broke down, allowing Alic to pick out Cotterill with an excellent pass. The Welshman burst beyond two defenders before drilling a low finish into the net to make it 2-2.

Nicky Clescenco came within inches of restoring Killie's lead after Tyreece John-Jules robbed Diabate of possession.

Sinclair then kept Saints in the game, first pushing away George Stanger's effort before producing a superb reflex save to deny John-Jules from close range as Kilmarnock continued to search for a winner.

Sports.title: Bournemouth punish Trafford horror error to sink Leeds
Sports.content:
Bournemouth made it six wins on the spin in all competitions without conceding as they beat toothless Leeds 2-0.

Marco Rose's side have now beaten Sturm Graz, Sunderland, AC Milan, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Leeds without conceding in an extraordinary run of results.

They were given a helping hand by Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford, whose Halloween horror show gifted Bournemouth the lead as Evanilson capitalised on a hapless pass out from the back.

The response from Leeds never came as they mustered just one shot on target from their 10 attempts on goal to a backdrop of a lowly 0.61 worth of expected goals. They have now scored just twice in their last five Premier League games.

The visitors had been the better team before falling behind but could not prevent their winless run stretching to five top-flight games. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was denied a goal on his 50th appearance for the club after his 11th-minute finish was ruled out for a handball spotted by VAR.

Bournemouth wrapped up the points in injury-time when Junior Eli Kroupi provided a wondrous assist, that included a nutmeg, to provide Amine Adli with the second goal.

Trafford's moment of madness costs Leeds dearly

Image: Evanilson celebrates with Justin Kluivert after firing Bournemouth in front against Leeds

Sky Sports' Lewis Jones:

Football can be a cruel game, especially for goalkeepers.

Leeds were the better side against Bournemouth up until the first goal. They had started brightly, looked comfortable and were asking questions of the Cherries. Then came the moment that changed everything.

Trafford's headloss in possession, gifting the ball straight to Justin Kluivert, was an invitation Bournemouth simply could not refuse. Leeds were then chasing a game they had been controlling.

The psychological damage was just as significant as the scoreboard. Leeds never really recovered, their confidence drained by a moment of self-inflicted punishment. Bournemouth had been handed the perfect platform and made sure they took full advantage.

Trafford has earned rave reviews since joining Leeds and there is plenty to admire about his potential. But this was a timely reminder that the England international is far from the finished article.

Farke calls Trafford mistake an 'own goal'

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking about Trafford's mistake:

"It was self-inflicted, an own goal. This was decisive. Overall we played a good away game.

"We don't have to speak about [it]. He is a terrific young goalkeeper and has saved us points this season. It's a life of a football player. The sun isn't always shining. But he will save us way more points than perhaps he cost us today. We win together, we lose together. My recommendation is that he doesn't watch the game back. Football can have annoying days, it's an annoying day for him.

"I want a confident goalkeeper who plays out from the back. He normally spots the scene better. It's hard to explain. It's important that he has the skills to bypass. We all have poor days. He shouldn't change his game just after one mistake. It's tough to deal with but no complaints."

'Kroupi will be key for us, he's a difference maker'

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose:

"We conceded a goal, then lucky us [it was disallowed], from then we grew into the game. We won a high ball and scored an easy goal but it was hard work. It was an open game. It was a difficult game and a difficult opponent. I'm happy we solved the challenge.

"He [Junior Kroupi] could be a key factor for us this season. He's not yet 100 per cent fit but he understands the game and how he solves issues in tight situations. This is a guy who in the Premier League where you get space can make a difference. He worked hard today but he knows every metre to fill up his tank. He played 25 minutes today [Saturday] and we're going to increase his match time more and more."

Brilliant Bournemouth on the rise

Sports.title: Fadinger's penalty downs St Mirren to end Motherwell's winless run
Sports.content:
Lukas Fadinger's late penalty brought Motherwell's seven-game winless run to an end and delivered three much-needed Scottish Premiership points against out-of-sorts St Mirren.

A host of chances were passed up by Alfred Johansson's men during a dominant display, which would have brought greater reward had they discovered a clinical touch in front of goal before the spot-kick as they moved into ninth spot on the table.

Saints dropped down to eighth as Craig McLeish's side, whose recent poor run of form continues.

The Lanarkshire side should have been ahead in the 10th minute when Tawanda Maswanhise was allowed time and space to fire in a shot from 18 yards, but he wildly blasted the effort high over the crossbar.

Another golden opportunity arrived moments later when a low cross from Emmanuel Longelo had Maswanhise racing towards the far post and the Zimbabwean was inches away from converting.

That sustained pressure on the Saints goal continued unabated in an impressive opening by Well, who forced a series of corners with the Buddies being swamped by waves of attacks.

Tom Sparrow then reacted first to a loose ball at the edge of the box and his shot was parried wide by visiting goalkeeper Jacob Chapman as the hosts piled on the pressure.

It may have been wasteful by the hosts, but the invention and creative spark down the flanks and from midfield was a much-needed return to the style which the Fir Park side had been serving up earlier in the campaign.

Ibrahim Said was next to miss a glaring chance when he steered a shot straight at Chapman when clean through in the 24th minute.

Image: Motherwell's Tawanda Maswanhise (L) and St Mirren's Henry Fieldson in action at Fir Park

Saints had been let off the hook, but the Paisley side struggled to get themselves properly into the contest in a first half of little promise that they could breach the Motherwell goal as Joe Hodge went into the book for a lunge on Ryan Carr just before the break.

Martin Moormann rattled a volley inches over the top just seconds after the restart as the traffic continued to flow towards St Mirren's goal before Marcus Fraser saw yellow for a professional foul in the 52nd minute.

Another clear Motherwell miss came on the hour mark with Said swivelling inside the box and, from 16 yards, dragged the effort wide when he should have been busting the net.

St Mirren began building some pressure of their own in a bid to claim a smash-and-grab three points, but those hopes ended eight miutes from time as referee Don Robertson pointed to the spot after a VAR check for a Henry Fieldson handball.

Fadinger slammed home to secure a long-awaited for Motherwell and their under-pressure manager.

Sports.title: Forest fans boo their team as scoring woes continue in loss at Brentford
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest's poor goalscoring run continued as wasteful finishing contributed to a 2-0 defeat at Brentford – and they were booed off by their own angry fans.

"What the f******* hell was that?" sang the away fans as Brentford did not need to be particularly good to overcome Oliver Glasner's side and keep track with the Champions League places.

That anger was shared by Glasner himself in his post-match press conference, the head coach acknowledging things must change or Forest will be searching for their sixth manager since the start of last season.

"We have to accept it's not good enough," said the Austrian. "That's why it's for me, now time to change things."

Asked what those things are, Glasner replied: "Everywhere. And I feel I could see a few things from day No 1. I feel now that maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff. It's a clear way, I will tell what we want to do, what we have to do. And if the players buy in, we can have a turnaround. If not, the sixth manager will come in."

Nikola Milenkovic's own goal after good work from Dango Ouattara gave the Bees the lead - but there were no shots on target until the 76th minute, when Igor Thiago doubled the lead via a deflected strike.

Image: Igor Thiago celebrates after giving Brentford a 2-0 lead against Nottingham Forest

That was partly due to Forest's poor finishing. They had two golden chances to score, one in each half: James McAtee curled wide from inside the box after being given time and space to get there, before half-time substitute Ryan Yates headed over from four yards out.

Forest remain the lowest scorers in the Premier League this season with only six so far - and they wasted 14 shots before finally getting one on target in the 79th minute, a pea roller from McAtee that Caoimhin Kelleher gratefully collected.

Scoring and creating meaningful chances remains a concern for Glasner's Forest, who remain in the bottom three.

4: CHANCE! Mamadou Sangare volleys wide for Brentford after a corner was cleared to his path.

20: ANOTHER! Thiago is played into a good area but drags a shot wide of goal.

24: HUGE CHANCE! McAtee goes on a solo run into the Brentford penalty area but curls wide from inside the box.

30: GOAL! Ouattara is released from Caoimhin Kelleher's long-range ball and his cross is diverted into the box by Milenkovic.

38: OFF THE BAR! Mathias Jensen curls a free-kick which cannons off the top of the crossbar.

54: BIG MISS! Morgan Gibbs-White crosses for Yates who cannot convert from four yards out.

76: GOAL! Thiago makes it 2-0 after being set up by substitute Jaidon Anthony.

Does Glasner blame players for performance?

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner:

"No, they tried again. You can't say they had a lack of effort. But again, you feel you're controlling the game, you create a few good situations, and all of a sudden they're 1-0 down. It was the fourth goal we conceded from a long ball from a goalkeeper, so it's lack of awareness losing the duel, and we're 1-0 down.

"Then the players tried and tried. I think in the first 20 minutes in the second half, we just played in their half. Then I could see they're getting nervous. We're crossing and crossing and this and this.

"But again, if you always make some mistakes, or the same mistakes in defence that you've done, if in too many games you're not able to convert the chances you have, then we have to admit right now it's not good enough.

"For me, I don't want to talk about statistics and about whatever, because the reality is we didn't score a goal, we conceded two, we had enough set pieces, we didn't score again from a set piece, and it's not to blame. I take responsibility for everything. That's why I said, and I always take responsibility for the things I decided.

"I decided everything. It's just one person to blame, and that's me. That's why I say I can't and I won't continue in the same way as Oliver Glasner. I will change things. That's so clear for me, because otherwise, again, it's the same. You asked the fifth manager, I think you're asking the same question [that you gave to the other four].

"I think the performances are better than the ones [the other four] have been, but it's the same. And if things won't change, you will ask the sixth [manager to come in]."

Sherwood: Buck stops with Glasner and Marinakis won't hang about

Image: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis

Analysis fom Tim Sherwood on Soccer Saturday:

"They're not good enough, he's right about that. He's very honest with his appraisal of his side. They are not good enough [but] he's got to get on with it. There is nothing he can do until January. He ain't ging to be there in January

"They will lose next week against Manchester City and he'll get sacked in that international break. They will be on their next manager. Look at the history of this football club, they change managers.

"Marinakis, I quite admire his stance, Marinakis. He gives someone an opportunity - okay people might say he does not give him long enough - but he pulled that club from where they've been to the Premier League and he's made changes along the way.

"He doesn't suffer fools. He will not have anyone speak out against his football club. And I quite like it, he doesn't sit on his hands and wait, he just makes decisions and he will go and get another manager. He's probably saying we spent the money, we brought some new players into the football club, some of them you knew all about and you're not getting the best out of them.

"The buck stops with the manager and they can't change personnel at the moment they need to find someone who can get the best out of them and the position that they find themselves in, in the league, is not good enough."

Andrews: That was Brentford's best win of the season

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews:

"It's probably our best win of the season because you've got to show different traits to some of the other games.

"I think the schedule this week, for a start, hasn't been favourable to us. That's two cup rounds in a row where we've had the most condensed week out of anybody.

"Two difficult away trips and we didn't get the result we wanted to [against Sunderland], so there's that element to it as well.

"And then the opposition and how they play, how they try to set up and condense the pitch. It's pragmatic at times, they test you in different ways. They've got some very talented players that you have to keep quiet and you have to keep your concentration and focus.

"There was also some smart play today and leadership on show from our players that I really, really liked. On so many levels, I think it's a brilliant win."

Sports.title: Lankshear scores twice in Boro win
Sports.content:
In-form Will Lankshear bagged a brace as Middlesbrough maintained their position at the Championship summit with a comprehensive 3-0 victory over Charlton at the Riverside.

Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Lankshear netted twice to take his tally to 15 in all competitions.

While the early exchanges were not without the odd nervy moment for a home side who came into the match unbeaten in their last 10 league matches, a long throw into the Boro box led to a quick counter and a shot from the division's top scorer Lankshear, resulting in a corner.

Charlton's Tyler Bindon picked up a yellow card inside 10 minutes for a late challenge and the resulting free-kick led to a header into the side-netting from Riley McGree, which seemed to give the home team and supporters a lift.

The first goal came shortly after, with the tricky feet of Amario Cozier-Duberry on the right ensuring he found enough space to pull the back to the edge of the 18-yard box for Berhalter, who produced a tidy finish to the goalkeeper's right. Arthur Okonkwo may well feel he could have done better, however.

Charlton went on to produce a couple of half-chances themselves, including a close-range shot from a wide angle from Joe Rankin-Costello, which was comfortably saved by Radek Vitek.

A deep cross from Cozier-Duberry then found the ever-dangerous Tommy Conway all on his own at the back post, but his curling shot went narrowly wide, while just after the half-hour mark a long Charlton throw was headed goalwards by Miles Leaburn and had Vitek scrambling, but missed the target.

McGree was given a deserved yellow for a heavy challenge on Charlton's Kayne Ramsay in the opposition box after losing control of the ball, with Ramsay having to be replaced at half-time.

The second goal came shortly before the break, with Berhalter producing a sumptuous through ball to find Lankshear. Cries of offside from the away side were ignored by the linesman and Lankshear produced a tidy dink finish to double the lead.

Charlton had a couple of threatening moments at the start of the second half, but Middlesbrough soon took control, with a McGree shot over the bar followed by a curling strike from Cozier-Duberry that looked destined for the top corner but went narrowly wide.

After a couple of dangerous looking crosses from Middlesbrough captain Callum Brittain that were begging to be converted, the victory was finally sealed in the 82nd minute.

Within seconds of being introduced from the bench, Charlton's Nathaniel Chalobah slipped on the edge of his own box and the ball dropped kindly to Lankshear, whose left-foot strike emphatically found the top corner, taking his league tally to 13 goals in as many games.

Lankshear was replaced immediately afterwards with what looked like cramp, with another excellent afternoon's work done and dusted.

The managers

Middlesbrough's Kim Hellberg:

"It helps to play in a team like ours…I don't think there's many teams in Europe that create more chances than us. I think he has unbelievable team-mates around him that suit him very well.

"I think he's exactly the same boy that came through the doors some months ago. There's always a smile on his face, except when he misses chances, even in training.

"A lot of it is about being better every day and that's what you can control. I'm not thinking about what will happen after 46 games in May as that will not help anyone.

"I want to finish first or second of course, but for us it's all about being better."

Charlton's Nathan Jones:

"We felt we were well in the game, but then we never gave ourselves a chance really with that defending and second half we kept giving the ball away.

"We didn't do the basics well enough and we have to find a formula to improve. At the minute we're conceding goals we shouldn't concede.

"We came here last year with a weaker a squad and we kept a clean sheet. We defended for our lives and put our bodies on the line and they're not doing that now. That's the worrying thing and that's what we have to turn around."

Sports.title: Bristol City hit back late to stun Bolton
Sports.content:
Michael Skubala enjoyed the happiest of birthdays as Bristol City came from behind to stun Bolton 3-2 in the SkyBet Championship with an added-time Scott Twine winner.

The visitors trailed 2-1 with six minutes of normal time remaining but Sam Bell levelled before fellow substitute Twine ensured manager Skubala celebrated his 44th birthday with three points.

City's win was their first in five games while Wanderers have now gone three matches without victory and six weeks since their last success at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

Skubala's afternoon threatened to have an unhappy ending as Josh Sheehan and Sam Dalby put Bolton 2-1 up after Dom Ballard's fourth goal of the season fired the Robins into a 13th minute lead.

But Bell, a 78th minute replacement for Lorent Tolaj, tapped in Cam Pring's cross from close range before Twine converted from another substitute, Jed Wallace, three minutes into added time.

A section of the away fans had jeered Skubala's decision to take off Tolaj, who twice put the ball in the net only to be denied by an offside flag.

Trotters chief Steven Schumacher made eight changes from his team's previous 5-1 mauling by Middlesbrough while City were looking for a hat-trick of wins in the north west after successes at Preston and Burnley.

The treble was on when former Leyton Orient star Ballard tapped in Jason Knight's cross.

But the visitors led for just three minutes. There seemed little danger when Welsh international Sheehan, one of the three survivors from the Boro bashing, picked up possession. As defenders backed off Sheehan let fly from 25 yards, with goalkeeper Brad Collins well beaten.

That was the prelude to a chance-filled remaining half hour. Ballard teed up Tolaj, who forced a save from Jack Bonham - deputy for the injured Gavin Bazunu.

Tolaj should have done better and when he did find the net minutes later, his header was debatably ruled offside.

Collins denied Atsuki Ito before City fashioned a run of chances, none of which Luke McNally, Rio Cardines and Pring could convert.

However, Wanderers finished the half on the front foot and Ito struck Collins' right hand upright with a low shot and Sam Iling-Junior fired narrowly wide.

Tolaj's frustrating afternoon continued 10 minutes after the break. Played in by Ballard's pass, the Swiss striker clinically converted from 16 yards - only to be flagged offside again.

Bolton eventually hit the front after 57 minutes as Thierry Gale's cross was helped on by Ito and Dalby claimed the goal from close range.

Bonham came to Bolton's rescue, saving low down from McNally and then keeping out a low drive from Wallace.

Just as crucial was Collins stunning 83rd-minute save from Ruben Rodrigues. And instead of being 3-1 down City roared back to snatch victory.

The managers

Bolton's Steven Schumacher:

"It was a game we should win. We should definitely not lose it.

"For probably 80 minutes we were in complete control. They scored with their first attack while we should have had a goal to kill it off but we didn't take it.

"Ruben had a huge chance to make it 3-1 a minute before they went down the other end and scored.

"They are the small margins because if we go 3-1 they lose all their energy. But when they got their second goal it gave them a huge lift.

"We became a bit ragged after we had to make a change in the backline. The game became more stretched and they have some good players like every team in this league.

"But we can't keep conceding three goals if we are going to win games."

Bristol City's Michael Skubala:

"If they are turning at me, no problem. As long as they don't turn at the players, that is the most important thing. It is my job to take that pressure. But I will always make decisions I think will win us the game.

"You have to do that, to be fair to the lads. Tolly has been injured and only just made this game and was tiring.

"If I don't make those decisions then Sam Bell doesn't get a chance to show what he can do.

"We had a wobble in the second half but after that the lads were excellent. We created some big chances.

"But what I liked was our character. The subs coming on to impact the game is what you want.

"The group work hard and I love them to bits. They definitely won that game."
