Sports.title: Ayari on target as Brighton stun Manchester City to close gap on leaders
Sports.content:
Manchester City have lost two consecutive league games but no alarm should be sounded. Enzo Maresca’s fast-passing team were defeated on Saturday because Yasin Ayari took one of Brighton’s rare chances, the 11th-minute winner deriving from what appeared a wrongly awarded free-kick for Elliot Anderson’s “foul” on the same player.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be proud of victory here – and of being third. They are worth the lofty position and who would bet against Champions League qualification for them?

They can be proud of protecting their lead admirably because Maresca’s men kept coming at them. City’s problem was the final touch or finish and not creating enough for the lethal Erling Haaland.

When Nico O’Reilly, a second-half substitute, zipped the ball across goal towards the end, Iliman Ndiaye sprayed wide: a fair summation of what cost City.

Ndiaye and Josko Gvardiol were replaced after this by Phil Foden and Allan Elias as Maresca tried to salvage a point or better. It did not occur but his stewardship continues to impress, three months in.

City were slick throughout as when Ayyoub Bouaddi’s quick feet found Enzo Fernández and he poked the ball out to the left with a no-look pass that found the menacing Jérémy Doku.

View image in fullscreen Yasin Ayari opens the scoring in the first half. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

But they were made to look chumps when Ayari scored despite the move emanating from the free-kick given wrongly against Anderson. Lewis Dunk swept the dead ball right to Diego Gómez and from this point City slumbered. When Gómez crossed, Matheus Nunes missed his clearance, the ball came back in via Maxim De Cuyper and Ayari scored into an empty goal, with Gianluigi Donnarumma stranded.

As in City’s Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over Brighton here on Wednesday the visitors pummelled the hosts – for a period. City required a spark so Anderson stepped up, his snake-hips along the right creating space for a pinpoint ball that Ndiaye should have headed home not wide.

Quick Guide Manchester City 0-1 Brighton key facts Show • Brighton have beaten Manchester City away from home in any competition for the very first time, at the 18th attempt (D5 L12). • Manchester City have failed to score at home in the Premier League for the first time in 23 games, since a 2-0 defeat to Spurs in August 2025. • Brighton have won five of their last six Premier League matches, keeping a clean sheet in all five victories, indeed they have the most clean sheets (6) in the competition this season. • Manchester City have lost consecutive Premier League games for the first time since August 2025, which included a 2-1 victory for Brighton. • Manchester City had 21 shots against Brighton, their most attempts without scoring in a Premier League home game since November 2024 (23 against Spurs). • This was the first Saturday 3pm Premier League game between two sides in the top three since October 2019, when Liverpool, as leaders, beat third-place Leicester 2-1 at Anfield. Opta Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Senegal international next wowed with a throwback slaloming run which took him, from the right and near halfway into Brighton’s area. Suddenly the target gaped and if he had driven beyond Bart Verbruggen and not into the Brighton goalkeeper’s gloves it would have been a goal of the season contender.

It was the centrepiece of a swashbuckling response from City, as a Doku raid wreaked havoc along Brighton’s right and Haaland, Gvardiol and Fernández all might have found an equaliser.

If this thrust and cut recalled Pep Guardiola’s finer City vintages there was an added element of pace that is Maresca’s particular special sauce. A 50-yard diagonal speared from Anderson to the galloping Doku was another moment of high quality. And, as half-time neared, Haaland was the recipient after more Anderson scheming: the Norwegian adjusted his feet and unloaded but was thwarted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Manchester City pushed hard for an equaliser but were repelled by Brighton’s defence. Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty Images

There was a loud City cry for a penalty when Luka Vuskovic handballed but no infringement was the ruling; the same as when Ndiaye’s cross seemed to be parried by Dunk’s arm.

Maresca kept his word about City (currently) being “Gio plus 10” as Donnarumma started, though there were two changes from the loss at Aston Villa as Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki were dropped, Matheus Nunes and Bouaddi selected.

For the second half the Italian could retain his XI as City promised they might score soon. This was if the ascendancy of the opening period continued. But Brighton dominated for a passage, as they did during the initial exchanges.

De Cuyper blasted over a fine chance before Ndiaye’s radar was better, another blazing run along the right this time ending with a blistering shot that Verbrugged tipped on to the bar.

This was end-to-end fare that, now, had Pascal Gross tipping the ball in and De Cuyper heading, Donnarumma diving right to fend away from goal.

On 55 minutes Maresca brought on Cherki for Bouaddi and the Frenchman’s contribution was to thread Nunes in – the right-back’s fierce effort was saved.

City kept pressing but were repelled by Brighton so Hürzeler’s side move to 19 points, two behind Maresca’s team: expect both to remain high up throughout.

Sports.title: Evanilson profits from costly Trafford blunder as Bournemouth punish Leeds
Sports.content:
Accidents will happen. They also have consequences. Leeds were playing well, certainly better than Bournemouth for the first 30 minutes until James Trafford committed his grievous error. The goalkeeper made a horrible mess of a pass to an unwitting Ao Tanaka. In stole Justin Kluivert to set up Evanilson for a fifth goal in six matches. Where Leeds’s confidence sagged, Evanilson continued to find the best form of his time on the south coast.

“I just met him and told him you are a real No 9,” Marco Rose said of the Brazilian who was full of intelligent movement. “He has to reward himself with goals and that is what he is doing.”

Thursday’s Prague assignment in the Europa League was kept in mind as Evanilson departed after 75 minutes. The continued rise of Bournemouth, celebrating a sixth successive win, is testament to changing times, thoroughly modern football scoring 16 unanswered goals in those victories. They are now matching the standards of Andoni Iraola’s regime.

Trafford fell victim to a determination to chase everything down as Leeds followed three former European champions in Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa in submission to the swarm. Eli Junior Kroupi supplying Amine Adli for the stoppage-time goal that confirmed victory was the latest example of a club finding players others cannot reach.

View image in fullscreen Amine Adli wheels away having secured the points for Bournemouth in stoppage time. Photograph: Maja Smiejkowska/Reuters

For Leeds, there is no need to press any panic buttons. “I can really speak too negatively,” said Daniel Farke. “I am not concerned about the performance or the commitment.” Trafford has otherwise looked an astute summer signing. “I am pretty sure he will save us more points than he lost us today,” said Farke.

Talking of panic, recent transfer speculation has linked Dominic Calvert-Lewin with Manchester United. The striker’s career revived in West Yorkshire, he is surely too sensible to join Eric Cantona, Rio Ferdinand, Gordon McQueen and Joe Jordan in crossing the Pennines to join English football’s elephants’ graveyard. Leeds remain a different model to the analytics-led disruptors, but with serviceable, solid recruitment. At Bournemouth, promising beginnings, solid foundations were not built upon.

Tyler Adams, booed by away fans for the manner of his departure from Leeds, was a reminder of the 2022-23 relegation season. Within that promising early spell, Leeds’s defence broke up Bournemouth’s three-match sequence of scoring in the first eight minutes at home. “They matched our intensity,” said Rose.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That laid a platform for Calvert-Lewin to get the ball in the net, converting a cross from James Justin. Celebrations were soon curtailed. An inadvertent rebound off the striker’s biceps as he bundled home called the video assistant referee into play. A goal was denied. “Lucky us,” said Rose while Farke lamented the scratching of “one of the best team goals of the season”.

Evanilson and Marcus Tavernier have been Bournemouth’s most consistent players this season. For that first half-hour, they were muted. Then came Trafford’s rush of blood, bearing close resemblance to an error committed in Manchester City colours against Tottenham at the start of last season. “My recommendation is that he shouldn’t watch the game back,” said Farke of an incident he compared to an own goal. “James is a terrific young goalkeeper … it happens.”

Bournemouth thereafter locating their rhythm deepened Leeds’s plight. Trafford was not alone among his team in losing his previous confidence. Tanaka punting wildly out of play as half-time beckoned embodied their collective sag.

Trafford’s foibles continued beyond the break, home fans jeering another misplaced clearance. Such mistakes resulted from Bournemouth zipping with an energy that belies a small squad playing through a packed schedule. Calvert-Lewin, starved of service, was forced to drop deep in search of any involvement.

Quick Guide Bournemouth 1-0 Leeds key facts Show • Evanilson is the first Brazilian to score a Premier League goal on Halloween since Raphinha did so for Leeds against Norwich in 2021; the only other Brazilians to do so are Ramires and Philippe Coutinho, both in 2015. • Bournemouth have won three consecutive Premier League games without conceding for the first time. • After winning one of their first 13 league matches against Leeds, Bournemouth are now unbeaten in their past four (W2 D2), with this the first clean sheet they have registered against them since September 1988 (0-0). Opta Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

A decent save from a skidding Tavernier free kick brought partial redemption for Trafford. The arrival of Kroupi, edging his way back to fitness, added a firepower and creativity unavailable to Leeds. Having scored three of Leeds’s nine goals in nine games, the burden on Calvert-Lewin is heavy, particularly when service to him is light.

“Football is very often just about one goal,” said Farke, but Bournemouth’s second, from Adli, confirmed the match had escaped.

Sports.title: Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red card
Sports.content:
Get ready for another week of agonising over the sorry state of Manchester United. The legends of old will rage on podcasts, clips of a fuming Gary Neville will fly around social media and by the time United play again there is every chance a new manager will be in the dugout.

There were echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge as the walls closed in on Michael Carrick here on Saturday. United missed chances at 0-0, just as they did when Ten Hag lost to West Ham a day before his sacking two years ago, and Chelsea exacted punishment after initially delivering a performance so bad it had you worrying for the nascent Xabi Alonso project.

Chelsea were appalling during the first half, so it was just as well their opponents were in a giving mood. United had opportunities to make their decision to give Carrick a stay of execution look like a wise move rather than the consequence of executive-level confusion, but the finishing was awful and the defending was worse. Morgan Rogers cantered past five players to make it 1-0 and a seventh defeat in 13 games was confirmed when Lisandro Martínez’s faux hard man act led to him being sent off after conceding the penalty that allowed Cole Palmer to seal Chelsea’s rise into fourth place.

Here was a moment to symbolise United’s decline under the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Martínez has had a lot to say about those above him recently, but this is a player who should have been sold along. United have too many in that category and it is hard to see a change of manager alone fixing the problem.

View image in fullscreen Omar Berrada, Manchester United’s CEO, and Jason Wilcox, their director of football, in the stands at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Carrick could limp on until the international break. He is symptom rather than cause, although perhaps a different voice is required. United host Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, but they will be playing in the Championship if this persists.

They are winless in nine games, their worst run since 1988, and are drifting into a relegation battle. The ending was similar to last week’s defeat to Bournemouth, the away end serenading Carrick before booing United’s players, and there was plenty of hate to go around. Chants criticising Jason Wilcox’s work as director of football and urging the Glazers to sell up captured the sense of mutiny.

The first half had been encouraging from United, but with Benjamin Sesko absent until the new year the lack of a finisher proved costly. Bruno Fernandes, restored after clear the air talks with Carrick, fired an early chance over, Amad Diallo and Bryan Mbeumo produced glaring misses and the returning Matheus Cunha had a goal ruled out for offside at 0-0.

The spotlight was also on Alonso, defeats to Tottenham in the league and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup sparking criticism over team selections, and he lifted Chelsea by handing Estêvão Willian his first start in the league this season.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes, the Manchester United captain, cuts a dejected figure at the final whistle. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Estêvão was dangerous on the right flank as Alonso adjusted without João Pedro up front. Pedro Neto rather than Danny Welbeck led the line in a 4-2-3-1 system, but it was United who threatened first. Diogo Dalot combined with Cunha before Andrey Santos, who left Chelsea for United in the summer, swept a shot just wide.

Both sides were vulnerable. Chelsea had a long list of absentees – illness ruled Jordan Henderson out in midfield – and their defence wobbled without Maxence Lacroix. United, though not exactly secure whenever Chelsea punched through on the counterattack, felt optimistic at first.

The visitors had an escape when Senne Lammens spilled a Neto shot and an offside Estêvão tapped home. Diallo ran at Marco Palestra and Fernandes shimmered in a floating role from the left.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United key facts Show • Chelsea won a Premier League home game without conceding for the first time in 13 matches, since a 2-0 victory against Brentford in January. • Manchester United are winless in their past nine games in all competitions (D3 L6). They last had a longer run in April to September 1984 (10 games). • Cole Palmer (pictured) scored his 50th Premier League goal for Chelsea, in his 105th appearance; he is the third-fastest to reach the milestone for the club after Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84) and Diego Costa (85). • At an average of 23 years and 89 days, Chelsea named their joint-second youngest starting XI in a Premier League match (also 23y 89d against Newcastle in October 2024). Only against Crystal Palace in December 2023 have they had younger (23y 21d). Opta Photograph: David Klein/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Chelsea, enjoying neither possession nor control against Santos and Carlos Baleba, were forced back. Levi Colwill intervened when Cunha broke through and Wesley Fofana, a £75m accident waiting to happen, took flak from the home fans after a couple of trademark brain fades.

United could not take advantage. There were a couple of flashes from Chelsea as half-time approached; Moisés Caicedo diverted a Fofana header against the woodwork and Neto shot wide after a stumble from Harry Maguire.

Chelsea were more assertive at the start of the second half and it was easy to predict United’s unravelling. They were punished when Mbeumo turned into trouble. Caicedo blocked his path, Roméo Lavia nicked the ball past Baleba and Rogers sauntering through the middle placed United’s failure to strengthen in defence into sharp focus.

It was brilliant from Rogers, but a bit like a goal you see at the end of a five-a-side between a group of dads playing for the first time since 2019. Maguire barely lifted a leg, Martínez gawped and Rogers dinked over Lammens for 1-0.

United had to dig in. Good luck with that. Lavia was running the midfield for Chelsea. United’s response to falling behind was to crumble. Martínez was on a booking when he elbowed Fofana at a corner. Peter Bankes reviewed the incident and showed the centre-back a second yellow before Palmer made it 2-0 from the spot.

Chelsea relaxed. Estêvão had a scorching strike ruled out. Baleba, still unable to complete 90 minutes, made way for Kobbie Mainoo and the home fans jeered when Mason Mount came on. Mount has toiled since leaving Chelsea for United in 2023. Old Trafford is the place where talent goes to die. Carrick will merely be the latest victim.

Sports.title: ‘I’m not here to be liked’: Glasner defiant as Brentford capitalise on Forest woes
Sports.content:
For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest, the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”.

“For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation than the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.”

Forest, once again, didn’t play too badly. No side has underperformed their xG as significantly as Forest, who went into the weekend third in Opta’s expected table but third-bottom in real life. Here, they had two-and-a-half times as many chances as Brentford. They could claim a degree of misfortune in that both goals went in off the luckless Nikola Milenkovic, the first an own goal after Murillo had misjudged a long clearance to Dango Ouattara, the second credited to Igor Thiago as he latched on to Jaydon Anthony’s clever low cross. But Glasner was accepting no excuses. “It’s not anger,” he said. “It’s necessary.”

The result, Glasner said, was “disappointing and frustrating. And we have to accept it’s not good enough. If you lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why it’s for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.”

One player, he revealed, had asked to travel home alone. “I said no, we can go back with the coach. For example, I have no understanding if somebody wants to go home on his own today from London to Nottingham. No, go with the bus like everybody else. No extras, no extras.”

What the change looks like remains to be seen. Glasner was keen to stress that he takes full responsibility and, at times, seemed to have sympathy. “They tried,” he said. “You can’t say they’ve had a lack of effort. But again, you feel you’re controlling the game. You create a few good situations, and all of a sudden you’re 1-0 down. It was the fourth goal we conceded from a long ball from a goalkeeper. So it’s lack of awareness, losing then the duel, and we’re 1-0 down.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap endured another difficult game in front of goal for Nottingham Forest. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

“It’s not a lack of effort, but there are a few things that are very obvious. We’re talking about the realities. We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it. And if you can’t change it, we need different personnel. And if the club doesn’t want to change it, they need a different manager. I’m desperate to change it. Desperate.

“I think we see the football is OK. We don’t give them many chances. So we kept them to seven [Opta stats said six] shots here at Brentford. So we are creating enough situations. We have the personnel. But we need to get more out of the players. And this is where I see my responsibility. I felt it was more hugging than now. But if hugging doesn’t work, there’s also an opposite way. And again, I don’t need to be liked. I’m not here to be liked. I’m here to bring success to this club. And that’s what I think. Not what I think. That’s what I will change.”

Quick Guide Brentford 2-0 Nottingham Forest key facts Show • Brentford have scored the opening goal in eight of their last nine Premier League games, and only Manchester City (37) and Arsenal (32) have done so more often in the competition since the start of last season than the Bees (27). • Nottingham Forest have failed to score in five of their nine Premier League games this season, no side has done so more; that’s despite having more xG than their opponents in seven of those nine matches. • Since the start of last season, only Erling Haaland (33), João Pedro (20) and Antoine Semenyo (18) have scored more non-penalty goals in the Premier League than the 16 of Igor Thiago (pictured). Opta Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

For his part, Keith Andrews described the win, bafflingly Brentford’s first since they beat Chelsea before the last international break, as their best of the season. “We had to show different traits to some of the other games,” he said. “There was a lot of smart play and leadership from our players.”

Unless morale disintegrates completely, Forest, surely, will be fine. The ball will start running for them. But for now the fates remain against them. And it is that, more than anything, that Glasner needs to change.

Sports.title: Manchester United miss chance to close on WSL top three in drab draw at Everton
Sports.content:
A group of well-choreographed, fancy-dress-wearing school-age dancers fully embraced the Halloween spirit on Saturday as they boogied to one of Michael Jackson’s greatest hits at half-time here. Alas, the match itself was no thriller.

For Manchester United, the only scary thing about this game was how little they tested Courtney Brosnan in Everton’s goal in the first 75 minutes as they demonstrated their lack of creativity.

Brosnan did well to save from Elisabeth Terland’s strike, as United grew into the game late on and began to apply some pressure, but this was a fixture worthy of finishing goalless or – as Sky Sports put it – ghoul-less.

Terland has scored five Women’s Super League goals against Everton, but Brosnan was equal to her close-range shot after Jess Park’s through ball.

“It was not a good performance, but we aren’t always going to perform amazing or good,” said the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid. “But it’s [about] always finding a way to win and today we didn’t.

“We need to be better. Out of possession, we were late, jumping late, to the individual duels, and in-possession we missed that creativity or connections we were having in the last matches.”

Everton, who are winless in all 15 WSL meetings with United, will bee the happier with the point, and their encouraging performance, but they missed the opportunity to climb above their opponents into fourth and might wish they could have converted some of their good midfield play.

Their former Manchester United full-back Hannah Blundell hooked a dangerous effort, left-footed, towards the top corner in the first half, but her shot was saved by Phallon Tullis-Joyce, who also held on to shots – directed straight at her – from Ornella Vignola either side of the break.

Rosa van Gool and Yuka Momiki were combining well for Everton in midfield to frustrate United. United had won away at Everton in the past four seasons, but they were second best in the first half and unable to break the deadlock in the closing stages, despite making improvements after Simi Awujo came on.

United have been on a positive run, winning three and drawing one of their previous four WSL matches, the derby against Manchester City through a morale-boosting late equaliser, as well as enjoying a 100% record in the Players Cup, but they were stifled by an Everton side whose midfield kept the ball well.

Olid, who took over from Marc Skinner in August, said: “After such a positive performance on Sunday [against City] there is always that question – [are we] going to keep that standard or are we going to go a little down, like a hangover after that good match? I expected we would be better than we were. If this has to happen for us to learn and improve, we are going to do that.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A Park effort sailed high over the bar, after an Andrea Medina shot was blocked inside the Everton area, but otherwise there was relatively little to note of United’s first hour, from an attacking perspective.

This was Everton’s first draw of the league campaign, after three wins and four defeats, and they climbed above Arsenal – who play on Sunday – into sixth. They remain two points behind United, as Scott Phelan continues to oversee a steady – if unspectacular – spell in charge.

The Everton head coach said: “In the first half, I thought we were competitive, we showed some good bits with the ball. We just probably lacked a little bit of end product and belief in our game to finish the good passages of play we had. Second half, not so much, but it did highlight the togetherness of the team and the defensive organisation.”

His team certainly did look defensively well-organised. All they were really lacking was a top-quality focal point in attack, in a wretched game that did little to generate suspense.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Pressure grows on Nuno as West Ham beaten at home
Sports.content:
Nuno Espirito Santo is facing mounting pressure after West Brom’s stylish 3-1 win at the London Stadium left West Ham, the Championship promotion favourites, six points off the pace in eighth place.

A second consecutive home defeat contained few saving graces for Nuno, who faced the wrath of fans on the final whistle. Albion, slick and measured, moved into the top four with their 3,000 travelling fans revelling in the discomfort of Nuno, once manager of arch-rivals Wolves.

After falling behind in nine of their previous 15 games, the Hammers’ conceded first again on 20 minutes, with the unmarked Norwegian midfielder Felix Horn Myhre firing home from point-blank range. West Ham leveled when a Jarrod Bowen shot deflected in off Callum Styles, but within three minutes of the restart Albion were back in front. Jimmy-Jay Morgan struck his fourth goal of the season from the corner of the six-yard box. Then, within two minutes of Walker-Peters limping off with a thigh injury, and with Nuno using up all his five substitutes, Price’s corner was only half-cleared to Styles and his fierce, deflected shot made it three.

View image in fullscreen West Ham fans leave early during their defeat to West Brom. Photograph: Martin Dalton/Shutterstock

Asked about visiting fans’ taunts that he would be “sacked in the morning”, Nuno responded: “This is the reality: we can only change this if we win games. There is pressure every day. We have conceded six goals at home in two games and we have to fix it. That cannot happen. The idea and the approach is to try and score first. That is the objective of any team and it’s our responsibility to change it.”

Quick Guide League One roundup: Huddersfield thump Bradford Show An overhead kick from Joe Low opened the scoring as League One leaders Huddersfield swept aside 10-man Bradford 3-0 in the West Yorkshire derby. Huddersfield went in front after four minutes and two goals in six minutes at the start of the second half from Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor killed off the contest at Valley Parade. The Bradford captain, Antoni Sarcevic, was sent off with a second yellow card in the 70th minute. Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis ensured second-placed Stockport kept pace in a 2-1 comeback over AFC Wimbledon at Edgeley Park after Jayden Stockley broke the deadlock for the visitors in the 47th minute. Third-placed Oxford and Barnsley finished with 10 men in their 1-1 draw. Hosts Barnsley were left short-handed for the majority of the contest after Jack Shepherd was sent off in the ninth minute. Vimal Yoganathan’s 32nd-minute opener for Barnsley was cancelled out by Mark Harris on the hour, and the Us went down to 10 men after their goalkeeper, Jamie Cumming, was sent off with two minutes remaining in normal time. Luton beat Peterborough 2-0, Plymouth played out a goalless draw with Reading, Leicester split the points in a 2-2 draw with Stevenage and Leyton Orient beat Cambridge 3-0. Notts County were 2-0 victors at Mansfield, MK Dons drubbed Doncaster 6-1, Wycombe won 2-0 against Burton and Wigan beat Bromley 3-2. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The in-form Will Lankshear hit a double as Middlesbrough maintained their position at the top with a comprehensive 3-0 victory over Charlton at the Riverside. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Lankshear netted twice to take his tally to 15 in all competitions.

Swansea provided the perfect response to last weekend’s hammering at QPR by beating Blackburn 4-0. The hosts were three goals to the good by half-time thanks to Stephen Eustáquio, Joseph Opoki and Filip Lissah, with the Scotland international striker Ross Stewart scoring his first goal for the Swans on the hour mark to complete the rout. Tony Mowbray’s Rovers side had arrived in Wales having won four of their previous six games, including last weekend’s 2-0 home victory over Wrexham, but were simply blown away in the first half as Vitor Matos’ men went on the rampage.

View image in fullscreen Ross Stewart celebrates scoring Swansea’s fourth against Blackburn. Photograph: Gareth Everett/Huw Evans/Shutterstock

Headed goals from Fer Lopez, Adam Armstrong and Ladislav Krejci helped Wolves beat Cardiff 3-0 at Molineux. Cesar Peixoto’s side gave themselves the platform for victory by scoring twice in the first 15 minutes, and Wolves made it four games unbeaten and back-to-back wins without conceding, ending Cardiff’s three-match unbeaten run.

Cameron Bragg scored the first Championship goal of his career as Southampton made it 17 home league matches in a row without losing with a 4-1 victory over QPR. Kuryu Matsuki, Keven Schlotterbeck and Welington also got on the scoresheet as Saints stayed fifth, but kept pace with the rest of the leaders.

Two-goal August Priske was praised by his manager, Chris Davies, after the recalled Danish striker helped Birmingham beat Lincoln 3-1 at the ProAmpac Stadium. He scored either side of the break to take his season tally to seven, with Alex Cochrane securing the win after Imps substitute Tom Bayliss had reduced the deficit.

“He gave us a real focal point, with his size and his strength,” said Davies. “He’s very mature for his age and he has all the tools, the temperament, the technical skills, the physicality and again he just needs to keep hungry, keep pushing.”

Mark Robins saluted his on-song Stoke side but admitted they could have been “more clinical” despite putting bottom side Preston to the sword with a comfortable 2-0 victory. Goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn did the damage as Robins’ team claimed an impressive seventh victory in their last 10 league games.

Quick Guide League Two: Aimson stunner seals it for Salford Show Will Aimson scored a spectacular long-range goal as top-of-the-league Salford battled to a 2-1 win over in-form Exeter. The 32-year-old centre-back opened his Salford account in style two minutes from time after Luke Garbutt had cancelled out Sonny Cox’s first-half opener for the Grecians. Barnet and Crewe drew 1-1, as did Accrington and Northampton, and Tranmere came from behind to secure their first home win since early September with an impressive 3-1 victory over Cheltenham at Prenton Park. A double from Dylan Jones and a stunning strike from Charlie Whitaker before the break overturned Charlie McCann’s early opener to give Rovers all three points. Fleetwood followed their Carabao Cup win over Arsenal with a 3-1 victory over Bristol Rovers at Highbury. Matt Lawlor’s side picked up the three points thanks to goals from Aaron Loupalo-Bi, Rhys Bennett and Josh Roberston. Colchester were dealt a 3-1 defeat by Walsall, Grimsby beat York 5-2, Swindon secured a 2-1 victory over Rotherham, Gillingham won 2-1 at Shrewsbury, Port Vale beat Rochdale 4-2, and Oldham fell 1-0 to Crawley. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Fabio Celestini’s tenure as Burnley head coach began with a disappointing 0-0 draw against Portsmouth at Turf Moor as the Clarets failed to capitalise on their first-half advantage. The Swiss manager, who celebrated his 51st birthday on Saturday, saw his side create a host of chances before the break, but a lack of clinical finishing ultimately cost them.

Kyrell Lisbie scored twice in the early stages as Millwall eased to a 4-1 victory against struggling Derby at The Den. The Lions scored three goals in the first 17 minutes to cruise to just their second win in eight league games. It was another worrying afternoon for the Rams, though, who were never in the contest and remain second from bottom, four points from safety, and without a win in nine games.

Michael Skubala enjoyed the happiest of birthdays as Bristol City came from behind to stun Bolton 3-2 with an added-time Scott Twine winner. The visitors trailed 2-1 with six minutes of normal time remaining but Sam Bell levelled before fellow substitute Twine ensured manager Skubala celebrated his 44th birthday with three points. City’s win was their first in five games while Wanderers have now gone three matches without victory and six weeks since their last success at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Musaba celebrates after equalising against Watford. Photograph: MB Media/Getty Images

Alessio Dionisi hit out at his players after Watford surrendered a two goal half-time lead to lose 3-2 at Norwich, increasing the pressure on his position. Watford looked well placed to take the points after Myron Boadu opened his account for the club with a well-taken double, but Norwich looked a totally different side in the second half, and never looked back after Ben Chrisene had pulled one back in the 54th minute. Anthony Musaba raced through down the right to level the scores after 62 minutes, and nine minutes later it was 3-2 as Paris Maghoma fired home.

“I am furious,” said Dionisi. “It is difficult to explain the difference between the first and second half. Football is crazy, I know that, but to lose a game like that – it’s impossible There were nearly 1,300 Watford fans here today and I would like to be saying ‘thank you’ for their support rather than saying sorry, again.”

On Friday, Ben Brereton Díaz’s first goal of the season sealed a deserved 1-0 win for Sheffield United against Wrexham at Bramall Lane. The Chile forward, in his third spell on loan with the Blades, struck the only goal in the first half.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher apologises to Aston Villa for ‘clumsy and wrong’ comments
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has apologised to Aston Villa for using “clumsy and wrong” language when discussing the club, after club had threatened legal action. “I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong,” Carragher wrote on X on Saturday.

“I can assure Villa fans it was tongue-in-cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV [Up the Villa]!”

On Friday, Villa had announced plans to take legal action against Carragher for his “unacceptable insults”, in a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris. The pundit had said Villa fans should “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”

The former Liverpool defender made his remarks on the Stick to Football podcast while discussing the prospect of Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. Carragher said: “I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans, but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not. So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.

“But there will be teams below Aston Villa and they [Villa] will take their manager or they will take their players, so shut the fuck up, Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United.”

Aston Villa have not responded publicly to Carragher’s apology, at time of writing. They face Fulham at home in the Premier League on Saturday night.

Sports.title: Full throttle Brighton have the depth, quality and guile to hang in there with Arsenal and Man City, writes JACK GAUGHAN, as individual mistakes haunt Enzo Maresca's men in latest defeat
Sports.content:
Full throttle Brighton have the depth, quality and guile to hang in there with Arsenal and Man City, writes JACK GAUGHAN, as individual mistakes haunt Enzo Maresca's men in latest defeat

A game condensed into 15 seconds. Jeremy Doku loses possession on the touchline but won't have that, thundering into a tackle to recollect and then sets off beating two men. He seems in the mood for destruction.

An expectant Etihad is up, the Premier League's trickiest winger cutting loose and Manchester City are in. One calm final ball and an equaliser is on.

Doku tries to find a lurking Erling Haaland, or at least it appears so, because the pass is so bad that Brighton are already storming upfield themselves.

Around 15 minutes after that, Fabian Hurzeler is roaring at his bench. He is chest bumping substitutes and backroom staff with defiant pride, vindication of the words spoken about seeking revenge in the immediately aftermath of losing on penalties here in the cup a matter of days ago.

Brighton stayed in Manchester after Wednesday night and Hurzeler spent that time plotting, organising the battle plan to topple league leaders who have been fallible defensively under Enzo Maresca this season but are producing scintillating attacking moments.

Hurzeler leaves the north west following a little getaway at the Lowry Hotel having drawn and won against City over the course of two 90 minutes. His stock is soaring, his side a fascination and the faint chorus of 'we're gonna win the league' from the away end might just grow a little louder over the coming weeks if they can keep this up.

Manchester City were turned over by Brighton to make it back-to-back league defeats

Yasin Ayari's first half goal was all that was required for Brighton to leave as the victors

Brighton's manager peeled away from the group as they enjoyed being serenaded by the away end, instead sharing a moment with match winner Yasin Ayari, whose third goal of the campaign owed much to the quick thinking of Lewis Dunk to restart play from a dead ball with haste and the individual mistake of Matheus Nunes, failing to clear Diego Gomez's cross. Ayari and Dunk were those to miss from the spot in the Carabao Cup.

'Wednesday was brutal,' Hurzeler said. 'We promised ourselves that we won't have the same feeling.

'We created energy, positivity. How the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.'

Hurzeler discussed the virtue of luck here in midweek and City's was out on the day, now only two points between the teams after consecutive league defeats.

The joyous, and somewhat knowing, celebrations between staff members shone a light on the preparation that went into this result and how it quite clearly serves as a warning shot.

Brighton showed across four days that they have the depth, quality and wherewithal to be at least be considered strong enough to stay close with City and Arsenal. More specifically, they showed on Saturday that they can mix the way in which they play, adept to altering circumstances.

Their full throttle movement in midfield before half time confused their City counterparts, the home midfield discombobulated – arms pointing frantically, basic organisational shouts becoming more hurried – and that filtered through to other areas of the pitch.

Maresca was seem directing Elliot Anderson on who to follow and there were occasionally some befuddled looks.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was full stretch but could do nothing about Ayari's pinpoint strike

Enzo Maresca was in disbelief as his side spurned numerous opportunities to score a goal

Out of possession, home wingers were often full backs and full backs were often stationed as wingers as they followed their men, with Brighton happily piercing through any gaps. For a while, City were taken for a ride on the waltzers.

And then later on, when City pushed and pushed, Brighton went to a back six and contained.

They still gave up a number of very presentable chances, City failing to convert five of those – most notably two for Iliman Ndiaye and Nico O'Reilly's late header – but the rearguard action is proof that they own the minerals to enjoy more days like these before May is done.

'SILLY' CITY

Brighton managed to create four big chances from just nine touches inside the City box, indicating that once Maresca's midfield is breached then they are too easy to play through.

The Italian – who dropped Marc Guehi - is concerned by the volume of individual mistakes at both ends of the pitch after the Nunes error.

'We're probably conceding [too many] silly goals,' Maresca said, with the defeat at Aston Villa also pockmarked by them.

'We created enough but unfortunately didn't score. For sure we are not happy. Nobody is happy when we lose. But we were aware that we weren't going to win all the games.'

Maresca said he had not reviewed two penalty appeals for handball and the decision to award a free kick in the build up to Brighton's 11th-minute goal.

Brighton showed enough quality this week to suggest they can hang with Arsenal and Man City

MATCH FACTS Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Gvardiol 5 (Foden 79); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 6 (Cherki 55, 7); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 79), Fernandez 5 (O’Reilly 65), Doku 5; Haaland 5. Manager: Enzo Maresca 6. Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 7; Costinha 7, Vuskovic 7, Dunk 8, Boscagli 6 (Hadjam 64, 6); Gross 6, Chema 6 (Wieffer 64, 6); Gomez 7 (Rutter 84), Ayari 7, De Cuyper 7 (Yalcouye 72); Kostoulas 6 (Hinshelwood 72, 6). Scorer: Ayari 11. Booked: De Cuyper, Gross, Chema. Manager: Fabian Hurzeler 8. Referee: Craig Pawson 6.

ANGLES OF ATTACK

Left back Josko Gvardiol was largely tucking in to become a third centre half and Nunes told to occupy the sort of attacking positions that the Croatian usually devours.

And interestingly, were City to win their appeal against the guilty verdicts – the sanctions for which would likely spell relegation – then left back is an area they would be expected to look at.

Sources have indicated that Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert is one potential target who was scouted extensively last season before City decided against bolstering their ranks in that area in the summer.

Rayan Ait-Nouri is looking to leave, while any signings in that position would present intrigue as to how Gvardiol and O'Reilly are used in future.

Sports.title: James Trafford's old ghost returns to haunt him as Marco Rose's Bournemouth side claim another heavyweight scalp to make it six wins on the spin
Sports.content:
James Trafford's old ghost returns to haunt him as Marco Rose's Bournemouth side claim another heavyweight scalp to make it six wins on the spin

How fitting it was, amid this season of werewolves and vampires, that it was one of James Trafford’s old ghosts that came back to haunt him.

No witches or zombies will give the Leeds goalkeeper a sleepless night quite like this familiar howler that cost his side the game.

The visitors dominated Bournemouth for most of the first half with confident, flowing football and thought they had a deserved lead when Dominic Calvert-Lewin bundled the ball into the net early on after a stunning passing move only for the goal to be ruled out for a handball.

Leeds were firmly on top…and then they had a goal-kick. Trafford didn’t take it but received it short and tried to pass it out to Ao Tanaka only to play it straight to the lurking Justin Kluivert, who squared it to Evanlison for a tap-in.

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded at the Etihad Stadium against Tottenham at the start of last season, on his second league start for Manchester City, when he - again - received a short goal-kick and tried to pass it to a team-mate who was already surrounded. City signed Gianluigi Donnarumma 10 days later and Trafford’s City career was all-but over.

The England keeper has been able to resurrect it at Leeds, and came into the game with the best save percentage of any stopper in the Premier League, and marshaller of the second-best defence in the division behind only champions Arsenal.

Trafford made a fine save from a Marcus Tavernier free-kick, and another effort late on from Junior Kroupi but the damage had been done. He could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time. The Bournemouth supporters, who jeered him every time he touched the ball, made sure he didn’t forget it.

‘James is a terrific young goalkeeper,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘I’m pretty sure he will save us way more points than he perhaps has cost us today. We win together, we lose together. We’re all happy to have him. He’s still top class and has all my trust and all my love. My recommendation is that he shouldn’t watch the scene back!’

It was almost identical to the goal Trafford conceded against Tottenham at the start of last season when he - again - received a short goal-kick and passed it straight to the opposition

The English goalkeeper could do little about Amine Adli’s finish that doubled Bournemouth’s lead in second-half stoppage time

Cherries slay another giant

Bournemouth have made such a habit of punching above their weight in recent years, that victories over traditional Premier League big boys no longer seem as remarkable as they once did. Running your club brilliantly, signing excellent players and developing them with superb coaches season after season will tend to normalise such success for a club of this size.

The Cherries are no longer content to constrain their heroics to slaying mere domestic giants. For the fourth match in a row, they put a former king of Europe to the sword. In the space of 10 days, they have dispatched AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa - all 3-0 - and now former European Cup winners Leeds.

Yes, they needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip. Brazilian sensation Rayan went close before substitute Adli wrapped it up late on after a stunning through ball from Kroupi.

Bournemouth needed a bit of luck and a glaring mistake to get them ahead but, once they got in front, they rarely looked like letting it slip

MATCH FACTS Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 7; Smith 7 (Diakite 88), Hill 8, Silva 7, Truffert 6; Adams 7, Christie 7 (Cook 6); Rayan 6 (Adli 88), Kluivert 7 (Kroupi 68, 8), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 76). Scorers: Evanilson 31, Adil 90. Booked: Christie, Adams. Manager: Marco Rose 7. Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 5; Justin 6 (Bahoya 84), Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 7; Bogle 6, Ampadu 6, Tanaka 5 (Stach 65, 6); Gudmudsson 6 (Longstaff 65, 5); Wilson 6 (Aaronson 84), James 7 (Nmecha 65, 6); Calvert-Lewin 6. Booked: Elvedi, Ampadu. Manager: Daniel Farke 6. Referee: Michael Salisbury 6. Attendance: 12,041.

Rose finding his feet

What is even more impressive is that Bournemouth are doing it without Andoni Iraola at the helm, and under a manager in Marco Rose who was even feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games.

Now, it’s six wins in a row in all competitions. Sixteen goals scored, none conceded. Even for Bournemouth, who make the remarkable look normal, that’s quite something.

Not only that, they are doing it without influential midfielder Alex Scott, out with a hamstring injury, pulling the strings. When you have Ryan Christie and Tyler Adams keeping things ticking in the middle, with Justin Kluivert and Kroupi ahead of them, you barely even noticed.

Marco Rose was feeling early grumblings of discontent from sections of the fanbase after failing to win any of their first six league games

A real number nine

We’re approaching that time of year, with Halloween already upon us and Christmas coming into view, when the constant churn of January transfer rumours will soon become inescapable.

An early one doing the rounds is how Manchester United are ‘exploring a move’ for Calvert-Lewin.

Don’t fall for it, Dominic. He lost here but how different the afternoon could have gone had the ball not bounced on to his arm before going into the net. Even in defeat, this is still a club under Daniel Farke that’s stable, competent and moving in the right direction.

If United are really in the market for someone who knows where the net is, few are doing it with more ruthless efficiency than Bournemouth striker Evanlison, who made it four goals in as many games for the Cherries.

‘I just saw him said: “You are a real number 9”,’ said Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.

The same warning applies to him too.

Sports.title: Coventry heap more misery on Sunderland: Insipid Black Cats hit new low to leave Regis Le Bris looking haunted by grim prospect of relegation after 3-1 defeat
Sports.content:
it a horror show that left Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris looking increasingly haunted and clinging a little less securely to his job. Brand it the stuff of nightmares for the furious supporters who made the long journey back to the north-east fearing relegation. Roll out the clichés because they all apply after this ghoulish display had Le Bris and his players well and truly spooked. It was x-rated stuff from insipid Sunderland in what had been billed as an early-season relegation shoot-out. They lacked intensity, were a shambles defensively and remain rock-bottom after being well beaten by a Coventry side who deserved everything they got. As the ska classic Ghost Town by legendary Coventry band The Specials boomed out over the public address system, it was Sunderland who were left looking like dead men. Jack Rudoni (right) was the key man again for Coventry as they dismantled Sunderland Regis Le Bris's side remain bottom of the Premier League with their season looking bleak Le Bris said: 'Are we in a relegation scrap? It’s obvious when you look at the table. 'Are we worried? Always. It’s football and you can’t relax. 'We won’t give up just because it’s a bit tough. I feel the unity of the club and the players.' SKY BLUES FLYING Coventry’s acclimatisation to the Premier League after 25 years away has not been plain sailing. Frank Lampard’s men are clearly a united force, however, and that togetherness harvested back-to-back victories at Nottingham Forest and home to Newcastle a few weeks ago. A reality check came with defeats at Tottenham and a 1-0 reverse to Fulham here last weekend when the Sky Blues were booed off. But they were comfortably the better side against Sunderland as they chiselled out a third win from five Premier League games. They led in the 17th minute when Tatsuhiro Sakamoto produced a stunning left-foot finish which flew into the net after Sunderland failed miserably to clear their lines. The manner in which Taiwo Awoniyi strode through the Sunderland rearguard to fire home and double Coventry’s lead 20 minutes later was far more shocking. Sunderland fans booed their team off at the break but things got worse in the 52nd minute when Jack Rudoni’s deflected left-foot strike beat Robin Roefs. Frank Lampard's side now have three wins this season after 25 years away from the league Could Coventry beat the drop? You would have your doubts. But only a fool would turn his back on the Sky Blues now. There is too much energy, and too much drive, coursing through the veins of a football club with momentum behind it. Lampard, whose side climbed out of the drop zone, said: 'I’m very happy with the energy we showed and the quality in the goals we scored. 'The positivity in the performance rubbed off on the stadium. It’s a nice feeling to be out of the bottom three but things can change very quickly and there’s such a long way to go.' BLACK CATS ON THE SLIDE Sunderland, let it be remembered, finished seventh last season and qualified for Europe for the first time in 53 years. But second-season syndrome is threatening to hit the Wearsiders like a tonne of bricks. During the first half, they created precious little as Brian Brobbey scuffed a low shot wide when Coventry led 1-0. That felt like a big moment and they finally got off the mark in the 67th minute through Enzo Le Fee’s penalty after Ethan Pinnock’s handball. But it never looked anything else but consolation for Sunderland, whose supporters made their feelings clear, although many had cleared off long before the end. Le Bris said: 'It’s normal to react like this but I know they believe in the club and we’ll stick together.' It is now one win in nine for the Black Cats, who look a pale shadow of the side who had 17 points at this stage last season. Sunderland look a shadow of the side that finished seventh in their first year back last year RUDONI A CLASS ACT If Coventry are to defy the odds and beat the drop this season, the influence of Rudoni will be crucial. The midfielder's educated left boot again proved an important weapon for his team and he is likely to be attracting admiring glances from some higher-placed clubs. He scored a goal and was in the thick of things when Alderete was sent off in the closing stages. Rudoni's technical qualities are certainly of the Premier League and he should not be short of offers if Lampard's men fail to beat the drop.

Sports.title: Fallon Sherrock celebrates pocketing huge £501k jackpot after beating Luke Littler - and hits back at critics who questioned her place in Netflix challenge
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock has shared a picture of herself, champagne bottle in hand, celebrating her £501,000-winning triumph over Luke Littler.

Sherrock, 32, beat reigning world champion Littler in one leg of darts in the globally broadcast Netflix competition Beat Luke Littler on Friday.

The streaming giant billed it as an event giving 'amateurs a chance at life-changing money'.

Players could not be members of the PDC Tour, meaning Sherrock - who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019 - was allowed to compete.

The announcement that she would be allowed to take part earlier this month drew some criticism, which Sherrock, who has an MBE for services to darts, reflected on after her win.

'I mean, it’s been tough,' she said after her victory in Manchester. 'Obviously I do see the backlash and I do see all the negative comments. But at the end of the day, I fit the criteria for this.

Fallon Sherrock has shared a picture of herself, champagne bottle in hand, celebrating her £501,000-winning triumph over Luke Littler (source: fsherrock/Instagram)

Sherrock also recently shared pictures of her Halloween outfit (source: fsherrock/Instagram)

The 32-year-old has been showing off her spooky costumes ideas ahead of Saturday (source: fsherrock/Instagram)

'I’ve never had a tour card, and I wouldn’t class myself as a pro really, because all I do is just play darts for the enjoyment of it.'

More than 3,000 people auditioned in London and Manchester to take on The Nuke, with hopefuls travelling from far and wide, queuing from the early hours of the morning.

'I don't need the money,' Sherrock told Daily Mail Sport at the London auditions. 'But I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you?

'I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

The PDC president, Barry Hearn, who was involved in the audition process, defended the contest. Asked whether Sherrock’s inclusion was unfair, Hearn said: 'No, not at all. She’s not a PDC tour card holder. She’s entitled to enter. Why should she be denied?'

He added: 'Do you want just a series of 20 matches where someone can't even throw a dart? No, of course we want excellence competing against excellence, and that's what it was all about.'

After Littler had defeated 14 amateurs, some as young as 14, he was always going to have a tough task against Sherrock, who has won 21 times on the PDC Women's Series.

She had been closest to the bull to start first and hit a 180, only the third maximum of the night, before taking out double 20 to clinch the prize.

Luke Littler was defeated on Netflix on Friday night as Fallon Sherrock claimed £501,000

Sherrock needed just 14 darts to beat the two-time world champion and take home the prize

Sherrock, whose son Rory was among the crowd, said: 'It's insane, I can't put into words what it means, especially having Rory here - it's his first time at anything and he has seen me win.

'It's a great moment and I will memorise this forever. Give me an opportunity and I will take it every time. I'm really proud of myself, I rise to the occasion.'

Littler, who is a two-time PDC world champion, was humble in defeat, especially considering Lineker had earlier in the night claimed that he had 'put his reputation on the line'.

The 19-year-old said: 'Brilliant, that's what one person had to do - win the bull and go out in 15 (darts) and that's what she did, world class.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists he will NOT be sacked as Man United manager - despite side slipping closer to relegation zone after Chelsea defeat
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick believes he will cling onto his job as Manchester United head coach despite watching helplessly as his team slid closer towards the relegation zone at Chelsea.

Goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer – who converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds – consigned United to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge as they sank to 17th(check) place in the Premier League.

Earlier this week, Carrick was given more time by Old Trafford bosses to turn the club’s disastrous season around, but he is now without a win in nine games.

Asked if he will be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Roma, he replied: ‘Yes. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for the midweek now.’

The 20-time champions of England are faced with the humiliation of dropping into the bottom three and it was put to Carrick, a player and coach at United stretching back two decades, that seeing the club in such a position must be hurting him.

‘Yeah, pretty much exactly that,’ he said. ‘There is a lot of emotion. We're a great football club and we want to win football matches. Things have gone against us in a big way and unravelled quickly.

Man United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988

‘There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it any different, it's not going to change it.

‘You can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches. So that's the way it's got to be approached, for sure.’

Carrick insisted that he didn’t feel let down by Martinez, but did not even look at the Argentine as he left the pitch.

‘It has a major importance on the game. A huge moment. I think that is pretty obvious really,’ added Carrick. ‘The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure.’

The United fans continued to give Carrick their support while once again turning on the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso admitted Estevao’s positive performance will give him a selection headache after the wonderkid showed Chelsea what they have been missing.

Morgan Rogers' brilliant solo goal set Chelsea on their way to victory

The 19-year-old Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season and scored two disallowed goals for offside as well as creating several other opportunities.

‘He’s given me reasons (to pick him),’ said Alonso. ‘This is football and sometimes you don’t get what you want, but the best way to show it is not by being angry, it’s by being competitive and Este has done it really well.’

Alonso also hailed Romeo Lavia after the 22-year-old Belgian filled in for the unwell Jordan Henderson in midfield on short notice, and was arguably this game’s best performer.

‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance,’ Alonso said. ‘He's done so many things right. He’s been always connecting the defence with the attacker players, he's been able to switch the game, he's taken many right decisions, he's been very dynamic, competitive. I'm very happy for him and he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

Sports.title: Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs denies drugging and sexually assaulting male influencer in new court docs
Sports.content:
Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs denies drugging and sexually assaulting male influencer in new court docs

The man accusing Washington Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs of sexual assault is lying 'because he got caught stealing,' according to the latest filing from the NFL star's attorneys in the ongoing counter lawsuits.

Sports and marketing influencer Christopher Griffith previously accused Diggs of drugging and sexually assaulting him at the NFL star's Rockville, Maryland home in 2023. Griffith claimed Diggs then tried to silence him by ordering his brother, Darez Diggs, and others to attack the influencer, who claimed to have $100,000 in property stolen during the encounter.

Although Griffith and Darez Diggs have since settled that lawsuit for an undisclosed amount, the influencer was sued by Stefon Diggs for defamation in 2025 over the original sexual misconduct allegations – claims the NFL star has continued to deny.

Griffith has since filed his own counter lawsuit against Stefon Diggs, insisting the sexual misconduct allegations are true. Furthermore, attorneys working on behalf of Griffith claimed in their countersuit that Diggs defamed their client by suggesting the sexual misconduct allegations against him resulted from a botched robbery attempt.

In his July Instagram post referencing Griffith, Diggs wrote that someone was 'lying on my name because he got caught stealing.'

Now, in their latest filing obtained by The Daily Mail, Diggs' attorneys denied any wrongdoing on their client's behalf and insisted his post was protected speech because it was true. One of Diggs' attorneys, Mitch Schuster, also commended the court's decision to deny Griffith's motion requesting a change of venue.

Stefon Diggs of the Washington Commanders warms up before kickoff against the 49ers

Diggs was accused by sports and marketing influencer Christopher Griffith (pictured) of drugging and sexually assaulting him at the NFL star's Rockville, Maryland home in 2023

'The latest filing is a routine answer to Mr. Griffith's allegations, and operates to deny any and all liability, as Mr. Diggs has done throughout the entirety of this case,' Schuster told The Daily Mail in an email.

'Additionally, we are pleased with the Court's latest decision denying Mr. Griffith's motion to transfer venue. Mr. Diggs looks forward to presenting his defamation claims to a jury and remains confident that truth and justice will prevail.'

Griffith's legal team previously handed over more than 100 pages of messages to the court, which they claim support evidence of sexual assault. The content of the messages has not been revealed, but Diggs downplayed the court submission in his aforementioned social media post.

'100 pages?' Diggs asked. 'Okay post them then.'

Griffith's attorney did not immediately respond to The Daily Mail's request for comment.

Separately, Diggs is being sued in a second case by a former college teammate and personal assistant over defamation and conspiracy claims.

The 32-year-old receiver was initially sued in Miami-Dade County back in February by Nigel King (pictured), who played alongside Diggs at Maryland and later worked for the NFL star

Stefon Diggs is not personally accused of attacking King but his brothers, Seahawks star Trevon (pictured) and Darez, were. The complaint against Trevon has been dropped

The 32-year-old receiver was initially sued in Miami-Dade County back in February by Nigel King, who played alongside Diggs at Maryland and later worked for the NFL star.

As seen in the complaint obtained by The Daily Mail, King claims Diggs falsely blamed him for the 2024 theft of the NFL star's Ferrari, which allegedly led Diggs' associates to attack King at a Miami strip club in December.

Stefon Diggs is not personally accused of attacking King, but his brothers, Seattle Seahawks cornerback Trevon and the aforementioned Darez, were listed as defendants in the original complaint. King's attorneys have since dropped allegations against Trevon Diggs.

The Daily Mail has been unable to reach Darez Diggs for comment about the complaint.

Stefon Diggs has denied orchestrating the attack in a motion to dismiss filed on his behalf and obtained by The Daily Mail.

In May, he was also found not guilty of felony strangulation as well as assault and battery charges against his former personal chef Jamila Adams.

The Commanders, it seems, were not fazed by the off-field issues and signed Diggs to a one-year deal with more than $10 million. Diggs has been slowed by hamstring and hand injuries this year, but was recently cleared off the team's Week 8 injury report.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez's self-destruction sums up a broken Man United as Michael Carrick's future hangs by a thread - and there are still questions to ask of Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez's self-destruction sums up a broken Man United as Michael Carrick's future hangs by a thread - and there are still questions to ask of Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, writes IAN HERBERT

The sun was high and fierce and Michael Carrick shielded his eyes from it on the few occasions he got to his feet and tried to direct the Manchester United players, who did not seem to hear him. The United contingent hurled personal abuse at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. The scrutiny was remorseless and unyielding.

For a time, there seemed to be hope - and no one can say that this latest hammer blow for Carrick removes the doubts about Xabi Alonso’s methods – but it was crushed by the same fecklessness and mindlessness that is burying United alive.

Carrick did not cast so much as a glance at Lisandro Martinez - who had just finished off the team’s hopes by leaping with Wesley Fofana and extending an elbow into his face to concede a penalty - when he walked past on the way to the tunnel.

Bruno Fernandes and some others made a half-hearted protest about the dismissal but Carrick didn’t. He knew. This looked for all the world like a footballer looking to leave the field early – making no attempt to play the ball as he was up with Fofana, having been booked for a reckless challenge on Morgan Rogers, just three minutes earlier.

The Argentinian, whose words publicly challenging the club a few weeks back will always belong to the story of these Carrick-era death throes, will perhaps want to trash talk the club again when he has been shown the door. But it was also his own gross inadequacy which had allowed Morgan Rogers to dance through the defence to put Chelsea ahead. Martinez should never darken the door of a United squad again.

Michael Carrick’s future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

Lisandro Martinez, publicly outspoken earlier this month, was booked twice inside two minutes

Bruno offers hope

There are few grounds for optimism from here but Fernandes is one. When he forfeited the chance to write a new script for himself – blasting into the stand after Bryan Mbeumo’s cross had gifted him a golden opportunity – the prospect of him righting the wrongs of the past week seemed forlorn.

By then, he had already been dumped on his backside by Romeo Lavia and Moises Caicedo and ceded possession. But he brushed off the mockery of the Chelsea faithful to put in a performance which demonstrated that he has a part to play at United.

In front of the small United away section before the game, he went through a free-kick taking routine, arcing one into the top-left corner and striking another against the bar.

He was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in. When United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick. He lingered before United’s fans at the end and they accepted him. The turmoil remains but he will be needed.

Fernandes was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in and United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick

Chelsea unconvincing

There can be no overstating the gravity of the week just passed for Xabi Alonso: a lamentable performance in defeat to Tottenham, the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and the Spaniard’s suggestion that trophy didn’t matter, which has gone down badly with the fans.

His brief programme notes made it clear how much he wanted something better here but the yawning gaps between Chelsea’s midfield and defensive lines and the ease with which United exploited them in the first half were disturbing. Wesley Fofana was lamentable.

United’s Amad could have plundered them twice – first burgling Fofana on the half-way line but lacking the pace to accelerate on and score, then easing into space and failing to despatch when one-on-one with Mike Penders. Cole Palmer’s error allowed Matheus Cunha to send Fernandes off but Mbeumo couldn’t connect with his cross. United’s failure to capitalise was fateful.

Wesley Fofana was lamentable and United’s Amad Diallo could have plundered them twice

Sublime Rogers

As both sides squandered chances and laboured under basic defensive challenges, it was hard to countenance the notion that two gladiators of European football used to compete in this fixture and actually contested a Champions League final.

The occasion cried out for a moment of class and it was Morgan Rogers who provided it, taking a ball Romeo Lavia had won, dancing his way through half of the Manchester United team and slipping the ball home.

The defending shamed the traditions of the visiting team. Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Martinez and Harry Maguire just watched Morgan go. But it was Rogers, taking his Chelsea tally to six goals and four assists in all competitions, who turned the game around.

Morgan Rogers had scored a brilliant solo goal for Chelsea's second-half opener to show up United’s awful finishing

Brittle, brittle United

It was always clear that the test of United’s mettle would come if they fell behind. The general view of the fans marching through Euston Station at 11am was that if United scored first they would come away with the points. If they conceded, their heads would drop and the psychological failure at the heart of this team would come to the fore. And so it came to pass.

In a straw poll of 15 or so at Euston, only two thought Carrick was the man to restore ‘Standards’, to quote the mantra captured on an Old Trafford banner last week. The way Chelsea turned the screw just bore that pessimism. Cole Palmer converted the penalty Martinez had conceded to finish things off.

Estevao the jewel

It was to the jubilant cheers of the Chelsea faithful that Estevao left the field towards the end and this was an afternoon which will live long in the memory for him. Twice he had the ball in United’s net – pouncing on Senne Lammens' failure to hold a cross in the first half and taking Palmer’s pass to crash home in the second – but twice he was denied by VAR.

By the end, he had the control of Chelsea’s right as he interlinked with Palmer and came close a third time. Some will say this calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show.

Some will say Estevao's display calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show

What next for Carrick?

As the minutes ticked down on another desperate result for United, the away section sang Carrick’s name once more and, significantly, he walked over towards them alone once more, just as he had after the defeat at home to Bournemouth. But it was a less emphatic assertion of empathy and support for him this time, and he did not linger so long.

The talk of Eddie Howe’s availability grows. It emerged on Saturday that under the terms of his departure agreement with Newcastle United that he will cost United only £3million. The United fans are really not convinced by him and it looks like the club will work through many more managers before a corner is turned. The constant will be that support base, who began and ended the match singing Sir Matt Busby’s name. They will always have their history.

Sports.title: New footage shows Bruno Fernandes' honest reaction to Man Utd losing at Chelsea
Sports.content:
New footage shows Bruno Fernandes' honest reaction to Man Utd losing at Chelsea

Manchester United were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, plunging them further into disaster, and Bruno Fernandes' reaction told a story

View Image Bruno Fernandes was visibly emotional after the full-time whistle (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes appeared to be wiping away tears after Manchester United suffered another damaging defeat at Stamford Bridge.

‌



United were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea on Saturday afternoon as their winless run reached nine matches. Second-half goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer settled it for the home side, who also benefited from a red card for Lisandro Martinez.

Michael Carrick's position as manager is now under new more scrutiny, with United sitting in 17th place, just above the relegation zone in the Premier League. They have taken just seven points from their nine matches - the club's worst start to a campaign since 1988.

Having been dropped for the 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth last weekend, Fernandes was back in the starting line-up as captain against Chelsea. The playmaker held clear-the-air talks with Carrick in mid-week after his provocative comments in Como made headlines.

But Fernandes was powerless to stop another defeat as United spurned numerous chances to take the lead before collapsing after the break. His emotions were there for all to see after the final whistle.

United's players went over the away end at Stamford Bridge to applaud the travelling supporters, who stayed until the end. Fernandes was caught by the TV cameras staring blankly ahead and as he walked off he seemed to be wiping tears away.

Before the game, Carrick insisted that he didn't have a problem with his captain and he praised his performance in defeat in west London. "I was happy with the team first half, especially individually in it," he told TNT Sports. "The discipline, the role, the quality of the football were all there."

Carrick's job has been under threat for the past few weeks, with the United hierarchy considering replacements, including Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte. But the supporters have stuck by their former midfielder, chanting his name while attributing the blame to the club's owners.

Asked about the fans, Carrick said: "There is a lot of emotion, we're a great football club, and we want to win football matches. The supporters come, make a lot of effort, pay a lot of money to watch us play. You can see from today the boys had the game in the right place and things have gone against us.

"Things have gone against us, and gone against us in a big way. Unravelled quickly. A lot of emotion right now.

"We have got to move forward and take the things that worked for us today. A lot of the good things, especially in the first half and use that moving forward."

Despite winning just two of his 13 games this season, Carrick is expecting to remain in charge for Tuesday's Champions League game against Roma.
