In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out
Sports.content:
Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, 19, has been identified as the innocent bystander fighting for life after being shot in the head and neck outside a Queensland pub.

She remained in a critical and unstable condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital on Monday afternoon. Metro South Health confirmed the teenager is still fighting for life in the intensive care unit.

The teenager was active on social media just hours before the shooting. She and her partner were seen lip syncing to Justin Bieber's Daises in a video posted on Saturday afternoon.

Four people were wounded outside Fitzy's Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on Saturday night, while more than 100 spectators, including families with young children, attended the Logan City Titles boxing event.

Phil Austin, from the Australian National Boxing Federation Queensland, categorically rejected suggestions it was a bikie or organised crime attack targeting the boxing.

Austin was in the venue's foyer when the shots erupted.

'The wider community is questioning how can this happen in Logan?' Queensland Police Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said on Monday.

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau remains critically injured after suffering gunshot wounds to her head and neck

Vision of bullet marks on a mirror after four people were shot outside Fitzy's Loganholme during a boxing event on Saturday night

Boxing official Phil Austin was in the foyer when shots erupted, with flying glass striking his arm

'That's a popular local pub, a well-respected institution. That location had children, teenagers, mums and dads at that sporting event.'

Taskforce Maxima is a specialist Queensland Police squad that investigates outlaw motorcycle gangs and serious organised crime.

It is assisting Logan CIB and State Crime Command, which are jointly leading the investigation into the Fitzy's Loganholme shooting.

But Austin told Daily Mail that speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime was 'people putting two and two together and getting five'.

'I haven't seen any reputed organised crime figures at a fight show in this country in years,' he said.

'Bikies used to go to events, but since the government changed their laws, you just don't see them.'

Austin said he did not recognise any of the victims and could not say whether they had been attending the boxing.

'I don't even know if they were there to watch the boxing,' he said.

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) remained in the intensive care unit on Monday afternoon

Austin rejected speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime

'There's more than just boxing happening at that pub.'

He said no fighters or trainers appeared to have been involved and challenged assumptions that the boxing event itself had been targeted.

'We just happened to be there,' he said.

'It could have been the flower arranging show. It's just the fact that we were there.

'We have no idea why what happened happened. The only thing that we know for sure is it's a tragedy.'

Austin said he had just finished seeing a fighter and left the room being used as the dressing rooms near the venue's front doors when the shooting began.

'I'm in the foyer. I've got maybe a couple of metres, and then there's just a series of shots very, very quickly,' he said.

'We're talking about five or six shots in that or less seconds.'

Police say shots were fired from a Mitsubishi's front passenger window near the venue's drop-off area

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside the vehicle, according to police

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) had shared a video lip syncing to a Justin Bieber song just hours before the shooting

Flying glass struck the back of his arm.

'I was wearing a long shirt. Nothing hurt, but it just sort of reinforced me like, okay … this is happening,' he said.

'Before I could sort of basically say to myself, 'Oh crap,' it's over.'

Austin saw a car with its lights on but did not see anyone get out.

'It was my impression that they were actually still in the car,' he said.

Police said a Mitsubishi approached the passenger drop-off area during an intermission and shots were fired from its front passenger window.

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside.

Austin went to alert his crew in the boxing hall at the rear of the venue, away from where the shots had been fired.

Three men aged 27, 37 and 38 remain in hospital with serious injuries but are improving, police said

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting

'Then people's reactions start to kick in, and there's a bit of pandemonium, really, a lot of very, very angry people,' he said.

'They used the boxing room, basically, like a safe haven for everybody.'

Patrons began leaving through the back as hotel staff and security marshalled the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said everyone who witnessed the violence would carry some trauma from the night.

'This could have been your family member,' she said.

'This was a random group of people at the front of a popular hotel that became victims.'

The three other victims, men aged 27, 37 and 38, all suffered gunshot wounds to their abdomens. The 38-year-old was also shot in the arm.

All three remained in serious conditions on Monday but were improving, Adams said.

Police have not confirmed whether the men knew one another.

Police believe the attack involved pre-planning but say it remains premature to speculate about gang or organised crime involvement.

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting.

CCTV from nearby homes showed its occupants being collected by another vehicle after the car was torched. Police believe one of those involved may have suffered burns or another injury.

A ute was also found burnt later that night, with investigators still examining whether it was connected.

Adams urged anyone who knew or suspected who was responsible to come forward.

'There will be people out there who know who did this or suspect who did this,' she said.

For Austin, who has a son the same age as the critically injured teenager, the shooting has hit particularly hard.

'I've got a son her age, so it's really, really hit home hard,' he said.

He offered the federation's support to the victims, their families and friends.

'This is an awful, awful time for everyone,' he said.

'Let's just hope this girl recovers. It's just awful.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn was stopped in the second round of his world title challenge against Garcia in Las Vegas, with a brutal right hand sending the Briton crashing to the canvas before the American finished the job.

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old.

But he appears to have an unexpected opponent in mind.

Benn took to social media to share a fight poster featuring himself and McGregor, accompanied by the caption: 'Benn vs McGregor coming soon, 2027'.

He added to the speculation by responding: 'Any day of the week.'

Conor Benn (pictured above) has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia

Benn is understood to be interested in making the fight happen and is expected to explore potential terms with the Irishman.

Benn has previously been tipped to face McGregor in a lucrative crossover bout, with boxing legend Roy Jones Jr suggesting that the fight would make sense.

He said the crossover bout would be one of two major paydays for the Brit before he considers bringing his career to a close.

Jones also suggested such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn.

The prospect would offer Benn the chance to headline another major event without the pressure of a world title being on the line, while a fight against McGregor would attract an audience well beyond traditional boxing fans.

McGregor is one of the biggest names in combat sports, having become a global superstar during his time in the UFC before stepping into the boxing ring to face Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

The Irishman is also coming off a difficult period of his own, having suffered a fresh setback on his return to the Octagon against Max Holloway.

A fight with Benn would undoubtedly attract huge attention, although there is no indication yet that the pair are close to agreeing a deal.

Roy Jones Jr has said such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn

Benn's call-out comes after a brutal night in Las Vegas, where his hopes of becoming a world champion were ended in devastating fashion.

The British fighter had talked up his chances of upsetting Garcia, but the American's speed and power proved too much.

Garcia caught Benn with a vicious right hand in the second round, dropping him heavily to the canvas. Benn managed to get back to his feet, but Garcia immediately went on the attack again, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in after just one minute and 25 seconds of the round.

It was a crushing result for Benn, who had worked his way back into contention following his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Benn lost their first encounter by decision in April 2025 before getting his revenge with a points victory in November.

He subsequently returned to welterweight to challenge Garcia for the WBC title, but the American proved a step too far on the night.

The defeat also raised fresh questions about Benn's future at 147lbs, with making the weight having been a talking point in the build-up.

After the fight, Benn admitted he was unsure what came next and spoke about the sacrifices his boxing career had demanded of his family.

Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old

He made it clear that spending time with his children was his immediate priority, leaving his next move uncertain.

A lucrative showdown with McGregor would offer a very different route back into the spotlight from another world title challenge.

McGregor, meanwhile, has endured his own difficult return to competition.

The former two-weight UFC champion had been out of action since breaking his leg during his trilogy fight with Dustin Poirier in July 2021.

His long-awaited comeback against Holloway was supposed to mark the start of a new chapter, but things quickly went wrong.

McGregor injured his knee after attempting a jumping kick in the opening seconds of the fight. Unable to continue, he was forced to withdraw after just 69 seconds, handing Holloway the victory.

The result was a frustrating setback for the Irishman, whose return had generated enormous interest among UFC fans.

McGregor subsequently announced plans to undergo surgery, leaving his immediate and long-term future uncertain once again.

McGregor's long-awaited comeback ended in disaster at UFC 329 in Las Vegas (above)

The Irishman blew his knee out after throwing a kick within the first seconds of the bout

At 38, he remains one of the most recognisable figures in combat sports, but another comeback will depend on his recovery and whether he can return to full fitness.

A boxing match with Benn would be a different proposition from another UFC appearance, though it would still require McGregor to make a significant commitment to training and preparation.

McGregor is no stranger to a crossover fight.

His most famous venture outside MMA came in August 2017, when he faced Floyd Mayweather in one of the most heavily promoted boxing matches of all time.

McGregor had never competed in a professional boxing bout before, but that did little to dampen interest in the contest.

The pair embarked on an extraordinary promotional tour, trading insults in front of huge crowds as the fight became a global spectacle.

McGregor made a competitive start, but Mayweather quickly took control before stopping him in the 10th round.

Mayweather improved his professional boxing record to 50-0, while McGregor returned to the UFC having secured a huge payday and further cemented his status as one of sport's biggest commercial attractions.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'
Sports.content:
Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'

Australian boxing legend Jeff Fenech has been hospitalised with heart problems, with his NRL star son-in-law Bradman Best revealing the family’s concern ahead of his Kangaroos debut.

The four-weight world champion, 62, was admitted to Strathfield Private Hospital around 10 days ago after suffering severe fatigue, breathing difficulties and feeling unwell.

Fenech has since had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests to investigate whether a potentially life-threatening staph infection has returned.

A recurrence has not been confirmed.

Best, who has a baby daughter with Fenech’s daughter Kayla, disclosed the hospital stay while discussing the boxing great’s influence on his career.

The Newcastle centre is preparing to make his Australian Test debut against Fiji on Sunday, but took time to acknowledge Fenech’s health battle.

Jeff Fenech, 62, has been hospitalised after suffering heart problems, fatigue and breathing difficulties

Bradman Best paid tribute to his father-in-law ahead of his Australian Test debut

Fenech has reportedly had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests for a possible recurrence of a serious infection

‘Jeff has been massive for me, I just want to give a quick shout-out to him,’ Best said.

‘He’s actually in hospital at the moment.

‘I’m thinking of him. He’s tough, he’s always a fighter.’

Best said Fenech had become an invaluable source of advice as he worked towards representing Australia.

‘Jeff has done a lot for me in my career,’ he said.

‘I was visiting him last week and he’s always giving me tips on what to do and how to be better.

‘It’s special having a father-in-law like that who’s a four-time world champion.

‘He’s an icon in Australia and it’s special having a bond like that with him.’

Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his world-title clash with Erislandy Lara have been disrupted by his trainer’s hospitalisation

Fenech became one of Australia’s greatest boxers, winning world titles across four weight divisions during a career that earned him the nickname ‘The Marrickville Mauler’

Asked whether Fenech’s condition was serious, Best remained hopeful.

‘Yeah, he will be right. He’s always a fighter. He’s been in there with a few heart problems and stuff, but he’ll be good.’

The hospitalisation has also interrupted Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his planned WBA middleweight world-title clash with Erislandy Lara.

Fenech became Tszyu’s head trainer in July, helping guide him to a unanimous decision victory over American star Errol Spence Jr.

Tszyu credited the veteran trainer with helping inspire that result, which set up his pursuit of a world championship in a second weight division.

With Fenech sidelined, fellow trainer Basil Nassis has taken charge of Tszyu’s work in the gym.

The Lara bout is expected to take place in Australia in November or December, according to the reports.

Fenech hopes to recover in time to be involved, although the Telegraph reported he is unlikely to perform padwork during the build-up.

The latest scare follows two major heart operations.

In October 2019, Fenech underwent emergency open-heart surgery in Thailand while preparing Jack Brubaker for a fight against Tszyu.

He needed another six-hour open-heart operation in 2024 during a serious infection.

Sports.title: British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
'Bring him on,' roared Daniel Dubois when asked if he would like a third fight against the greatest boxer of his generation who has beaten him twice.

Oleksandr Usyk, who is in a state of limbo somewhere between vacating all the heavyweight tiles and semi-retirement, is a genius so may not fall readily into the trap baited on the banks of the Thames in the dark hours of this Sunday morning.

Ukraine's war hero will have watched Dubois annihilate the gallant Fabio Wardley and recognised that Dynamite Daniel is no longer the callow youth he wiped the canvas with a couple of times during his reign as the undisputed world champion.

Promoter Frank Warren is not given to understatement but when he said 'Daniel has matured now' he was only scratching the surface of the transformation.

It may be a stretch to compare Dubois with the once terrifying Sonny Liston but to those rivals wearing the other belts he needs if he is to become undisputed then he is starting to look like a monster.

'I want them all,' said WBO champion Dubois. He was referring to the winner between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December, who will thereby hold a WBA title, as well as IBF and WBC champions Filip Hrgovic and Ajit Kabayel.

Daniel Dubois knocks down Fabio Wardley during his annihilation on Saturday night

Dubois has declared himself ready to fight anyone in the heavyweight division

Their availability, especially that of AJ or the Gypsy King, will be determined no doubt by there being many more millions in the Aladdin's Cave from which Saudi Arabia has helped finance the welcome flux of mega-fights of late.

If so then Warren is promising a 2027 bursting with monthly heavyweight spectaculars as lustily anticipated as Dubois' second demolition of Wardley . At the rapid conclusion of which another packed O2 crowd was switching its allegiance from a love affair with Fabio's romanticised emergence from white collar boxing to realisation that Britain has a world beater in the ascendancy.

One who may be growing, also, into more of a box office star than the monosyllabic Liston ever was. If his accurate bravura prediction of a 'bash and smash' slaughter of Wardley and his most jovial media conference yet which followed are anything to go by.

Having nursed his confidence in the Dubois family cocoon Daniel now has a mansion of his own to live in and a selection of race cars to drive. No more Mister Shy Guy but none the less likeable for that.

The transition to full manhood was rounded off over the two fights with Wardley. This included recovery from two early knockdowns in the first Fight Of The Year battle to a brutal 11th round stoppage victory.

And now the onslaught triggered by a staggering right hand blow only 17 seconds after the first bell which imposed an eight count on the ropes. Followed by an overwhelming TKO in round two. Wham, bam and thank you man. No criticism this time of a delay in calling it off. In flew the white towel, in jumped referee Steve Gray.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua fight each other in December - and Dubois wants the winner

There has been some nagging at the edge of Dubois' triumph. Suggestions that Wardley came back too soon after the second-half beating in May. But if five-and-a-half months is not sufficient time to recover then how long would be? The immortal Joe Louis used to fight once a month, for heaven's sake.

Wardley, honest man that he is, blamed himself. Having lived to fight another day he vows to do better enough to launch a comeback campaign for another world title. Meanwhile Dubois, at 29 last month, heads for the stratosphere as champion of the next generation of heavyweight boxing.

As the new monster of the prize-ring? It took The Greatest Of All Time to stop the Liston beast In his awesome tracks. Might Usyk be the Muhammad Ali in waiting for Dubois? Maybe. Perhaps not since he is the older legend now. It would be fascinating finding out.

The tombstone on Sonny Liston's grave in Las Vegas describes him simply as A MAN. Frank Warren is right about Dubois becoming exactly that.

Sports.title: F1 Mexico GP: Norris tops final practice by 0.001s from Antonelli
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has topped third and final practice at Formula 1's Mexico Grand Prix, beating championship leader Kimi Antonelli in a tight session at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

Norris dipped just 0.001s under Antonelli's initial benchmark as all four top teams looked in the mix on the tricky high-altitude circuit, with several midfield running into power unit trouble.

A quiet opening phase saw Ryo Hirakawa get a lot of airtime in the Haas. Having covered FP1, the Toyota-backed driver returned to the Haas as a substitute for Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the Mexico weekend.

Ocon was benched by the squad for reasons which are yet to be fully clarified, with the Frenchman having a heated exchange with his race engineer in FP2.

Read Also: Formula 1 Haas drops Ocon for F1 Mexico GP

While 32-year-old debutant Hirakawa was building up confidence around the difficult and slippery, high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, champion-elect Antonelli and Charles Leclerc traded blows during the opening stages of the session as all frontrunners were running medium tyres.

Having missed valuable track time in FP2 with engine trouble, Lewis Hamilton came to the fore just before the halfway mark with a 1m18.268s, picking up where Ferrari left off as the squad was satisfied with the initial set-up direction on Friday.

Leclerc took another tenth out of his team-mate's lap time, before Hamilton took top with a 1m18.162s lap to lead the medium-tyre runs that dominated the first half of practice, followed by Leclerc and Antonelli as both Red Bull and McLaren looked a clear step behind.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Bolting on softs, reigning world champion Norris briefly claimed top with a 1m17.873s ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri and George Russell, who lamented a lack of grip through the tricky Turn 12 right-hander entering the Foro Sol stadium.

As Leclerc got out of shape through the Esses and backed out, Antonelli jumped to the top of the timesheets with a 1m17.601s lap, but not before voicing his frustration at Max Verstappen's impeding in Turn 1.

Antonelli then went purple in sector one on his next flyer but ultimately didn't improve. That opened the door for Norris to pip him by just 0.001s to head into qualifying with the fastest time of the weekend.

Leclerc found a late improvement with a rapid first sector but stayed in third, 0.117s behind, closely followed by Piastri. Verstappen was fifth, 0.351s behind as he struggled with his brakes, setting up another close qualifying session between 2026's four top teams.

An untidy third sector left Hamilton over four tenths adrift in sixth, followed by Russell and Hadjar, who called his Red Bull "the worst car I've driven this weekend, it's terrible".

Racing Bulls again looked well poised to win the best of the rest battle, with Liam Lawson pipping rookie team-mate Arvid Lindblad to ninth as they rounded out the top 10.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Manuel Eletto / Getty Images

Hirakawa ended his session in 19th, just ahead of Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas. Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto didn't manage to set a lap time after encountering a power unit issue on his out-lap, with a puff of smoke emanating from an ill-sounding engine.

Home hero Sergio Perez also failed to set a lap, with Cadillac announcing it would have to perform a "precautionary engine change" ahead of qualifying.

Sports.title: Red Bull provides timeline for long-awaited new F1 wind tunnel
Sports.content:
Although Red Bull has turned its 2026 Formula 1 season around in impressive fashion, the technical team led by Pierre Wache is still dealing with several limitations behind the scenes. One of the main ones is perhaps the wind tunnel, the oldest on the entire F1 grid.

Former team principal Christian Horner repeatedly described Red Bull's wind tunnel as "a Cold War relic" and said working with the 70-year-old facility near Bedford was like looking at "two different watches", highlighting that the correlation had more than once failed to match what happened on track.

Red Bull has seemingly suffered little from that while improving its 2026 challenger, although Mekies acknowledges that the new facility should, in theory, provide the team with a competitive advantage.

"I think you're right. As much as the wind tunnel that we are using has ultimately been producing extraordinary results over the last few years, I think you are right in your assessment that it is most likely the oldest one on the grid," Mekies said when asked about the wind tunnel by Autosport.

"As a result, if you jump to a state-of-the-art facility – and the team have really tried to design and now produce something that will put us back at the very first place in that area – of course you expect a competitive advantage from there."

Wind tunnels have become a major area of investment in F1. McLaren used Toyota’s in Cologne from 2010, but has been able to rely on its own facility since the summer of 2023 – something clearly linked to the team’s progress since then.

Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Aston Martin also has a state-of-the-art wind tunnel on its Silverstone campus, described by Adrian Newey as the best in the business, although the benefits have yet to be reflected in the on-track performances due to other limiting factors.

The latter also underlines that a new wind tunnel does not immediately guarantee an improvement and that it often takes time to fully understand the new tool and extract its maximum potential.

"So, [the competitive advantage] is not going to come up as soon as we switch on everything," Mekies admitted. "But it's certainly going to unlock potential and give the talented people that we have in the aero department another way to express their ideas."

When Verstappen mentioned the new wind tunnel as one of the less obvious factors giving him confidence for 2027, he immediately made clear that it would naturally not help with the initial development of the RB23, which is already under way. However, he added that it could contribute to further development of the 2027 car throughout the season.

When Autosport asked Mekies whether he had an update on when Red Bull would actually be able to start using the new wind tunnel – which is located on the Milton Keynes campus, making things easier logistically as well – the Frenchman responded: "In terms of the timeline, it is not ready yet. It's something that will come online sometime during next season.

"Is it the first quarter, second quarter or third quarter? We will see. It will be based on how much time we need to get it online first, and then also to complete the calibration work. So, it will most likely be for the second part of the 2027 car and hopefully for most of the 2028 car."

Sports.title: Haas drops Ocon for F1 Mexico GP
Sports.content:
The Haas Formula 1 team has made the shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the remainder of the Mexico Grand Prix weekend.

Hirakawa will act as Oliver Bearman’s team-mate for final practice, qualifying and Sunday’s race, having also taken Ocon’s VF-26 on Friday morning as part of the rookie mandate for FP1 sessions.

Ocon returned for second practice, finishing 13th, but caused a stir following his spat with race engineer Laura Mueller over whether to stick to the soft tyres or switch to medium rubber.

A Haas statement read: “Ryo Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix.

“Ryo participated in FP1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Friday, his third free practice outing of the season driving the VF-26, finishing 15th overall.

“The Japanese driver will partner team-mate Ollie Bearman through final practice and qualifying on Saturday and Sunday’s 71-lap grand prix – marking Ryo's Formula 1 race debut.

“No further statements will be made at this time.”

Though Haas subsequently added: "No comment beyond the statement other than to confirm it’s not due to illness."

Ryo Hirakawa, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hirakawa’s F1 debut will come at the age of 32. He spent much of his career in Japan, becoming the 2017 Super GT champion, before moving to the World Endurance Championship.

He has claimed two WEC titles with Toyota, alongside victory at the Le Mans 24 Hours, and that relationship with the Japanese marque earned him a move to Haas as its reserve driver in 2025.

That came as the result of Toyota and Haas forming a technical partnership, leading to him contesting seven FP1 sessions and being a contender for a 2027 F1 seat - only to lose out to Rafael Camara.

For Ocon – who is set to be replaced by Camara – it marks a striking resemblance to how his Alpine stint ended in 2024, as he was replaced by successor Jack Doohan for the Abu Dhabi finale.

The 30-year-old Frenchman is likely to become Aston Martin’s reserve in 2027, Autosport understands, after a disappointing time since joining Haas in 2025 – comfortably being beaten by Bearman.

Sports.title: Stewards penalise Verstappen, Lawson after “unacceptable” F1 Mexico GP practice clash
Sports.content:
One of the most remarkable moments of Friday's Formula 1 practice sessions took place in the Foro Sol, otherwise known as the stadium section of the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

Max Verstappen tried to overtake Liam Lawson heading towards Turn 12 during the second session of the day, but the Racing Bulls driver defended, leaving both drivers side by side going into the stadium.

Verstappen was on the outside of Turn 13, where he felt he was forced off the track by his former team-mate. The Dutchman then went over the kerbs at Turn 14, after which the drivers from the two Red Bull teams made contact.

The incident caused damage to Verstappen's bargeboards, which he had to contend with for the remainder of the session, already compromising his day.

Afterwards, the four-time world champion was rather outspoken in the media pen. Asked by Autosport what happened from his perspective, Verstappen said he did not understand “what went through Liam's head” and added: “For me, it's just not very smart behavior when you're in his position, to pick a fight with me.”

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane described it as a storm in a teacup, partly related to the circuit in Mexico and what is required to get the tyres into the right operating window.

“When you're doing a lap here, an out lap or a cool-down lap, one thing that's really important is to do the last sector fast. Doing that gives you good tyres for Turn 1. Without that, you risk front locking and things like that. They were both going for that, and I think if I describe it with one word, it's just unnecessary.”

Stewards hand out tougher penalties following earlier warnings

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

After their media duties, Verstappen and Lawson had to report to the FIA stewards, who ultimately handed both drivers a one-place grid penalty for Sunday's race and a penalty point on their superlicences – a decision that took hours.

“On the approach to Turn 12 car 3 was on a preparation lap and car 30 was on a cool-down lap preparing for another push lap", the FIA document reads.

“The drivers of both cars behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable by the Stewards, particularly in view of the warning that had been given at the Team Managers meeting earlier this day.

“Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and ‘clumsy’. Noting that there had been similar incidents this year of actions between drivers in Free Practice, the Stewards have decided to escalate the penalty from that of a formal warning to a grid position penalty, particularly in view of the warning that had been provided at the Team Managers meeting and consistent with other incidents involving contact between the cars in Free Practice in previous years.”

With the stewards keen to send a message following earlier warnings, both Red Bull teams have ended up losing out after an incident that, according to Permane, was above all completely unnecessary.

“I'm sure both drivers have their opinion on it. I think in the cold light of day, they'll be calm and think, actually, we could have both done better”, the Racing Bulls team principal told Autosport.

“I don't think anyone's picking a fight with anyone, that's for sure. I think it's just one of those things. And as I said: unnecessary.”

Sports.title: The confusion surrounding Colton Herta's F1 superlicence explained
Sports.content:
After completing more than 100 kilometres during the first free practice session at the Mexico Grand Prix, Colton Herta appeared to have 40 superlicence points to his name, which would be enough to qualify for the document required to secure a Formula 1 seat.

The reality, however, has proved far more complicated than that. According to the FIA, Herta is currently still one point short.

Confusion surrounding IndyCar’s 2025 season

First, back to basics. There are two ways to accumulate the required 40 points from other championships. The FIA can either look at all the points accumulated over the previous three calendar years or consider all the points earned over the previous two years plus the current season.

“The driver must have accumulated at least 40 points. The FIA will consider the number of points accumulated in either (i) the three-calendar year period immediately preceding the year of the date of the application, or (ii) the two-calendar year period immediately preceding the year of the date of the application in addition to points accumulated in the calendar year of the application, whichever is higher”, the FIA's International Sporting Code states.

In Herta's case, it appears to be the former option: the previous three years plus the F1 practice sessions he has completed during the current season, as those are not tied to a specific year. The American has brought 35 points with him from IndyCar – more on that later – and earned another four through his F1 free practice appearances.

There has been considerable confusion in the Mexico paddock over those IndyCar points in particular, and whether the total should be 35 or 36. One of those points dates back to the 2023 IndyCar season; 30 come from the 2024 season, when he finished runner-up; the remaining confusion relates to 2025.

Anyone looking up the results of the 2025 IndyCar season online, for example on Herta's Wikipedia page, will see him listed in seventh place, which would be worth just four superlicence points. Herta finished that season level on points with Felix Rosenqvist.

Colton Herta, Andretti Global Photo by: Penske Entertainment

Initially – when the FIA conducted its investigation in July – Herta was listed sixth in the IndyCar standings, which would earn him six points. With those six points, he would now have reached 41 points, comfortably exceeding the required 40 – which was also the widespread belief in the paddock immediately after the first practice session.

However, that proved incorrect. The FIA subsequently informed Autosport that, following further investigation, Herta has definitively been classified seventh in the 2025 IndyCar season, meaning that, as things stand, he has only 39 points and does not yet qualify for a superlicence.

This means Herta needs one more F1 practice session to meet the requirements, for which Cadillac could use the upcoming Sao Paulo Grand Prix or the next F1 weekend on American soil in Las Vegas. Cadillac has already expressed its intention to give its protege more free practice outings, meaning he will meet the superlicence requirements in any case, but, according to the FIA, he has not yet done so in Mexico.

How long is the superlicence valid, and what does this mean for Cadillac?

An equally interesting question is exactly how long Herta's superlicence will remain valid once it can officially be applied for and issued by the FIA.

Strictly speaking, a superlicence is only valid for one year, which might suggest that it is now or never for Herta's potential F1 opportunity, and that it has to happen in 2027. This is linked to the 30 superlicence points from the 2024 IndyCar season, which might expire after 2027.

However, when Autosport put the matter to the FIA, the reality proved somewhat more complex than that as well – and somewhat more favourable for Herta. Yes, the superlicence itself is only valid for one year, but applying for it also provides a three-year safety net.

This safety net is linked to Article 13.1.5 b of the International Sporting Code, which states that the following is also sufficient to obtain another superlicence:

“The driver must also satisfy at least one of the following requirements:

“b) Have been granted a Super Licence (excluding Free Practice Only Super Licence) and, prior to application, have previously completed at least 100 km during a free practice session of an FIA Formula One World Championship competition, in any of the previous 3 years.”

Colton Herta, Hitech Photo by: Getty Images

In concrete terms, this means that once a driver has obtained a superlicence and it expires after a year, they fall into the category of 'previous licence holders'.

Those 'previous licence holders' can apply for another superlicence without having to meet the 40-point requirement again, provided they have completed at least 100 kilometres during an F1 free practice session.

This effectively means that, after applying for Herta's superlicence, Cadillac will have a three-year window in which to give him an F1 opportunity, if that is what the American team intends to do. If that opportunity does not come immediately in 2027, Herta's 30 IndyCar points will indeed expire in the future, but he can regain the superlicence in the following years with just one free practice session – without having to worry about the 40 points again.

Formally, Cadillac still has to confirm its driver line-up for 2027. Sergio Pérez's contract was renegotiated and extended until at least 2029 ahead of his home race in Mexico, but in Austin, Marcin Budkowski refused to answer a very simple question from the F1 presenter with a 'yes'.

The team principal was asked whether both drivers had contracts extending beyond the current season, but Budkowski avoided the question by saying that the FIA press conference was not the place to discuss it.

He thereby left the door open for a possible driver change ahead of the 2027 F1 season. Valtteri Bottas subsequently told Autosport, when asked, that he was not yet concerned about potentially losing his F1 seat.

Sports.title: F1 Mexico GP: Leclerc pips McLaren and Mercedes to top FP2
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc completed a perfect Friday at the Mexico Grand Prix after topping the second Formula 1 practice session, in spite of Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton retiring.

The Monegasque topped FP1 with a 1m18.128s before lowering that to a 1m17.827s in FP2 at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, pipping McLaren’s Lando Norris in second.

Norris was one of 10 drivers to have handed their car to a ‘rookie’ in opening practice, but the entry list returned to normal for FP2, with it no surprise to see many out early for the second one-hour session.

All three tyre compounds were in use early on and medium-runner Hamilton initially set the pace with a 1m18.741s, 0.498s quicker than second-placed Piastri on hard rubber in his McLaren.

But, like in FP1, track evolution made a significant difference at the low-grip circuit as Leclerc quickly lowered his team-mate’s benchmark by 0.484s to a 1m18.257s.

That was done on medium tyres whereas quickest with the softs early on was sixth-placed Max Verstappen, who set a 1m19.312s before contributing to the 15th-minute red flag.

The Red Bull driver opted to go wheel to wheel with Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson through the stadium sector and the rather excessive incident caused debris to fly onto the track.

So the session was halted for five minutes before green conditions returned and medium runner Kimi Antonelli quickly split the Ferrari pair with a 1m18.559s, 0.302s behind Leclerc.

But the Monegasque did subsequently appear set to stretch his advantage on soft tyres by going purple in the first two sectors, only to go wide through the stadium and abort his lap.

That cost him the lead as reigning world champion Norris, also now on softs, went top after 25 minutes with a 1m18.161s, moments before Leclerc locked up into Turn 1 and aborted yet another lap.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

Piastri then split the Ferrari duo with a 1m18.896s on softs, just as Hamilton started to lose power down the main straight before stopping at the Turn 3 exit after 28 minutes.

The seven-time world champion caused a brief VSC, before lap times tumbled further on the softs in the second half as Leclerc lowered the benchmark by 0.195s to a 1m17.966s.

Leclerc went better again on his next lap, a 1m17.827s, which was 0.103s quicker than second-placed Norris, who gave his MCL40 to Leonardo Fornaroli for FP1.

But with 20 minutes remaining that marked the end of the soft-tyre laps as drivers started their high-fuel runs, though this came much to the dislike of outgoing Haas driver Esteban Ocon.

The Frenchman told race engineer Laura Mueller “don’t do that to me” when she suggested going onto medium rubber, a switch that still ended up happening.

Regardless, the late high-fuel runs meant Leclerc remained the benchmark ahead of Norris’ 1m17.930s, which put the 26-year-old just 0.003s ahead of third-placed George Russell.

His Mercedes team-mate Antonelli finished one behind with a 1m18.044s, ahead of Verstappen (1m18.138s) in fifth and sixth-placed Isack Hadjar (1m18.237s) aboard the sister Red Bull.

Racing Bulls took seventh via rookie Arvid Lindblad (1m18.389s), while Alpine’s Pierre Gasly (1m18.407s), Lawson (1m18.455s) and Piastri (1m18.469s) respectively completed the top 10.

Sports.title: F1 Mexico GP: Leclerc beats Antonelli to top FP1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was comfortably fastest in opening practice for the Formula 1 Mexico Grand Prix, beating runner-up Kimi Antonelli in a session 10 rookies took part in.

The Ferrari driver set a 1m18.128s that was six tenths faster than Formula 1’s champion-elect, whose Mercedes stablemate Frederik Vesti completed the top three with a 1m18.861s.

Vesti – in for George Russell – was one of 10 rookies contesting FP1 with all teams bar Ferrari fielding a youngster, as Mexico is a good place to do so due to the session happening in unrepresentative conditions.

Not only does it start at least 90 minutes before qualifying and the race do on Saturday and Sunday respectively, but the track also evolves aplenty during the weekend as it is rarely used throughout the year.

That evolution was seen early in practice as Leclerc initially set the pace with a 1m21.965s, before lap times continuously tumbled as hard-tyre runner Antonelli soon went 1.151s quicker.

The 20-year-old gained another seven tenths on his next run, a 1m20.155s, before Leclerc lowered the benchmark again to a 1m19.197s, 0.303s quicker than Antonelli’s following lap.

Both drivers frankly dominated the early runs amid power-unit problems on Isack Hadjar’s Red Bull, before Lewis Hamilton got in on the act with a 1m19.869s to go third after 25 minutes.

The Ferrari driver subsequently went quickest by 0.060s on his next run, a 1m19.137s, before soft tyre runs commenced at the start of the second half of the one-hour session.

It began with Leclerc going 1.009s faster than his team-mate’s hard-tyre benchmark with a 1m18.128s, soon before Antonelli went 0.659s slower on a 1m18.787s.

Drivers outside of the top three endured a tougher time in the low-grip conditions: technical problems plagued Audi stand-in Freddie Slater, while McLaren pair Leonardo Fornaroli and Oscar Piastri went off in sector one.

Leonardo Fornaroli, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

Piastri – at the place he lost the championship lead last year – just couldn’t get a tune out of his MCL40, going 1.248s off the pace on his soft-tyre lap with 15 minutes remaining.

Instead it was Vesti who got amongst the act, going third with a 1m18.861s and just 0.080s behind Antonelli.

It was around that time that Jak Crawford caused a brief virtual safety car, having stopped at Turn 1 in Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin, before drivers returned to the harder compounds for the final 10 minutes.

So Leclerc’s 1m18.128s went unbeaten, 0.659s and 0.733s quicker than Antonelli and Vesti respectively, while Hamilton finished fourth by going 0.738s off the pace.

Fifth went to Max Verstappen’s Red Bull substitute Ayumu Iwasa, the reigning Super Formula champion who set a 1m19.113s on mediums, ahead of sixth-placed Pierre Gasly on soft rubber.

The Alpine driver set a 1m19.210s, while Fernando Alonso (+1.229s), Piastri (+1.248s), Oliver Bearman (+1.284s) and Arvid Lindblad (+1.350s) completed the top 10.

Sports.title: Hamilton on why he is “built differently” to stay in F1 for the “foreseeable future”
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton intends to continue racing in Formula 1 “for the foreseeable future” if he can remain competitive, having been asked if he can realistically expect to race in the newly-announced African Grand Prix.

Earlier this month F1 revealed its plan for a new race in Rwanda, which will hold the title of the African GP, from 2030 at the earliest.

Hamilton, a long-standing figure who pushed for F1 to return to Africa, would therefore need to remain in the series well into his 40s to compete in the inaugural race in Rwanda.

The 41-year-old dismissed doubts he would retire from F1 before the first African GP would take place despite acknowledging he would be in his mid-40s if the race was to take place in 2030 – the earliest the event is planned, subject to track and infrastructure construction being completed in that time frame.

“Firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years. I feel that I'm built differently,” Hamilton said ahead of this weekend’s Mexican GP.

“Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee, that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off. Did you see my reaction in the last race? My reaction is faster than some of the youngest people here.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

“So there are lots of tools that you can utilise to continue to keep yourself, your mind sharp, as long as you're willing to sacrifice everything, which I am right now. I can't say in four years whether I want to continue to do what I'm doing, but I love what I'm doing still now.

“I'm still all in, and I will be for the foreseeable future.

“Whether or not I can compete at 44 with a 20-year-old, who knows? But at 41, I can compete with a 20-year-old. So, time will tell. Whether I'm here in the 30s, we'll see.”

However, Hamilton accepted he would not stay in F1 if he was not competitive, effectively setting himself the target of challenging for pole positions, wins and world titles over the remainder of the decade.

“But I never want to overstay my welcome, in the sense of not having the performance,” he said.

“I don't want to be driving around with that [pace] really, really dropped off, my reaction dropped off, my drive dropped off. My pace is dropped off, which everyone has seen last year, but I've proved everyone wrong with that, and I'll continue to try to do so.”

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hamilton isn’t the oldest driver on the current F1 grid, with 45-year-old Fernando Alonso committed to racing for Aston Martin in 2027 – giving the seven-time world champion a clear example that it would be possible to stay in F1 until at least 2030.

Coincidentally, both after the US GP and in the build-up to the Mexican GP, Alonso took aim at some of his younger F1 rivals when he said “the quality of the drivers in the low third of the grid is very low”, having been involved in an opening-lap clash with Alex Albon in Texas.

Alonso has stood by his comments and explained he felt it was a long-standing issue in F1.

“When you are at the back of the grid, the cars are more difficult to drive,” Alonso said in Mexico. “They have less grip and mistakes are coming more often because you don't have the environment that is under control. The car does not welcome you in a nice way, so you make more mistakes.

"But I feel that all the incidents in lap one, all the touches, all the front wings that fly around, all these kind of things are not necessary. Especially if you are fighting for nothing at the back of the grid.”

While the two topics are not directly connected, it demonstrates a belief from both Alonso and Hamilton that age is merely a number when it comes to competitiveness and racing in F1 – providing the skills and reactions remain high.

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: Norris beats Antonelli by a thousandth of a second in final practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The reigning world champion led the driver who will almost certainly succeed him this weekend in the final practice session for the Mexican Grand Prix.

A late flying lap put the McLaren driver ahead by the narrowest of margins. As the track gained grip slowly, Norris’s time was only two-tenths of a second quicker than yesterday’s best. Oscar Piastri was just under two-tenths of a second slower in the other McLaren.

Charles Leclerc, who headed yesterday’s two practice sessions at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, produced the third fastest time. Following the disruption to his second session yesterday, Lewis Hamilton completed a productive hour of running, setting the sixth-fastest time.

Max Verstappen, who has collected a one-place grid penalty for qualifying, was fifth in his Red Bull. He complained about braking problems during the session and went off at turn four.

The two Mercedes drivers were separated by over half a second. George Russell was seventh, fractionally ahead of Hadjar. The Racing Bulls pair completed the top 10 and showed very strong one-lap pace.

Having been very pleased with his car on Friday, Pierre Gasly went off-track several times in the final session. He ended up 13th behind his team mate and Nico Hulkenberg. Gabriel Bortoleto’s challenging weekend in the other Audi continued as he failed to set a time. Home favourite Sergio Perez also failed to complete a timed lap as Cadillac are changing his power unit.

Sports.title: Ocon out, Hirakawa in as Haas make shock Mexican Grand Prix driver change | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Haas has announced Esteban Ocon will not drive for the team in the rest of this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

Ryo Hirakawa, who took part in the opening practice session for the team yesterday, will take Ocon’s place.

The team confirmed Ocon is not ill. It has not given any reason for the change and said “no further statements will be made at this time.”

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu repeatedly refused to elaborate on the reasons for Ocon’s ousting when speaking to Sky during the third practice session. He did not confirm whether Ocon might return to the seat later this year or who could serve as a substitute next weekend, with Hirakawa due to return to his regular World Endurance Championship seat with Toyota.

Ocon is already due to leave Haas at the end of the season. Haas previously announced Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will take his place next year.

Hirakawa, 32, made his ninth appearance in an official F1 practice session with Haas this weekend. He has won the World Endurance Championship twice and taken victory in the Le Mans 24 Hours, both with Toyota.

While Haas is yet to give any reason for Ocon’s departure, he has previously been let go by a team before the end of a season. In 2024 Alpine dropped Ocon before the final race of the year, prior to his move to Haas.

Ocon placed 13th in yesterday’s second practice session ahead of team mate Oliver Bearman. However he expressed dissatisfaction with the team’s choice of tyre strategy to his race engineer Laura Mueller.

Haas did not indicate Hirakawa will remain in the seat for the rest of the season. There are four further rounds scheduled after the teams leave Mexico.

Sports.title: Hadjar given formal warning for pushing paddock visitor | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Mexican Grand Prix stewards have given Isack Hadjar a formal warning for pushing a visitor to the paddock.

The driver stated that he was running late for FP1 and had stopped to have a photograph with a young fan, when he was approached by a paddock guest in an aggressive manner. One security person was walking behind him and was unable to intervene and prevent what was tantamount to an invasion of the driver’s private space. The driver initially resisted the move by placing his hand on the waist of the guest, holding him at bay, then the driver pushed him aside with his open right hand.

This latter action by the driver is regarded as a breach of the regulations however in mitigation of penalty the stewards considered the following matters (in accordance with the guidelines provided in Appendix B of the FIA International Sporting Code):

a) The driver was reacting to an uninvited and rather aggressive action by another person

b) The driver was endeavouring to make his way to the start of FP1 through a congested area

c) The driver did not have sufficient security present

d) The guest was invading his personal space without his consent.

e) The general issue drivers have experienced moving through the Paddock

Sports.title: Claims Bearman’s salary demands delayed contract talks are “absolute nonsense” – Komatsu | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu has trashed reports about his team’s contract negotiations with its drivers.

Asked in Mexico whether there was any truth to claims driver Oliver Bearman was demanding €6 million (£5 million) to drive for the team next year, Komatsu said: “I have no idea where that comes from, honestly.”

Komatsu said fake stories about the team circulated on social media earlier this year. “I’ve experienced this sometimes this season as well,” he said. “Some people say there’s no smoke without fire, but really, some people invent the story.

“You know what happened in Miami, about apparently I had an argument with Esteban Ocon? There’s just absolutely zero truth in that. Even those people claiming that they had some insider information, et cetera, absolute total nonsense.

“This one, again, I don’t know who smoked up this six million euro number. That’s the first time I saw it on Instagram or something that Stuart [Morrison, Haas head of communications] forwarded to me. I was just like, ‘Oh, another great somebody came up with this, a good thing to stir whatever up.’

“I have no comment to make because it’s just not even close to the truth. Why do we engage in such absolute nonsense? What’s the point of it? Those people are clearly not trying to help anything, right?

“It’s amazing these days that people don’t check the source. So, okay, I want to get some more clicks, I want to get some more likes, so they cut-and-paste those stories and keep running with it. Before you know it, there are 20 people running the stories, so they think it’s the truth. It’s absolute nonsense.”

Haas has already confirmed Rafael Camara as one of their drivers for next season. With Ocon leaving the team, Komatsu is keen to finalise a new deal with Bearman.

“Ollie is showing amazing potential,” he said. “He contributed a lot and he’s contributing a lot to the team’s success. We want to grow together. We want to move up the grid as a team.

“So again, first and foremost, we need a competitive car in 2027. It’s not going to be an easy challenge because, again, in 2026 we made a mistake, so we’re paying the price for 2027 as well.

“But our focus is really to maximise everything under control, really trying to roll out a competitive 2027 car, and then hopefully we’ll have Ollie on board as well and then take it from there.”

Sports.title: Verstappen and Lawson handed one-place grid drops for “unacceptable” practice collision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have each received one-place grid drop penalties for colliding during the second practice session for the Mexican Grand Prix.

The stewards decided both drivers were responsible for the collision at turn 16. They also gave each driver a single penalty point on their licences.

The pair made contact at turn 16. Verstappen tried to overtake Lawson earlier in the lap but the Racing Bulls driver refused to give way. Lawson left no room for his rival at the exit of turn 13, but when Verstappen rejoined the track the pair made contact.

The stewards ruled a grid drop penalty was deserved in this case because similar incidents had happened involving other drivers earlier in the year.

“On the approach to turn 12 car 3 was on a preparation lap and car 30 was on a cool down lap preparing for another push lap,” they noted. “The drivers of both cars behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable by the stewards particularly in view of the warning that had been given at the Team Managers meeting earlier this day.

“Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and ‘clumsy’.

“Noting that there had been similar incidents this year of actions between drivers in free practice, the stewards have decided to escalate the penalty from that of a formal warning to a grid position penalty particularly in view of the warning that had been provided at the team managers meeting and consistent with other incidents involving contact between the cars in free practice in previous years.”

Verstappen criticised Lawson for the collision. “[It was] not very smart behaviour, what he was trying to do there,” he said.

The pair have been previously team mates at Red Bull on two separate occasions. Lawson returned to Red Bull’s second team, Racing Bulls, after substituting for Verstappen’s regular team mate Isack Hadjar earlier this year.

While Red Bull have announced Verstappen and Hadjar will continue to drive for them next year, Racing Bulls are yet to confirm their drivers for 2027.

“At the end of the day, it’s not going to change my weekend, but if I were him, I would act a little bit smarter,” said Verstappen. “Also, when you’re fighting for your seat, it’s not very smart behaviour.”

Sports.title: Leclerc fastest again, Verstappen and Lawson face investigation over collision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc topped both practice sessions on Friday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

Ferrari have now led the last five practice sessions in a row, including all three at the Circuit of the Americas last weekend.

The day did not go entirely smoothly for the Maranello team, however. Lewis Hamilton came to a stop due to a power unit problem having completed just 13 laps. He was therefore unable to do a qualifying simulation run and ended the session outside the top 10.

Lando Norris set the second-fastest time, a tenth of a second slower than Leclerc. George Russell, back in his Mercedes after Frederik Vesti drove it in first practice, took third ahead of his team mate.

The Red Bull pair were next, led by Max Verstappen, though he was carrying some damage following an earlier collision with one of the team’s junior cars. Verstappen attempted to pass Liam Lawson on the inside of turn 12, but the Racing Bulls driver was unwilling to surrender the position.

Lawson took the racing line at the exit of the sharp turn 13, obliging Verstappen to use the run-off area. Verstappen rejoined the track and hit Lawson, damaging both cars. The collision scattered debris over the track and the session had to be red-flagged while it was cleared up. The stewards will investigate the incident.

Isack Hadjar slotted in sixth behind his team mate. All four Red Bull-Ford-powered cars appeared in the top 10, Lawson taking ninth, two places behind his team mate, with Pierre Gasly’s Alpine in between them. Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren was 10th.

Sports.title: Bottas ‘needs to do’ more weekends like Austin to keep Cadillac seat – Budkowski | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski explained what Valtteri Bottas needs to do to keep his seat at the team as test driver Colton Herta becomes eligible for a superlicence.

The team confirmed Sergio Perez will continue as one of its drivers next year. It is yet to confirm whether Valtteri Bottas will also get a second season.

Budkowski said the team extended Perez’s contract because he’s “been overall the quicker and the better driver this year.” He said Bottas needs to consistently perform at the level he demonstrated in Austin last weekend.

“He’s done a really good race in Austin,” Budkowski told Sky. “He was strong in qualifying, he was strong at the race. That’s what he needs to do, race in, race out.”

Bottas has been puzzled by his inability to match Perez’s pace in some races, says Budkowski, who admitted the difference could be down to the preparation of their two cars.

“It’s actually the question we’re asking ourselves collectively with Valtteri and with the engineering team, because some races we don’t actually see a reason for it in the data,” he said. “Valtteri doesn’t see a reason either in terms of the fact there’s no big issue in the car.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an experienced race driver, he knows what he can extract from a race car and what he can’t, and he just says ‘I can’t extract more pace from this car’.

“But let’s face it, we’re a new team, this car is not a perfect car. The car has been put together in a very short period of time by a team of people who have never worked together before and from a white sheet of paper.

“We have to accept that we’re not giving these guys the best possible equipment and we don’t have as a team enough strength and depth to have full certainty that the equipment we have is perfect. So we’re looking at it together, from the team’s side and from the driver’s side and that’s also why we’re taking the time to try to understand exactly what’s going on.”
