Sports.title: Leclerc puts Ferrari on top in practice again in Mexico | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc started the Mexican Grand Prix on top by setting the fastest time in the opening practice session.

It was the fourth consecutive practice session headed by a Ferrari, after the team led all three sessions in Austin a week ago.

The two Mercedes drivers came next, Andrea Kimi Antonelli leading Frederik Vesti, who took over from George Russell. Vesti lapped within a tenth of a second of the driver who can clinch the world championship on Sunday.

The majority of teams ran junior drivers in the opening practice session. Behind Lewis Hamilton, Ayumu Iwasa set the quickest time by any driver who did not use the soft tyres. Isack Hadjar in the other Red Bull ended the session outside the top 10 after being delayed by a power unit problem.

Pierre Gasly took sixth while Fernando Alonso put his Aston Martin much further up the times sheets than usual with the seventh-fastest time.

Oscar Piastri, the quickest McLaren driver, was only eighth. Leonardo Fornaroli, replacing Lando Norris for this session, struggled to brake as aggressively as he needed to at turn one, running wide during his soft tyre run.

Oliver Bearman and Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Formula 2 driver Nikola Tsolov became the first Bulgarian driver to participate in an official practice session and impressed by lapping a tenth of a second slower than the team’s regular driver.

Other newcomers had less smooth sessions. Audi sent Freddie Slater out of the garage with a fan assembly in his right-hand sidepod. He had to pit to have it removed, then return to the garage for a longer stay due to overheating. The stewards are investigating the team’s unsafe release of the car.

Jak Crawford, driving Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin, parked up with a technical problem after leaving the track at turn one.

Colton Herta ended the session at the bottom of the times but passed an important milestone. Completing 30 laps ensured he will reach the 40 superlicence points he needs in order to be allowed to race in Formula 1.

Sports.title: Reito Tsutsumi Blasts Raymundo Rojas in Two Fast Rounds
Sports.content:
Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) overwhelmed Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) with speed and clean combinations, forcing a second-round TKO in a super featherweight bout on Saturday’s Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli undercard. The Japanese southpaw took control early and gave Rojas little opportunity to turn his experience into anything useful.

Scheduled for ten rounds, the fight barely got going before the difference in technique became decisive. Tsutsumi pressed the action without sacrificing accuracy, putting punches together against an opponent who struggled to keep up. Rojas needed something to interrupt that attack, but he could not establish enough offense to make Tsutsumi hesitate.

The 24-year-old’s hand speed was the most obvious advantage. Rojas was repeatedly dealing with combinations rather than single shots, leaving him occupied with defending when he needed to be answering. Tsutsumi kept the initiative and prevented the Mexican from settling into a more competitive contest.

There was purpose behind the pressure. Coming forward alone would have given Rojas opportunities to use his own power, but Tsutsumi’s cleaner delivery made the aggression effective. He was able to attack quickly enough that the veteran had little room to build a response.

By the second round, Rojas had been unable to change the direction of the fight. Tsutsumi continued landing and brought matters to an early end, completing his fifth consecutive stoppage victory. It was another short night for a prospect whose opponents have struggled to make him work through the later rounds.

Rojas entered with eleven knockouts and more professional bouts behind him, giving him at least the possibility of making Tsutsumi respect his punching power. That possibility never became a sustained threat. The gap in speed and technique left Rojas trying to cope with the attack rather than impose his own fight.

For Tsutsumi, the encouraging part was how quickly he made those advantages count. A heavy favorite can win without revealing much, particularly against an opponent unable to offer a serious challenge. Here, the Japanese fighter at least avoided wasting time or letting the contest become untidy: he took charge and finished.

His strong amateur background, which included World Youth Championships gold, helps explain the polish he already brings to these early professional appearances. Saturday’s performance showed a fighter comfortable taking the lead on a major card, rather than one who needed several rounds to find his confidence.

The limitation is that another early finish leaves his longer-distance work largely unexplored. This was booked for ten rounds, but Rojas could not provide the sustained test that distance was intended to allow. Tsutsumi’s ability to adjust against someone who can match his speed or withstand his combinations remains a task for future opposition.

He has earned a more demanding opponent. Rojas could offer neither enough offense to slow him nor enough defensive success to extend him, and the result became one-sided quickly. Tsutsumi delivered what was expected of him, with the accuracy behind the stoppage offering more encouragement than the unbeaten record alone.

Sports.title: Canelo vs Mbilli Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates and DAZN Coverage
Sports.content:
Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) overwhelmed Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) for a second-round TKO in their scheduled ten-round bout. The Japanese southpaw took charge early, using his speed to land clean combinations before Rojas could establish himself.

Rojas struggled to cope with the quicker, more polished prospect and could not slow his attack. Tsutsumi kept pressing, turning his technical advantage into damaging offense rather than allowing the Mexican time to recover.

The second-round stoppage completed a one-sided performance and gave Tsutsumi his fifth consecutive knockout victory. Rojas brought regional experience and respectable punching power, but neither was enough to bridge the difference in speed and technique. Tsutsumi looked ready for a sterner test after another opponent failed to take him beyond the early rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0) upset David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds to claim the WBC Silver featherweight title. The Filipino southpaw started quickly, using his speed and cleaner power shots to prevent the taller favorite from settling.

Picasso had substantial height and reach advantages but too often allowed Martin to dictate the pace rather than keeping him outside. Martin’s busier work and heavier-looking punches gave him the stronger argument in rounds where neither fighter sustained control.

Picasso had his successes in a competitive fight, but his quieter stretches left openings for Martin to seize the initiative. Two judges favored the unbeaten challenger, rewarding a performance built on activity and effective aggression against a more established opponent. Moving up in weight, Martin earned a significant victory while Picasso paid for failing to make his physical advantages count.

Super featherweight Sultan Almohammed (6-0) scored a sixth-round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision over Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas after six rounds. The 18-year-old Saudi prospect dictated the action with persistent pressure, making the Mexican fight at his pace.

Almohammed maintained his intensity throughout, but Urvina Villegas proved tougher to finish than some of the teenager’s earlier opponents. The Mexican kept battling despite being outworked, forcing the heavy favorite to go the distance.

Almohammed closed strongly, putting Urvina Villegas down in the final round to underline his superiority. The knockdown capped a clear victory, even if the prospect could not produce another early stoppage. Six rounds against an opponent who kept competing gave Almohammed useful work beyond the quick finishes that had marked his early career.

Super middleweight Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) demolished Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) with a first-round knockout, ending their scheduled ten-round fight at 2:57. The unbeaten Kazakh attacked early with heavy, accurate punches, giving the Mexican veteran little opportunity to settle.

Nurmaganbet scored two knockdowns as his southpaw power proved too much for the 37-year-old. The violent finish immediately drew Knockout of the Year talk from DAZN.

Vázquez Rodríguez’s experience offered little protection once Nurmaganbet began landing, and he was overwhelmed before the opening round was over. This was a destructive performance, although beating an older opponent coming off a defeat leaves tougher tests ahead. Nurmaganbet supplied the kind of emphatic finish expected from a heavy favorite and delivered one of the early undercard’s biggest moments.

Emiliano Rojo stopped Flavius Biea at 1:37 of the fourth round, securing Team Mexico’s first victory of the night in their super middleweight bout. The 20-year-old controlled the middleweight bout with steady pressure, walking down his Romanian opponent and making him work at Rojo’s pace. Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) struggled to halt the younger fighter’s advance as Rojo’s activity gradually wore him down.

Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) looked comfortable taking the initiative against the more experienced veteran, keeping the pressure on until the referee intervened. It was an effective performance, although Biea’s recent stoppage defeats limit how much can be read into the result. The 20-year-old Rojo did what a heavy favorite needed to do, finishing an opponent whose career was already heading downhill.

Super middleweight prospect Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) defeated Hector Aguirre by an eight-round unanimous decision, but the unbeaten Cuban had to work for it. Aguirre pressed León and forced him into a tough, competitive fight that exposed some flaws in the favored prospect.

León started rounds well, only to let his work rate drop and allow Aguirre to back him up. Those lapses gave the Mexican opportunities to keep the action close rather than letting León take control.

Aguirre lacked the punching power to make those stretches more costly, but he pushed León through the full eight rounds before suffering his first professional defeat.

Sports.title: Carl Jammes Martin Stuns David Picasso in Ten Round Featherweight Upset
Sports.content:
Carl Jammes Martin pulled off a major upset against David Picasso, claiming the WBC Silver featherweight title by split decision after ten hard rounds. The unbeaten Filipino gave up noticeable height and reach, yet he neutralized those deficits through relentless tempo, explosive entries, and sharper power punching while Picasso struggled to enforce his natural advantages.

Picasso surrendered the center of the ring immediately. Instead of posting a long jab to halt the shorter challenger, the Mexican drifted backward and yielded control. Martin dictated every exchange, leaving Picasso hunting for single counter shots while mounting zero sustained offense.

The scores were 96-93 Martin, 95-94 Picasso, and 95-95 Martin.

Martin jumped on him immediately. Fast combinations carried the southpaw inside where his cleaner power punches caught the judges in tight rounds. Picasso fired back in spurts, but sporadic work never derailed the challenger.

The bout featured stretches of sharp technical exchanges, but Martin maintained a higher operational gear. Whenever Picasso tapped the brakes, Martin surged into the void, obliging the favorite to trade instead of resetting safely behind his guard.

That hesitation proved fatal for Picasso. A long reach functions as a defense only if it fires continuously. Because Picasso neglected to post a reliable perimeter, Martin stepped inside repeatedly without facing heavy incoming fire.

Martin handled tight spots well, staying composed whenever Picasso rallied. Securing the cards did not require total domination; Martin simply stayed busier and landed the more damaging shots across ten rounds to win over two of the ringside officials.

The split scorecards showed how tight several rounds were, yet Martin undeniably carved out the win through pure labor. He outworked the favorite during quiet sequences and scored whenever Picasso settled for single, isolated attacks.

The setback hits Picasso hard, coming shortly after his stoppage of Maicol Rincon and his resilient twelve round showing against Naoya Inoue last December. Toughness alone could not rescue this fight against a challenger setting an urgent pace.

Stepping up in weight elevated the magnitude of Martin’s triumph. The top ranked WBO super bantamweight proved he can outbox premier competition over the distance without relying on a knockout punch.

Martin walks away with a defining scalp and a clearer path to world title opportunities. Picasso departs carrying severe regret after failing to deploy the length, seasoning, and command needed to hold off a determined fighter.

Sports.title: Michael Zerafa Could Inherit Bentley’s Yoenli Hernandez Risk
Sports.content:
Michael Zerafa could inherit the world title opportunity Denzel Bentley left behind, but getting past Yoenli Hernandez would be a much tougher proposition. The Australian is reportedly the likely opponent for the vacant WBO middleweight championship, and I would strongly favor the Cuban if that fight gets signed.

Uncrowned reports that Zerafa is likely to face Hernandez despite Vito Mielnicki Jr. and Tim Tszyu sitting above him in the WBO rankings. The pairing has not been officially ordered. Bentley’s stripping has created an opening, but the dangerous opponent attached to that championship remains.

Calling Zerafa the beneficiary misses half the calculation. He could receive another chance to become champion while accepting the fight Bentley chose not to take. There is considerable value in that opportunity, provided Zerafa can do something with it.

His previous world title challenge supplies a warning. Erislandy Lara stopped him in two rounds in March 2024, dropping him with a combination finished by a straight left. Zerafa barely had time to establish himself before his championship bid was over.

Hernandez is orthodox and should be judged on his own work rather than treated as another Lara simply because both are Cuban. Still, Zerafa’s defeat showed how quickly an accurate opponent can punish his defensive openings. Against Hernandez, he would need to establish an effective jab and avoid remaining within punching distance after finishing his attacks.

Hernandez (11-0, 9 KOs) gives Zerafa another reason to be cautious. The Australian cannot afford to surrender the initiative while waiting for the Cuban to slow down. He would need enough offense to interrupt Hernandez’s work without becoming careless in the process.

The financial history makes this opportunity harder to celebrate without qualification. Warriors Boxing won the original Bentley–Hernandez purse bid with a $200,000 offer, of which Bentley was entitled to $150,000. Those figures do not establish what Zerafa would earn under a new agreement, but they illustrate the limited bidding interest in the original contest.

Bentley committed to a November 7 Zuffa Boxing fight against Shane Mosley Jr. instead. The WBO rejected his appeal and formally stripped him on Friday. He lost his championship while securing an opponent who, in my view, offers a more favorable matchup than Hernandez.

Zerafa has also pursued Chris Eubank Jr., publicly accusing the British fighter of pricing himself out of a proposed contest. Taking Hernandez would offer a clearer championship objective, but a damaging defeat could weaken Zerafa’s bargaining position for an Eubank fight later. There is no confirmed Eubank deal to sacrifice, though the commercial alternative matters.

If Zerafa accepts, he deserves credit for taking the risk. However, the belt becoming vacant does not make Hernandez easier to beat. Zerafa could be gaining access to a championship fight that leaves him facing a far greater challenge than the word “opportunity” suggests.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder And Jai Opetaia Agree To Fight
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia is taking a dangerous route toward a potential David Benavidez fight, with a deal reportedly agreed for him to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard. Wilder offers the Australian a recognizable name and access to Netflix’s audience, but his right hand could wreck those plans.

The heavyweight bout is not signed, according to Dan Rafael, who reported that the sides have reached an agreement. Fury and Joshua headline December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, giving Opetaia an opportunity to introduce himself to viewers who have never followed his cruiserweight career.

“Per source, while it’s not signed yet, deal is agreed to for Wilder-Opetaia to be on the #FuryJoshua card,” Rafael wrote on X.

That represents progress from the earlier discussions. Dana White had previously confirmed that Wilder was among the opponents being considered for Opetaia, while identifying Benavidez as the fight his cruiserweight star wants.

There is an obvious commercial reason to take this detour. Another cruiserweight victory might strengthen Opetaia’s standing among dedicated boxing followers without doing much to expand his audience. Wilder’s name could help him reach casual viewers, particularly on a card built around two of Britain’s most recognizable fighters.

The sporting reward is less clear. Wilder has won his last two fights, but his latest victory was a narrow split decision over Derek Chisora in April. Before those wins, he lost four of five bouts, including three defeats by stoppage. Opetaia would be facing a former champion whose recent results have diminished the value of beating him.

That leaves Opetaia in a tough position. Outboxing Wilder would invite the response that the American was already well past his best. Getting caught by him could cost Opetaia far more than a defeat at cruiserweight, because it would damage the unbeaten record helping sell a Benavidez fight.

Wilder does not need to rediscover everything he once had to make this dangerous. Opetaia still has to close the distance, land his combinations, and get out without leaving an opening for the right hand. Moving up in weight gives him less room for a mistake against a puncher of Wilder’s reputation.

There is also a difference between keeping active and taking a heavyweight fight before returning to cruiserweight. Even a victory could come with an injury or a hard enough night to complicate the timing of his next bout. Until Wilder is beaten and Opetaia comes through healthy, the Benavidez fight carries an extra obstacle.

For Wilder, the attraction is clear: beating an unbeaten cruiserweight star would give his career a substantial lift. For Opetaia, the calculation is tougher. He needs Wilder’s recognition, but he also needs enough of a performance to make viewers remember the winner rather than dismiss the opponent.

Netflix could give Opetaia the audience he has been missing. Whether that exposure is worth putting a potential Benavidez fight at risk is what makes this more than a routine undercard addition.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Leaves Top Rank, But Will Zuffa Pay?
Sports.content:
Keyshawn Davis is officially free from Top Rank, paving the way for Zuffa to sign him and jump-start talks for a clash with Richardson Hitchins. Still, switching promoters will not automatically fix the persistent hurdle stalling Davis through his recent negotiations: agreeing on purse money.

Tim Bradley addressed the split once Bob Arum confirmed Davis received an early release. Hitchins, who already signed with Zuffa, claimed Davis priced himself out of their bout by demanding $6 million. While that number is strictly Hitchins’ version of events, Davis previously turned down the financial package to challenge Devin Haney, proving money remains the sticking point.

Having both men under the Zuffa umbrella clears a major promotional hurdle, yet it guarantees nothing. Shakur Stevenson’s inability to finalize an in-house bout with Rayo Valenzuela serves as a clear warning that shared promotional backing cannot force fighters to sign off on numbers they dislike.

Bradley pushed that point on his YouTube channel, questioning Davis’ market value.

“Keyshawn ain’t worth no $6 million. Sorry, he not,” Bradley said on his channel. “The last time you fought at home, you didn’t even sell out the arena.”

That critique highlights Davis’ real test. Ring talent alone does not guarantee pay-per-view buys or live gates. Unless a promoter is willing to absorb a financial loss, Davis must align his demands with what the event actually earns.

Bradley made clear he views this purely as business rather than intimidation.

“I don’t think Keyshawn is scared of Hitchins,” Bradley said. “He wants what was promised to him. That’s it.”

Bradley did not cite evidence of an explicit promise, and he openly noted that his speculation about Davis possibly paying a buyout fee was just personal opinion.

Keyshawn now controls his promotional future. Going to Zuffa might make a Hitchins bout simpler to stage, but if his payout demands do not budge, his new team will run into the exact same dead end that Top Rank just walked away from.

The chances of Zuffa signing Davis are real simply because Dana White wants elite, recognized talent to build the promotion’s roster alongside guys like Shakur Stevenson and Richardson Hitchins. But signing him and actually getting him into a ring without losing their shirts are two completely different problems.

Keyshawn’s self-valuation has completely detached from his real-world box office metrics. Turning down a mandatory shot at Devin Haney for the WBO welterweight belt because a $2.14 million purse bid split felt “embarrassingly low” was telling enough.

Demanding $6 million to fight Hitchins, when Keyshawn’s career-high payday sits around $1 million, and he struggled to pack his hometown arena in Norfolk, shows he’s not in tune with his worth.

Zuffa has deep pockets, but Dana White did not build an empire by letting unproven ticket sellers dictate vanity purses. The entire UFC/Zuffa operational model relies on cost control, leverage, and making matches on company terms.

If Bob Arum and Top Rank, who developed Keyshawn from day one, decided letting him walk out of his contract early was better than dealing with his price tags, Zuffa is stepping right into that same situation.

If Zuffa signs him, it only works under two scenarios: Zuffa pays him a flat, inflated signing guarantee up front to lock him down, only to watch negotiations stall when they try to schedule Hitchins or Haney and realize Keyshawn refuses to budge on bout fees. Shakur Stevenson’s standoff over Rayo Valenzuela already showed that bringing guys into the same stable does not magically make contracts get signed.

Or Zuffa gives him a dose of reality. If Dana and company offer him standard market numbers tied strictly to live-gate revenue and pay-per-view incentives, Keyshawn might quickly discover that free agency does not mean a blank check.

Unless Zuffa is willing to burn millions just to stage Hitchins vs. Davis, Davis will either have to adjust his expectations or sit on the shelf.

Sports.title: Ducking Yoenli Hernandez Was Bentley’s Smartest Business Decision
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley no longer owns the WBO middleweight belt, but picking Shane Mosley Jr. over Yoenli Hernandez makes total sense for his career. Getting stripped of a world title is never an ideal situation.

Still, surrendering the hardware outside the ring sure beats taking a beating inside it against Hernandez. Bentley was simply not going to beat that guy.

By ducking Hernandez and sacrificing the WBO title, Bentley walks into an immediately winnable booking against Mosley Jr. instead. Dan Rafael reported that the WBO Grievance Committee officially dismissed Bentley’s appeal on Friday in a massive twenty-eight-page resolution. His November 7 bout can still proceed, yet he will enter the arena without his championship.

Dropping the belt hurts his prestige, but sharing twelve rounds with Hernandez would have extracted a much steeper toll. The Cuban amateur star operates as the real power at 160 pounds right now. Stepping into that mandatory test right as his promotional tenure began would have been sheer recklessness, especially with Hernandez likely stopping him early.

Mosley Jr. gives Bentley the perfect opening platform to look good under his new banner. Nobody should treat Mosley as a complete walkover, but that pairing remains manageable compared to facing the most lethal threat in the entire division.

The real prize sits just over the horizon. Should Bentley take care of business against Mosley, he immediately positions himself for massive in-house unification opportunities. Zuffa Boxing controls both IBF champion Aaron McKenna and WBC titlist Carlos Adames. A single victory over Mosley puts Bentley in prime position to challenge McKenna or Adames for their titles, completely bypassing the Cuban buzzsaw while fighting for even bigger gold.

Hernandez gets what he deserved anyway with an unblocked route to the vacant WBO strap. For Bentley, giving up the belt preserves his market value, protects his health, and sets up a direct line to brand-new world titles down the road.

Sports.title: Will Christian Mbilli Send Canelo Into Retirement?
Sports.content:
The former two-time undisputed super-middleweight world champion Saul “Canelo” Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) is a legend and a future Hall of Famer, but on Saturday night, October 31st, will the WBC champion Christian Mbilli send Canelo into retirement?

This world title bout is an intriguing matchup because it features Canelo’s skill set versus Mbilli’s work rate. The action is set to take place at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, airing live on DAZN PPV.

Back in June 2025, Christian Mbilli stopped Maciej Sulecki in the first round and won the WBC title. Three months later, Mbilli was involved in a hard-fought battle as his bout against Lester Martinez resulted in a split draw.

Going into this fight, the defending champion Christian Mbilli is the underdog. Despite the odds being against him, Mbilli has the opportunity to defeat the great Canelo Alvarez and send him into retirement.

Losing a fight is rare, but it’s not new to Canelo. What would be new is for him to lose this upcoming bout because it will mark the first time Canelo ever suffered back-to-back losses.

Suffering consecutive defeats could push Alvarez towards retirement. It’s a bold statement, and due to the statement, one would ask: what is Christian Mbilli’s path to victory?

Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) is a determined, physical, and hungry world champion. He’s facing a tall task, but his path to victory is his aggression and his punch volume.

The 31-year-old Mbilli has incredible endurance, which allows him to constantly press forward and attack the body and head of his opponent. Alvarez has experienced stamina issues in the past, so outworking and outlasting Alvarez is Mbilli’s clear path to victory.

On the flip side, if the 36-year-old Canelo Alvarez has anything left in the tank, then this bout could be tailor-made for him due to the fact that Mbilli will be standing right in front of him.

In the past, Alvarez has done really well against opponents who lack movement and footwork. With Mbilli posting up in a neutral position and constantly in attack mode, Canelo will have many counterpunching opportunities.

Canelo will have his chances in regards to landing the left hook, the uppercut, and shots to the body. Speaking of body punches, those types of shots are a big part of Mbilli’s arsenal, and it will be interesting to see if he can consistently land shots to Canelo’s body.

Styles make fights, and that’s why the Canelo vs Mbilli fight will be an action-packed event. However, the question is, on Halloween night, will Canelo be sent into retirement, or will he take a step towards one last run at becoming undisputed once again?

Ghana News.title: ‘Ghana Premier League not entertaining’ – Odotei on low patronage
Ghana News.content:
Vincent Sowah Odotei

Interim Management Committee (IMC) Lead Administrator of Accra Hearts of Oak, Vincent Sowah Odotei, has criticised the quality of entertainment offered by the Ghana Premier League, blaming it for the league’s poor attendance.

The Ghana Premier League has struggled with low attendances at stadiums in recent years, affecting the financial fortunes of clubs and the competition.

According to Odotei, fans are staying away from the stadiums because the league is failing to provide the entertainment that attracts supporters to football.

“Our football is not fit for purpose. Our football is not entertaining. In football, we’re not in the business of football; we’re in the entertainment business through it.

“Football is a drama. You need actors, you need stars that people will want to come and watch,” he said in an interview with JoySports.

Odotei cited former Hearts of Oak players Shamo Quaye and Ablade Kumah as examples of footballers who attracted supporters from their communities to the stadium.

“People came to watch Hearts of Oak because of Shamo Quaye and Ablade Kumah. They came from Tema, their community. You go to Newtown, Anas Seidu. You go to Mamprobi, Stephen Appiah and co. That’s where they come from.

“We don’t have that in our football. We are not providing the entertainment, so naturally, people will go to leagues that provide entertainment.”

Ghana News.title: Mahama secures six commitments in nuclear energy, agric, and other areas from Putin after Russia-Africa Summit
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has secured six commitments from Russian President Vladimir Putin following bilateral discussions on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, according to Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa.

The commitments are expected to deepen cooperation between Ghana and Russia in energy, defence, agriculture, education and security.

A statement by Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, outlining the outcomes of the meeting, said Russia had agreed to work with Ghana towards establishing a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power plant to strengthen the country's energy security and support industrialisation.

The proposed project is expected to revive Ghana's longstanding ambition to develop nuclear energy, an initiative associated with the vision of Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, whose administration began preparatory work on a nuclear research facility before the February 1966 coup.

President Mahama is also said to have secured a new defence cooperation arrangement aimed at helping Ghana acquire strategic military equipment to strengthen the capabilities of the Ghana Armed Forces.

On agriculture, the two countries are expected to deepen collaboration to increase grain production and improve access to fertilisers as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana's food security.

The statement further indicated that Russia had agreed to increase scholarship opportunities for Ghanaian students.

It said Ghana currently ranked second among African countries in terms of the number of students studying in Russia.

Another significant outcome of the discussions, according to the statement, concerns the participation of Ghanaians in the Russia-Ukraine war.

Following concerns raised by President Mahama, President Putin is said to have declared that Ghanaians would no longer be permitted to participate in the conflict, whether through irregular recruitment arrangements or voluntary enlistment.

The two countries have also agreed to revive the Permanent Joint Commission for Cooperation (PJCC), with Russia expected to host the next meeting in the coming weeks.

Ghana and Russia have maintained formal diplomatic relations since 1958, with both countries pursuing cooperation in various sectors over the years.

The latest engagements form part of efforts to strengthen the longstanding relationship and expand areas of mutual economic and strategic interest.

With a mixture of Afrobeats, highlife, dancehall and contemporary Ghanaian sounds, the beach rave is designed to give patrons an opportunity to unwind and enjoy live entertainment in a vibrant coastal setting.

Beyond the musical performances, the event features DJ sessions, games and other beachside activities, offering a complete entertainment experience for young people and music enthusiasts.

StarOil, Ayuda and KIVO are sponsoring the event.

As the celebration continues at Rehab Beach Club, patrons are set for an exciting blend of music, beach culture and Ghanaian entertainment.

Ghana News.title: GPHA honours industry partners, former management at 40th anniversary awards
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has honoured shipping lines, shipping agents, cargo customers, staff and former leaders as part of activities marking its 40th anniversary.

The awards dinner recognised industry players for their performance in cargo volumes and customer service, alongside individuals whose leadership and long service contributed to the development of the Authority and Ghana’s maritime industry.

Award categories included shipping lines and shipping agents by cargo volumes, roll-on/roll-off (RoRo) operations, dry bulk cargo volumes, container traffic measured in twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), outstanding customer service and top transit customers.

The ceremony also recognised past Directors-General, former directors of the Tema and Takoradi ports, union chairmen, pioneering female professionals and long-serving staff.

The event formed part of GPHA’s commemoration of four decades of institutional growth, industry partnership and service to Ghana’s trade and economic development.

Major-General Paul Seidu Tanye‑Kulono, the Director-General of GPHA, in a welcome address, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to recognise individuals and organisations whose leadership, dedication and partnerships had helped shape the Authority.

He expressed appreciation to past leaders and employees, as well as shipping lines, terminal operators, freight forwarders, transport operators, customers, and other industry partners for their contributions to the development of the ports.

Mr Johnson Asiedu Nketia, the Board Chairman, in his remarks, said the awards recognised commitment, professionalism, innovation and partnership among individuals and organisations that had contributed to the growth of GPHA and the wider maritime industry.

He said the Authority’s future competitiveness would depend on its ability to embrace innovation, improve operational efficiency, uphold good governance, and deliver value to customers and stakeholders.

Mr Joseph Bukari Nikpe, the Minister for Transport, delivering the keynote address, called for improved port efficiency, digitalisation and stronger connections among ports, roads, railways and logistics centres to position Ghana as a leading trade and logistics gateway for West Africa.

He identified six priorities for the sector: port efficiency and service excellence, digitalisation and innovation, multimodal connectivity, sustainability and safety, workforce development, and regional trade and integration.

The minister said achieving these objectives required sustained cooperation among government, GPHA, private-sector operators, customers and other stakeholders across the transport and logistics value chain.

He congratulated the award recipients and urged the industry to build on the Authority’s achievements through stronger partnerships, improved services and continued investment in people and technology.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa has earned my respect – Akwatia MP vows to lead demonstration if he resigns
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Akwatia, Bernard Bediako Baidoo, has thrown his support behind Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, declaring that he would personally lead a demonstration against the Minister if he resigns over allegations surrounding the distribution of financial support to Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa.

He described Mr Ablakwa as one of the best public officers the country has had, arguing that the Minister had been transparent in responding to concerns about the evacuation exercise and accounting for the funds involved.

His comments come after the Minority in Parliament demanded the resignation of Mr Ablakwa over claims that some Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa received less than the GH¢5,500 support package announced by the government.

The demand was made by the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, at a press conference in Parliament on Tuesday, October 27.

However, speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 31, Mr Baidoo questioned the basis of the Minority’s demand, insisting that the Minister had provided the necessary information when concerns were raised.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 31, Mr Baidoo rejected calls for Mr Ablakwa to step down, insisting that the Minister had earned his respect through his work in public office.

READ ALSO: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments

“I’ll say this today, the Honourable Okudzeto Ablakwa has really earned my respect as one of the best public officers we’ve ever had in this country. I’m telling you, and look, if he resigns, personally, I’ll lead the demonstration against him,” he said.

The Akwatia MP pointed to previous instances in which the Foreign Affairs Ministry had allegedly failed to respond promptly to requests for information under the Right to Information (RTI) process, contrasting them with the Minister’s response to the latest concerns.

He argued that Mr Ablakwa had made relevant information available within days of the matter being brought to his attention, suggesting that the Minister had demonstrated a willingness to account for the evacuation exercise.

Mr Baidoo also questioned the Minority’s decision to focus its allegations on payments relating to the commercial flights, while making little reference to the charter flight arrangements.

Turning to the Minority’s presentation of the figures, Mr Baidoo questioned the calculations used to arrive at the alleged financial discrepancies, arguing that they did not provide sufficient grounds for demanding the Minister’s resignation.

He challenged the approach, describing the press conference as poorly executed and arguing that the figures presented did not, in themselves, establish that the Minister had misappropriated or failed to account for the money.

“I would rather believe what the Minority has or has been saying, because they know better. But you see, when you take this presser, very unfortunately, badly done, incompetently done, I'm so shocked. If but for envy, for whatever reason, this should not come from the Minority of the Republic,” he said.

He further expressed disappointment that the Minority, which he believes should understand the processes involved in demanding accountability from public officials, had handled the matter in that manner.

Mr Baidoo suggested that the allegations should be examined on the basis of the information available rather than being used to push for the Minister's resignation.

He maintained that Mr Ablakwa's response to the concerns surrounding the evacuation exercise should be taken into consideration in assessing the calls for him to leave office.

Mr Baidoo, however, has dismissed the basis for the demand, arguing that the Minister’s response to the concerns raised and his willingness to provide information should be taken into consideration.

The demand follows reports that at least three people contacted from the evacuation list claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the GH¢5,500 announced by the government.

Meanwhile, Mr Ablakwa has denied the allegations, insisting that all Ghanaians on the evacuation list, including minors, received the full package comprising GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation.

Ghana News.title: Samson’s Take on Adu-Boahene: GHS49.1m stolen, or a story the evidence cannot sustain
Ghana News.content:
The High Court on Thursday dismissed an application by lawyers for former National Signals Bureau Director General Kwabena Adu Boahene and his co-accused to strike out portions of the Attorney General's written submissions.

Any suggestion that this signals the outcome is completely ignorant commentary on the law and procedure. Justice Achibonga's holding is essentially that a complaint about smuggling evidence or wrong attribution of testimony is immaterial because the court will only rely on the evidence on record and not merely what a lawyer says about it in his submissions.

If nonexistence evidence is found out, the court will expunge it. In fact, this early stage is only for prima facie determination and not pronouncement of guilt. Remember the famous ambulance trial involving Dr Cassel, Ato Forson and Richard Jakpa.

The High Court rejected their no-case submissions, but the Court of Appeal overturned that decision, acquitting and discharging them without requiring them to enter or, as we say, open their defence. That is precisely the kind of early termination the Adu Boahene defence now seeks.

If they are unsuccessful, they get to make their full case in a full trial. The question at this stage is whether the prosecution has presented enough evidence to require the accused persons to defend themselves at all. After calling four witnesses, the prosecution closed its case.

The defence has filed a 142-page submission of no case to answer. The Attorney General has responded in 25 pages, insisting there is a case to answer. When Attorney General Dr Dominic Ayine first announced this case, he alleged that 49.1 million Ghana cedis had been stolen through a fictitious US$7 million cybersecurity procurement.

He also spoke of luxury vehicles, expensive houses and properties abroad. NewsFile examined those allegations extensively. I took some flak for appearing to defend the Attorney General's decision to announce them publicly.

My position remains: the Attorney General has a right to inform the public, but the right to announce allegations is not a license to pronounce guilt. I'm a lawyer; I know that too well.

NewsFile has continued following the trial. We have even made a formal information request to ISE Holdings Limited, the Israeli company at the centre of the alleged procurement. But let's find out why the defence believes they have no case to answer. Here are five points from their 142-page submissions.

First, was the entire 49.1 million stolen? That's a question they ask. The defence acknowledges that three cheques were issued and the money moved. But they dispute the allegation that the entire amount was dishonestly appropriated. They point to banking records and transactions involving the National Security Coordinator as they seek to discount a total of 34 million Ghana cedis.

That's nearly 70% of the 49.1 million allegedly stolen. The prosecution has the burden to satisfactorily trace these funds and establish which transactions constituted dishonest appropriation. Money moving through an account is not by itself proof of theft.

The second argument important to the defence is that they ask the question: who authorised the transactions anyway, to be able to prove a crime? The defence argues that the source account was controlled by the National Security Coordinator for special security operations. They also rely on evidence that the coordinator signed or authorised the cheques. That's the difficulty they put the prosecution in.

The coordinator, at the material time, is deceased. But why were other appropriate national security officials not called to clarify the authorisation procedures and purpose of the payments? That's a question they ask. National security cannot excuse stealing, but neither can the institutional framework be ignored when determining whether stealing occurred.

Third, they ask, was the cybersecurity procurement fictitious? This was central to the Attorney General's original public pronouncement. The defence challenges the prosecution's account of the contracts, invoices, and alleged non-delivery. They point to documents concerning ISE Holdings Limited and argue that the prosecution has not established that the procurement was fictitious.

That is why Newsfile has sought information directly from ISE Holdings Limited. Was there a genuine contract? What was paid for? What was supplied? The allegation of fictitious procurement must equally rest on evidence.

Fourth, what became of the luxury properties so prominently announced? The Attorney General's initial disclosures painted a picture of substantial personal enrichment. The defence challenges whether the prosecution has established that the identified houses, vehicles, and other assets were acquired with the allegedly stolen funds.

Owning expensive property may attract the attention of law enforcement. They concede, but it does not, without more, prove that stolen money paid for those properties.

Fifth, and finally, what independently establishes the criminal involvement of Adu- Boahene's wife? The defence challenges whether the corporate relationship and financial transactions relied upon by the prosecution establish that Angela Adjei Boateng knowingly participated in the alleged crimes. Marriage is not conspiracy. Directorship is not proof of criminal intent.

Proof she did any wrong. The defence shouts the law loudly. I defended the Attorney General's right to inform the public when the case broke. I equally defend the accused person's right to challenge the allegations and insist that the state meet its burden. Accountability demands scrutiny of both those accused of stealing public money and those entrusted with prosecuting them.

So, after four witnesses, has the state established a case to answer on the alleged 49.1 million Ghana Cedi's theft? The supposedly fictitious procurement, the disputed assets, and the criminal responsibility of each accused? While the public commentary points to holes in the prosecution's case, the decision rests with the judge.

What matters is what the evidence actually establishes, not even the dramatic announcement and confident predictions at the start of the case or what you say. Let's never confuse the power to ….. with the proof required to convict. And that is my take.

Ghana News.title: Poison in Prison; Mahama’s 3rd term; Okudzeto’s evacuees – Enimil Ashon writes
Ghana News.content:
This “attempted poisoning” business at the Nsawam Prison! I am alarmed because I am concerned about the health of Chairman Wontumi.

But what type of poisoning was it: food, drug, drink? Or did some inmate blow a poisoned powdered substance that went through Wontumi’s nostrils or his mouth? In the first place, does Wontumi have a cell mate? Are prisoners allowed to share food, drink, or medicines with cellmates, or anybody for that matter?

The Ghana Prisons Service has, predictably, promised a “thorough” investigation. The question, however, is: what is being investigated–that someone attempted to poison Wontumi?

I thought the first action by the Service should have been to prove poisoning, and what better and more convincing proof can there be than the word of a medical officer?

First of all, was Wontumi rushed (sent) to the hospital? Is there a medical report? Ghana waits with bated breath for this report. Not unconnected with the poisoning issue is Wontumi’s call for prison reforms. News reports say he has begun to make interventions to improve the living conditions of inmates.

It is said of Krobo Edusei, one-time Minister for the Interior in the First Republic, that having spent time at Nsawam Prisons after the 1966 coup, he told friends that had he known or been ever told about the heat in Ghanaian prisons, he, as Minister, would have installed air-conditioners in all prison cells!!

Second matter arising: President Mahama and a feared third-term attempt.

Are the Minority in Parliament, in particular, and the New Patriotic Party seized of facts that make the President’s word a lie?. More than once, both directly and indirectly, Mahama has given his word that a third term is not on the cards for him.

For an undisclosed reason, however, the opposition is bent on letting everybody believe that they “know” the President is insincere in his protestations; that he, indeed, is eyeing a third term in office. Could it be because of the words of that Bono Region prophet whom Mahama visited recently?

The TV news item reported that the prophet predicted a third term for the President.

Or was it Prophet Roja’s statement on Angel FM and other platforms that he foresaw John Dramani Mahama making a comeback for a third term and claiming victory?

He “prophesied” during a radio interview that John Dramani Mahama would make a comeback to run for and win a third term despite prior statements.

Are these what is informing the conviction of the NPP? Haven’t we, as a people, decided to put no store by the word of these prophets, to the point of even banning them from prophesying on New Year’s Eve?

Since when did Ghanaians resume trust in the word of our prophets? In July 2024, Rev. Kusi Boateng, founder of Power Chapel World Wide Church, prophesied that Dr Mahamudu Bawumia would be crowned President of Ghana in that year’s elections.

To loud applause, he even predicted the exact date on which the results would be declared. Both prophecies turned out false. Rev Kusi Boateng was the former Executive Secretary of the National Cathedral Board of Trustees.

Knowing some of our prophets the way Ghanaians do, it is surprising that anybody, let alone a political tradition, would doubt the word of the President (or any human being, for that matter) based on prophecies by “men of God” whom we all, as a nation, have agreed should be ignored because they are stomach-prophets.

My biggest surprise is that the NPP is concerned that Mahama would attempt a third term. If the word of the opposition is to be believed, and Mahama has performed so abysmally, then there should rather be joy in the NPP camp if he “threatens” to attempt a third term. Why? Because, against such “unimpressive” performance, even a mental patient in NPP colours should win against Mahama.

Third Matter Arising: Okudzeto Ablakwa versus Evacuees’ Palava.

The NPP and the Minority in Parliament have questioned the disbursement of the GH¢49.72 million spent to evacuate 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa between May 27 and September 4. Among others, there have been allegations that some evacuees received less than the announced GH¢5,500 support package.

At the centre of it all is the man better known to Ghanaians for his ORAL crusade.

For a man who won admiration for his pursuit of righteousness over National Cathedral contracts and expenditures, the allegations are surprising, if not shocking.

Some citizens are pointing out the obvious, that the Minority are pursuing an agenda against NDC who made life uncomfortable for them in government.

They have made no secret of their intention not only to pay the Foreign Minister, personally, back in his own coin, but also, as a grand agenda towards 2028, to employ all the tricks deployed by the NDC while in opposition to create disaffection for Akufo-Addo’s government.

I think that for Okudzeto Ablakwa, the way forward should be simple: be as transparent as possible with records regarding charter flight arrangements and expenditure.

Ghana News.title: Make vote-buying costly in party elections — Bernard Mornah
Ghana News.content:
The leader of the People's National Convention (PNC), Bernard Anbataayela Mornah, has called on political parties to make vote-buying costly, campaign financing transparent, and competence central to the selection of leaders.

He said that when access to political leadership depended on who could pay the most, competence and commitment to public service risked being displaced, weakening members' confidence that their choices mattered.

Mr Mornah, in a statement, said the response must cut across all parties, adding that appeals to conscience had to be backed by rules that parties were willing and able to enforce.

Ban on inducements

He proposed that party rules expressly prohibit cash, goods, mobile-money transfers and payments through agents meant to influence votes.

Candidates, he said, should be held accountable for inducements they authorised or knowingly financed through intermediaries, with responsibility established through evidence.

Spending limits

Mr Mornah called for realistic spending ceilings and a requirement that candidates declare donations, their sources and expenditure, including support in goods or services.

Independent checks should be arranged and accessible summaries published, he added, noting that the Ghana Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) had also called for comprehensive political finance reform.

Election day support

Parties should organise modest transport and refreshments centrally, with published costs and equal treatment, he said, to reduce the chances of inducements being disguised as transport allowances.

“Candidates should not give personal allowances to delegates,” he added.

Candidate forums

He proposed compulsory forums where contestants would explain their records, understanding of the office and practical plans.

Candidates should have equal access to members through official party platforms, he said, so that personal wealth did not determine whose message was heard.

Sanctions

Mr Mornah called for an impartial complaints panel, confidential reporting channels, clear evidence standards and fixed decision deadlines.

Proven breaches, he said, should attract proportionate sanctions, potentially including disqualification or annulment, under rules adopted in advance and subject to appeal.

Lower cost of contesting

He also proposed moderate nomination fees, shorter campaign periods and shared campaign platforms to help capable members without wealthy sponsors to compete.

Regular membership dues, transparent fundraising and stronger political education would also reduce dependence on wealthy patrons, he said.

PNC's next step

Mr Mornah said that before its next internal elections, the PNC should adopt clear safeguards through its appropriate decision-making bodies, appoint a credible enforcement committee and brief candidates and members on the rules.

Every candidate should submit a campaign finance declaration, and the party should publish a financial compliance report after the elections, he added.

He clarified that the measures were proposed reforms, not a statement that each was already required by Ghanaian law, and that any sanctions should be consistent with applicable law and party constitutions.

"Our parties must reward service, integrity and ability," he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
