● Check the product label . Look for clear directions, manufacturer information, batch details, and relevant expiry or period-after-opening information.

● Be cautious about exaggerated claims. Promises such as guaranteed hair growth in seven days or permanent removal of every dark spot are warning signs.

● Consider your climate. In humid weather conditions like Nigeria, lighter lotions and gels are ideal, as they are more comfortable. Dry skin or hair benefits from richer products. But your personal preference and response still matter.

● Buy from reputable sellers like ShopAnoint and ORIKI . The y are legit and sell original haircare and skincare products. Counterfeit or poorly stored products can pose safety risks to your health, so take your time to verify the brand when shopping online.

● Introduce products gradually. Patch-test new skincare products and avoid starting several strong active ingredients at the same time. If a product causes burning, swelling, or a persistent rash, stop using it.

Final Thoughts

The ultimate guide to African beauty begins with understanding that there is no single formula for beautiful skin or healthy hair. African botanical ingredients such as shea butter, peppermint, uziza, cloves, castor oils, black seeds, and noney offer exciting possibilities.

At the same time, African-founded brands like BuyORIKI and ShopAnoint continue to contribute to the continent’s growing beauty industry. Whether you are exploring moisturizing body creams, gentle cleansers, natural hair conditioners, or botanical oils, the best products are those that address your specific needs without causing irritation or unnecessary buildup.

World.title: EPL Roundup: Awoniyi fires Coventry to victory as Manchester club stumble
World.content:
Nigerian forward Taiwo Awoniyi scored his first Premier League goal for Coventry City on Saturday, helping the newly promoted side secure a 3-1 home victory over Sunderland.

Awoniyi struck in the 37th minute to give Coventry a two-goal advantage after Tatsuhiro Sakakibara had opened the scoring in the 17th minute.

Jack Rudoni extended the lead seven minutes into the second half before Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty in the 67th minute to reduce the deficit for Sunderland.

The Nigerian striker was substituted in the 72nd minute, while compatriot Frank Onyeka was not included in Coventry’s matchday squad.

The victory ended Coventry’s run of consecutive defeats and moved them two points clear of the relegation zone.

Elsewhere, Ola Aina featured for Nottingham Forest in their 2-0 defeat away to Brentford. The defender was substituted at half-time as Forest suffered another setback in their battle to move away from the bottom end of the table.

Semi Ajayi played the full 90 minutes for Hull City in their 2-2 draw against Ipswich Town. The Nigerian defender received a yellow card in the 89th minute.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

United’s struggles deepen after Chelsea defeat

Manchester United’s difficult campaign continued with a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, further increasing the pressure on manager Michael Carrick.

The visitors were reduced to 10 men after Lisandro Martinez received a second yellow card in the 64th minute for an elbow on Wesley Fofana.

Chelsea capitalised on their numerical advantage, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer scoring in the second half to secure the victory.

The result extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine matches, leaving them just one point above the relegation zone after nine league games.

Carrick admitted that the dismissal significantly affected his side’s chances.

“It has a major importance on the game,” he said. “A huge moment.”

Brighton stun Manchester City

Manchester City also suffered a disappointing afternoon, losing 1-0 at home to Brighton and Hove Albion.

Yasin Ayari scored the only goal in the 11th minute, punishing City’s defensive lapse from a dangerous cross.

The defeat was City’s second consecutive league loss, following their 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa. It also ended Erling Haaland’s scoring run of seven consecutive league matches.

Brighton, who lost to City on penalties in the Carabao Cup during the week, moved into third place on 19 points, two behind the leaders.

City remain top with 21 points, although Arsenal have an opportunity to draw level or move ahead when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

Nigerian youngster Zadok Yohanna, who recently returned to training, was not listed in Brighton’s squad.

Bournemouth maintain impressive run

Elsewhere, Bournemouth continued their strong start to the season with a 2-0 victory over Leeds United.

The win extended their run to six consecutive victories in all competitions without conceding a goal and lifted them to seventh place.

Meanwhile, Sunderland remained bottom after their defeat at Coventry, while Nottingham Forest stayed second from bottom following their loss at Brentford.

World.title: ‘Don’t equate me with God, election is over, ‘ Nigerian governor warns supporters, political associates
World.content:
Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has cautioned his supporters and political associates against excessive praise-singing and the use of grandiose political appellation in addressing him.

He urged them to address him simply as “Mr Governor,” maintaining that all praises and accolades belong to God Almighty and that no political leader should be accorded attributes reserved for God.

Mr Oyebanji gave the admonition on Friday evening at the October edition of the monthly Evening of Praise and Worship programme held at Lady Jibowu Hall, Government House, Ado-Ekiti.

He said the period of political campaigns and elections had ended, stressing that the state had entered a new phase focused on governance, service delivery and the fulfilment of promises to the people.

Emphasising the need to avoid elevating political leaders to a status comparable to God, the governor specifically disapproved of appellations such as “Jinx Breaker”, “Owi Bee, Se Bee”, “History Maker” and “Back to Back”, among others.

“I think we have to put an end to all these appellations. Election is over, and from today, just address me as Mr Governor. I don’t want to hear all these appellations such as ‘Jinx Breaker’, ‘History Maker’ and all the rest.

“I permitted them because it was an election season. Election is over now, a new government has been sworn in, and we are in the era of governance. Politics is over. I don’t want anybody to equate me with God or give me an appellation that is an attribute of God.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking further, Mr Oyebanji attributed the relative peace, stability and development recorded in Ekiti State, particularly over the last four years, to the grace of God.

He said the achievements of his administration and the peaceful atmosphere across the state were testimonies to God’s faithfulness and continued intervention in its affairs.

The governor expressed confidence that the same God who had guided the state thus far would continue to sustain it, urging residents to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in God for greater accomplishments.

“I love the theme of this month’s edition because this is the first evening of Praise and Worship since this new administration was inaugurated, and the theme is apt. We are just here to praise God, and I know that as we praise God on behalf of Ekiti State, He will speak to us and also step into our situation,” he said.

World.title: Mike Adenuga: Blurring the line between commerce and compassion, By Tayo Williams
World.content:
Through the foundation, whose core programme interests are entrepreneurship, education, health, and rural development, Adenuga creates and supports initiatives that deliver knowledge, skills, resources and infrastructure that will drive enterprise, facilitate commerce, stimulate innovation, and improve living conditions. The foundation also targets vulnerable groups, Internally Displaced Persons, disaster relief, and national health crises.

Earlier this year, Chairman Mike Adenuga (GCON), founder of Globacom Limited, a characteristically unobtrusive business titan, made a huge dent in the world of giving. Through his Globacom outfit, he donated ₦1 billion to the Lagos State Security Trust Fund to “strengthen security infrastructure” in Nigeria’s economic nerve-centre. Typically, he did not make a song and a dance of it. That is his nature. Giving, for Adenuga, is noiseless and without fanfare, but it will echo across generations.

Sometime in 2020, the entire world was in a dark place. The COVID-19 pandemic was ravaging the world. Global economies had shut down, while humans were dropping dead at the speed of light. The situation was equally grim in Nigeria. There was panic in the land. Moved by the gravity of the issue, Adenuga donated ₦1billion to support every effort of the federal government to combat the virus, particularly the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Private Sector Coalition against COVID-19.

He applauded the federal government’s measures to address the negative impact of the COVID-19 virus on the health, finance and other sectors of the economy, and the CBN for what he described as a commendable and worthwhile initiative that deserves the moral and financial support of all stakeholders of the private sector. The Globacom boss did not stop there.

He went on to donate ₦500 million to the Lagos State Government. In a letter to Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Adenuga affirmed his readiness to work with the state government in the various efforts to combat the pandemic, while reiterating his conglomerate’s willingness to assist various bodies and institutions in the country with the supply of such essential items as health PPEs and other requirements.

But it is through his Mike Adenuga Foundation that he touches humanity the most. The proudly Pan-African philanthropic foundation was established to help Nigeria and other African countries to achieve social and economic independence, while contributing to an improved future for Nigerians and other African citizens.

Through the foundation, whose core programme interests are entrepreneurship, education, health, and rural development, Adenuga creates and supports initiatives that deliver knowledge, skills, resources and infrastructure that will drive enterprise, facilitate commerce, stimulate innovation, and improve living conditions. The foundation also targets vulnerable groups, Internally Displaced Persons, disaster relief, and national health crises.

Nigerian entertainers may well be the greatest beneficiaries of Adenuga’s large heart. Since 2003, when it began operations, Globacom has made Nigerian stars the faces (ambassadors) of its brand, while making them worth their popularity in affluence and influence. At a time when entertainers were being paid peanuts for their artistry, Globacom started dishing out millions of naira to its ambassadors, and helping them to live the life they only fantasised about.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Aside from direct financial commitments including massive sponsorships, Globacom still retains a large number of key players in the entertainment industry, and they have been blessed immeasurably by this patronage.

Popularly known as the ‘Spirit of Africa’ because of his vast business empire traversing telecommunications, banking, oil and gas, and real estate among others, Chairman Adenuga became a national sensation when Globacom entered the Nigerian telecommunications field back in 2003. He promised to build a truly Nigerian brand that would make life easier for Nigerians, and he proved it in no time.

Globacom made history as the first telecommunications network to introduce per-second billing at a time Nigerians had been told that it was an impossibility. Consequently, this began the revolution that made mobile telephony not just an exclusive preserve of the privileged and well-heeled, but a necessity for Nigerians of all ages from the North to the South and everywhere in between.

From its early days, Globacom had always defied market odds to delight Nigerians. The company launched a slew of futuristic products and services, such as being the first to offer 2.5G when others were on 2G, MMS, international SMS connectivity to over 804 networks in 174 countries, BlackBerry solutions, international prepaid roaming, voice SMS, personal ringback tunes, and Magicplus.

Globacom soon became the fastest-growing telecommunications company in Africa, with an active subscriber base of over 23.68 million (as of June 2026) and a vast network of already laid fibre criss-crossing all parts of Nigeria and a submarine cable that runs from the United States of America to Lagos through the United Kingdom and 17 other European and African countries.

Before Globacom, he had founded and developed Devcom Bank and Equitorial Trust Bank into highly profitable companies that played active pioneering roles in developing the public, commercial and retail sectors of the economy. Later, the two companies were consolidated into Equitorial Trust Bank, which later merged with Sterling Bank Plc, with Dr Adenuga as the largest shareholder of the newer bank.

He owns a 25.1 per cent stake in construction giant, Julius Berger, through Goldstones Estates Limited and also owns 74.4 per cent of Conoil, one of Nigeria’s largest petroleum marketing businesses, through Conpetro Limited.

Conoil was the first indigenous company in Nigeria to explore, discover and produce oil in large commercial quantities, with the fastest on-stream production activity from licence award to the first production in only nine months. Aside from operating six oil blocks in the Niger Delta, Conoil is also the market leader in aviation fuels.

Since his emergence on the socio-economic radar of Nigeria many decades ago, Adenuga has steadily blurred the line between commerce and compassion. He has alchemised his economic successes into great philanthropy, touching and turning lives around across Nigeria and beyond. It is safe to say that philanthropy is at the heart of everything that the business titan does.

It is no surprise, therefore, that he holds Nigeria’s highest honour for a non-government official, the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON); Ghana’s highest civilian national honour, the Companion of the Star of Ghana (CSG); and France’s highest national honour of Commander of the Legion of Honour (Chevalier de la Legion d Honneur).

These titles are a fitting tribute to a man who has redefined the art of giving, made it a public sacrament, and shown clearly that he is not just about making money but making it available as resources for advancing the lot of humanity.

Tayo Williams is a Lagos-based media practitioner and public affairs analyst.

World.title: Caring Africa urges nationwide implementation of national care policy
World.content:
Caring Africa has urged the federal and state governments to begin implementing Nigeria’s newly approved National Care Policy and Implementation Plan, 2026-2030.

The organisation, which served as a technical partner to the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in developing the policy, said its approval is only the beginning of efforts to establish a national system for childcare, elderly care and other forms of paid and unpaid care.

The Federal Executive Council, presided over by President Bola Tinubu, approved the policy on Wednesday alongside the National Action Plan on Ending Violence Against Children and the National Policy on Menstrual Health and Hygiene Management, 2026-2030.

The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, announced the approvals at a press briefing in Abuja on Thursday to mark the 26th anniversary of United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 on Women, Peace and Security.

According to the ministry, the National Care Policy recognises unpaid care work, promotes regulated childcare and elderly care services, sets minimum standards for care centres and provides for a National Care Fund.

States’ adoption of policy

Blessing Adesiyan, founder and Chief Care Officer of Caring Africa, said the next stage should be to domesticate the policy across Nigeria.

Ms Adesiyan said care services such as health, education and social welfare are delivered substantially at state level, making adoption of the policy by the 36 states important to its implementation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“A federal policy that stays in Abuja will not change anything for a woman looking for childcare in Oshodi or caring for her mother in Sokoto,” she said.

Ms Adesiyan called for the policy to be taken across the six geopolitical zones and adopted by the states.

Nigeria joins countries that have adopted national care policies. Brazil enacted its National Care Policy in 2024, followed by a funded national plan, while Chile signed its Chile Cuida care system into law in 2026.

Kenya has also launched a national care policy and is implementing it at county level, while UN Women supports more than 50 countries in developing national care systems.

What the policy provides

The policy is built around 11 pillars covering unpaid care work, care infrastructure, maternal and newborn care, childcare, ageing and elderly care, disability care, the care workforce, regulation of the care economy, care financing and employer-supported care.

Under the childcare component, the framework provides for a tiered licensing system for childcare facilities, minimum standards on space, staff ratios, safety, hygiene and nutrition, as well as a national register for childcare workers.

It also proposes a pathway for informal crèches to meet regulatory requirements rather than simply being excluded from the system.

For care workers, the policy proposes defining care work as a formal occupation under Nigerian labour law, with training and certification pathways and a national caregiver database. It also proposes a minimum wage floor for care workers, health insurance and pension access.

The framework also proposes a dedicated care line in the federal budget and a National Care Fund to pool public, corporate and development financing for care services.

Burden of unpaid care

Caring Africa cited data showing that women and girls perform about 80 per cent of unpaid care work in Nigeria, including childcare, cooking, cleaning and caring for sick or elderly relatives.

The organisation also cited estimates that Nigerian women spend about 4.3 hours a day on unpaid care work, compared with 1.12 hours for men.

It said only about five per cent of Nigerian children aged zero to two are enrolled in licensed childcare.

The National Bureau of Statistics estimates that formalising the care economy could create 17 million jobs, while research by Economist Impact indicates that accessible and quality childcare could enable 1.7 million more Nigerian mothers to enter the workforce by 2030.

Ms Adesiyan said the policy would also provide a framework for employers to support workers with caregiving responsibilities through measures such as paid leave and employer-supported care.

She said the policy’s provisions on maternal and newborn care would extend support into the postpartum period, while its broader framework covers ageing, disability and care within households.

“The stress of sustained caregiving carries a real physical health cost, which we rarely count. This policy is the first instrument we have that touches it,” she noted.

World.title: Lagos BRT passengers endure hours in traffic as motorists take over dedicated lane
World.content:
Passengers travelling on Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) buses along Ikorodu Road in Lagos spent hours in traffic on Friday and Saturday as private and commercial vehicles used the lanes reserved for the buses.

Some passengers who had waited in queues at the terminals before boarding found themselves stuck in traffic for hours, defeating the purpose of using the BRT service to avoid congestion.

This reporter boarded a BRT bus at the Ikorodu terminal at about 11 a.m. on Friday, heading towards Fadeyi, but the bus did not reach Palmgrove until about 2 p.m.

PREMIUM TIMES observed heavy traffic from Agric through Owode, Ogolonto and M12 towards Ketu, with private and commercial vehicles occupying the BRT corridor and impeding the movement of buses.

Some passengers who boarded buses at the Ikorodu terminal at about 10:15 a.m. were still around Ogolonto by 11:24 a.m.

The situation was worse on Saturday, when both lanes serving inward and outward traffic along the Ikorodu corridor were heavily congested, leaving BRT buses unable to move freely.

PREMIUM TIMES also observed police officers attached to the Owutu Police Division assisting private motorists seeking access to the BRT lane.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

No LASTMA officials were seen enforcing the restrictions on the use of the dedicated lane during the period observed.

The BRT corridor is meant to give public transport buses priority over other vehicles and reduce travel time for commuters. However, the unauthorised use of the lane appeared to have undermined that purpose during the two days.

In a recent statement, the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) reiterated that the lane was reserved for designated BRT buses and other vehicles authorised by the agency.

The statement, issued by LAMATA’s Head of Corporate Communication, Kolawole Ojelabi, identified private vehicles, some military and paramilitary vehicles, and local government buses among those not permitted to use the corridor.

“The only exceptions to this rule are emergency response vehicles such as fire trucks and ambulances, and only when responding to emergencies,” the agency said.

LAMATA said the unauthorised use of the lane disrupted bus operations, contributed to traffic congestion and endangered passengers and other road users.

The agency warned that the regulations remained in force and that offenders could be apprehended and prosecuted under Lagos traffic laws, regardless of their status or affiliation.

It said penalties could include fines, vehicle impoundment and other legal sanctions.

LAMATA urged motorists, security agencies and government bodies to comply with the rules governing the BRT corridor.

Mr Ojelabi told PREMIUM TIMES via text message that the regulations governing the BRT lane clearly specified the vehicles permitted to use it.

He said an enforcement squad under the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation had been deployed to ensure compliance.

“We are working with traditional rulers and law enforcement agencies to ensure compliance, and the media to appeal to road users to obey the law,” Mr Ojelabi added.

The BRT lane is a dedicated roadway or traffic lane reserved exclusively for high-capacity public buses, allowing them to bypass regular traffic congestion. The buses are run under a public private partnership between the Lagos State Government and franchise operators.

The first BRT system and lane in Lagos was officially introduced and opened on 17 March 2008.

World.title: Gov. Lawal presents staff of office, vehicles to 19 Zamfara emirs
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal has presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 emirs in Zamfara State.

The coronation and presentation ceremony took place at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital.

Dignitaries in attendance included His Eminence the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe, and the Emir of Gwandu.

After their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first-class emirs and eight second-class emirs.

Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC Ultra SUV (2025/2026 model), a Mikano ZNA Hilux vehicle and an EV Antique Model car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities.

In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability and development.

He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively.

He said, “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the State.

“It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity, and compassion.

“I expect every emir to carry out their responsibilities without discrimination, uphold justice, and ensure that the traditional institution remains accessible to all members of the community.

“Our people must find guidance, fairness, and reassurance in their traditional rulers.

“Recognising the importance of royal palaces as centres of traditional authority and community engagement, I reaffirm our commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces.

“This is part of our broader effort to strengthen these institutions and improve the conditions in which traditional rulers carry out their responsibilities.

“We are also providing official vehicles to the 19 emirs. These include GAC ULTRA SUVs (2025/2026 models), MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicles, and EV ANTIQUE MODEL cars (DDP).

“This provision is intended to facilitate travel across your respective emirates, encourage closer engagement with your communities, and improve coordination with government institutions.

“I expect these vehicles to be properly maintained and used responsibly in support of your official duties.”

The governor also urged the royal fathers to build a productive partnership between their emirates and the state government.

Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain fully loyal to the authority. He also encouraged them to respect and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution as they discharge their duties.

World.title: Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, Omoyele Sowore, and members of his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital.

In a statement on Saturday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday, said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off.

It partly reads, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti.

“The suspects are Joseph Tayo ’32yrs’, Olatunji Abayomi ’41yrs’, Isaac Amba ’22yrs’, Kehinde Ajigbana ’18yrs’, Tosin David ’18yrs’, Solomon Iyanu ’18yrs’, Ogunsola Ayomide ’21yrs’, Ojo Ayodeji ’22yrs’, Kayode Dada ’32yrs’, Segun Olatunji ’28yrs’ and Salami Emmanuel ’53yrs’.

“Items recovered include two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, one pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards, thirteen mobile phones, two vehicle keys, one flash drive, one 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, one gas lighter and ₦250.”

The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the individual roles of the suspects and determine their possible connections with the attack.

The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice.

The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.”

Reacting to the arrests, Sowore demanded that the alleged masterminds and sponsors of the attack be identified and brought to justice, insisting that the incident was a coordinated assault and not an ordinary altercation.

The presidential candidate made the demand in a post on X on Saturday, describing the arrests as an admission that the incident was a violent attack.

He also alleged that some of the attackers were associated with the City Boys group and called for investigations into possible links between the incident and officials of the state government.

Sowore urged the Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, and the Department of State Services to preserve and release CCTV footage from the scene to help identify those involved.

“Arresting 11 suspects is not enough if those who planned, financed, coordinated and facilitated the attack remain untouched,” he wrote.

He also demanded an explanation from the police over their initial description of the incident as an altercation.

World.title: 2027: ‘Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu’ – South-East govs tell Igbo
World.content:
Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu.

The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo.

Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms.

He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms.

The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections.

“A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said.

Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process.

Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours.

He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income.

According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance.

“When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said.

He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities.

Uzodimma

Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East.

He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu.

He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East.

“We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said.

The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the Federal Government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development.

“We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said.

Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers.

In his remarks, Nwifuru commended the skills acquisition and empowerment initiatives of the APC-led administration, urging South-East women to vote massively for the party.

He described the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development.

The governor dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC.

He urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the January 2027 elections and subsequent polls.

Soludo

Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements.

He said the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the Federal Government.

Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, stressing the need for the region to strengthen its political alliances.

He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet.

He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC).

He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges.

Vanguard News

World.title: Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community
World.content:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

The Kebbi State Police Command has said that it is aware of the security incident in Ribah, Zuru Local Government Area, on 30th October 2026, when suspected bandits launched two successive attacks on the community.

Police image maker, in a statement on Saturday, revealed that the first incident occurred at about 7:25 pm, when the assailants attempted to block Rambo Junction along the Ribah–Dirin Daji Road under Zuru emirate, as their attempt was promptly foiled by the joint security forces comprising the police, military and local vigilante group, who engaged them in a gun duel and dispersed them.

The statement added that the attackers later regrouped and returned, shooting sporadically from different directions within the town.

However, during the ensuing exchange, one Hassan Boder, aged 47, a security guard at a newly constructed filling station along Ribah–Kanya Road, was fatally hit by a bullet. Upon receipt of a distress call, the joint security team swiftly mobilised, engaged the attackers and successfully repelled them.

Usman explained that security operations have since been intensified, with aggressive patrols ongoing to dominate the area and efforts underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators.

“Yes, we are aware of the attack and we have repelled it by forcing the terrorists to retreat due to superior firepower. The combined security forces have dominated the area to prevent further attacks on the communities,” he said.

World.title: Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France
World.content:
A protester stands next to a street fire during nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students, in Nantes, western France on October 31, 2026. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by ALAIN JOCARD / AFP)

Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and elsewhere on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched across France against soaring living costs and police violence, with some demonstrators dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween.

While the third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests was largely peaceful, tensions erupted in several cities later Saturday.

After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination.

Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges.

“A hard core

of several hundred rioters” at the rear of the march attacked police with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail, the police prefecture said. Officers were seeking “to restore public order”, it added.

In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene.

In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators.

– ‘Dressed up as angry citizen’ –

Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead.

Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.”

A protester wearing a Marie-Antoinette costume (L) holds a placard reading “Give them brioche” flanked by a protester dressed as a wizard holding a placard reading “A potion for the revolution” during a demonstration in Lyon, central-eastern France on October 31, 2026, part of nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP)

“We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice,” said Camille Guerin, 31, a demonstrator in the western city of Nantes.

Authorities said that some 320,000 people rallied across France including 70,000 in Paris.

According to youth organisations, nearly half a million people demonstrated across the country, including 200,000 in Paris.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday that police had prepared for street violence on a scale “comparable” to the unrest two weeks ago, when shops were looted and public buildings set ablaze.

Between 400 and 800 hard-left activists were expected in Paris, said an informed source.

– Elections looming –

The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen topping opinion polls.

The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.

Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.

Similar youth-led demonstrations have been seen across Europe in recent weeks.

Thousands of young Germans took to the streets nationwide on Saturday.

In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest.

“I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits,” she said.

“Struggle is classy, it needs to come back into fashion.”

– New school blockades –

Student protesters complained the police did not authorise a march through the centre of the French capital and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week.

“Starting this Tuesday, we will blockade our universities and high schools, and we will do so again on Thursday before joining the demonstration on November 5 called by workers and trade unions,” said Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union).

Ahead of the protests, some shopkeepers barricaded their businesses.

In eastern Paris, Wael Boubaker, a cafe employee, covered a storefront with plywood panels.

“Everyone is staying home. No one is going to come and buy anything,” Boubaker said.

Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who accused Macron’s government of “taking an increasingly authoritarian turn”, joined the march in Paris.

With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending.

Nunez said authorities had detected social media calls for Halloween gatherings on Saturday evening that urged protesters to spark a “revolution”.

World.title: US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio
World.content:
Marco Rubio

US President Donald Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday.

“We can achieve military objectives if we seek to,” Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting.

But Rubio added that Trump “hasn’t made a decision” on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday.

“I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said.

While he slammed Tehran for “actively and openly” targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump’s preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran.

But he did not commit to a timeline for talks.

“I’m not going to characterize neither the progress on those talks nor any timeframe on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” Rubio said.

Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections.

Trump earlier warned of the potential for fresh military action after US midterms, saying previously that he was weighing up whether to “finish them off.”

But any further attack would spark concern among US allies.

On Thursday, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP: “We are calling for a diplomatic solution, and really, escalation does not benefit anyone.”

AFP

World.title: EPL: Brighton stun Man City, 10-man Man Utd beaten by Chelsea
World.content:
Brighton’s French midfielder #10 Georginio Rutter is put under pressure by Manchester City’s Portuguese midfielder #27 Matheus Nunes (L) and Manchester City’s English midfielder #05 Elliot Anderson (R) during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)

Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday, while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea.

Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first ever away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title.

The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials.

Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday.

Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead.

Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time.

But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side-netting late on.

Players celebrate following the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)

City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola.

However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight.

Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday.

– Man Utd self-implode –

Manchester United’s nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period.

Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring.

Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty.

Chelsea’s English midfielder #10 Cole Palmer (L) vies with Manchester United’s Brazilian striker #10 Matheus Cunha (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four.

“The two halves of football couldn’t probably be further apart,” said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma.

“We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half.”

Only Nottingham Forest’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford ensured United did not drop into the bottom three.

Nikola Milenkovic’s own goal and Igor Thiago’s strike took the Bees up to sixth.

Bournemouth extended their fine form with a 2-0 win over Leeds thanks to goals from Evanilson and Amine Adli.

Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Coventry.

Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw.

kca/nf

World.title: US Court denies discovery request against Tinubu, DCI group in FOIA litigation
World.content:
Tinubu

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA –The United States District Court for the District of Columbia has denied a motion by Aaron Greenspan seeking limited discovery from Nigerian President Bola Tinubu and DCI Group in ongoing litigation under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).

Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, in a post on his X account stated that in its October 30 ruling, the Court determined that the proposed discovery concerning alleged cyberattacks on Greenspan’s website was not sufficiently relevant to the underlying FOIA dispute involving the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).

“The Court’s decision makes clear that this Freedom of Information Act proceeding cannot be used to pursue discovery unrelated to the legal questions before it,” said attorney Christopher W. Carmichael.

“By denying the request for discovery against President Tinubu and DCI Group, the Court reinforced the importance of keeping this litigation focused on the issues properly before it.”

According to him, the Court also denied a separate motion by nonparty Karl Von Batten seeking permission to file an amicus curiae (friend-of-the-court) brief, as well as Greenspan’s related request for judicial notice.

Additionally, the Court denied Greenspan’s motion for summary judgment.

“The Court also denied the plaintiff’s motion for summary judgment and rejected a separate request to introduce an amicus brief,” said Attorney Oluwole Afolabi.

“While the underlying FOIA issues remain before the Court, these rulings establish important procedural boundaries and clarify which matters are appropriate for consideration in this litigation.”

World.title: SULTAN MUHAMMAD MACCIDO: 20 YEARS ON
World.content:
HALILU MACCIDO pays tribute to his father Muhammad Maccido, former Sultan of Sokoto who died in the ill-fated ADC Airlines crash of 2006

Twenty years have passed since the tragic day we lost a remarkable father, a revered traditional ruler, a distinguished statesman and a guiding light. Yet two decades on, the memory of His Eminence Sultan Muhammad Maccido remains as vivid in our hearts as ever. Time has moved on, but the love, admiration and respect we hold for him have not diminished.

To us, his children and family, he was a loving and devoted father whose wisdom, guidance and prayers remain an enduring source of strength. To the Sultanate, he was a custodian of tradition and a symbol of dignity. To the nation, he was a father figure whose life was defined by humility, faith, service and an unwavering commitment to peace, unity and the well-being of others.

Baba lived a life of purpose. He led with wisdom, carried his responsibilities with humility, and touched countless lives through his kindness, generosity and sense of duty. His leadership went beyond the throne. It showed in his character, in his devotion to his people, and in his belief in peace, justice and mutual understanding.

Though his time with us was cut short, the legacy he left continues to speak long after his passing.

His life reminds us that true greatness is measured not by the position one holds, but by the lives one touches, the values one upholds and the difference one makes in the world.

Baba, 20 years without you have taught us that while a father may depart this world, his influence never dies. We miss your presence, cherish your counsel and hold dear the lessons you instilled in us. We wish you were here to see the years pass, to offer your wisdom and to guide us with the quiet strength and dignity that were uniquely yours.

Today we remember you not only with tears and longing, but with immense gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of being your children. Your life was a blessing, your guidance a gift, and your legacy is a responsibility we must continue to honour.

As we mark 20 years since your return to your Creator, we pray that Allah (SWT) envelop you in His infinite mercy, forgive your shortcomings, illuminate your grave, reward your good deeds abundantly and grant you Jannatul Firdaus al-A’la. May He accept your service to humanity as Sadaqatul Jariyah and reunite us with you in Jannah. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

May your noble legacy continue to live through us and through all whose lives you touched.

Your memory remains a blessing, your legacy an inspiration, and your place in our hearts irreplaceable. Rest in eternal peace, Baba.

. Halilu Maccido is the son of the late 19th Sultan of Sokoto

World.title: Uwaleke Seeks Credible Delivery Framework for New Capital Market Master Plan
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

Renowned professor of capital market, Uche Uwaleke, has underscored the need for the newly launched Nigeria Capital Market Master Plan (NCMMP 2.0) to be accompanied by a credible delivery framework that establishes measurable annual milestones, provides for regular independent evaluation and makes it possible to distinguish between completed activities and reforms that have produced tangible economic outcomes.

The NCMMP 2.0 (2026-2036), which was launched in Abuja recently by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, is a roadmap designed to expand Nigeria’s capital market from about N250 trillion to N750 trillion by 2036.

In an article titled ‘NCMMP 2.0: The Gaps in National Alignment and Inclusive Consultation,’ which he made available to THISDAY, Uwaleke described the Master Plan as a commendable and ambitious undertaking that deserves recognition.

He said: “The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the sponsors, FSD Africa and the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), and the consortium of consultants led by Genesis Analytics and Bourse Consult deserve commendation for investing the expertise, resources and collaborative effort required to articulate a strategic vision for Nigeria’s capital market over the next decade.

“The aspiration to build a diverse, efficient, transparent and innovative capital market that positions Nigeria as a regional financial hub and mobilizes the capital needed to drive wealth creation and a US$1 trillion economy by 2030 is quite compelling. There is every reason to be confident that the plan can make a meaningful contribution to Nigeria’s economic transformation.

“However, the success of a masterplan of this magnitude will depend not only on its aspirations and proposed reforms, but also on the realism of its time horizon, its alignment with national development priorities, the inclusiveness of its formulation and the strength of the institutional arrangements for its implementation.”

Uwaleke, who is the Director of the Institute of Capital Market Studies, Nasarawa State University, Keffi, observed that one fundamental question was whether a 10-year implementation horizon, spanning 2026-2036, is the most appropriate framework for the NCMMP 2.0.

He argued that while a long-term vision was necessary for transforming a capital market, the implementation programme must be anchored in a timeframe that is sufficiently realistic, measurable and aligned with the country’s prevailing economic policy framework.

“In this respect, Malaysia’s Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030, launched on 9th March 2026, offers a useful model. Malaysia has adopted a five-year implementation horizon within a broader 20-year vision extending to 2045.

“This approach distinguishes between the long-term destination and the medium-term actions required to get there. It allows policymakers and market participants to translate strategic ambitions into specific, time-bound priorities, assess progress against measurable milestones and recalibrate interventions in response to changing economic conditions without losing sight of the overarching vision. Nigeria would have benefited from a similar architecture,” he said.

According to him, Nigeria already has a National Development Plan for 2026-2030, situated within the longer-term Nigeria Agenda 2050, adding that a capital market masterplan covering 2026-2030 would therefore have provided a natural and coherent framework for aligning capital market reforms with national economic priorities, while preserving a longer-term perspective towards 2050.

He explained that it was not merely a question of administrative convenience or the choice of a more convenient planning cycle, but goes without saying that the capital market does not operate in an economic or policy vacuum.

“Its development is profoundly influenced by macroeconomic stability, fiscal and monetary policy, the investment climate, public-sector borrowing, pension and insurance regulations, infrastructure development and the government’s broader economic priorities.

“The market can mobilise capital, facilitate investment, deepen financial inclusion and support enterprise growth, but it cannot independently overcome policy constraints that lie beyond its institutional reach. indeed, the NCMMP 2.0 document itself provides a compelling reason to take this alignment seriously.

“It acknowledges that the first Capital Market Master Plan, covering 2015-2025, achieved only 63 per cent of its planned activities, with just two of its 21 macro-objectives fully achieved by the end of 2025, while the remaining 19 were at varying stages of execution.

“A revised masterplan was subsequently developed in 2021 to reflect market realities, while the absence of alignment with Nigeria’s national development blueprints weakened broader buy-in from policymakers.

“These are significant lessons. They suggest that ambitious targets and extensive stakeholder engagement, however valuable, cannot substitute for a planning framework that is integrated with the national policy environment and commands sustained political and institutional ownership. It would therefore have been prudent to make the NCMMP 2.0 a medium-term implementation plan for 2026-2030, explicitly aligned with the National Development Plan for the same period, within a longer-term capital market vision extending to 2050.

“Such an arrangement would have offered a more direct connection between capital market reforms and national economic objectives, made it easier to assign responsibilities to relevant government institutions, and strengthened accountability for delivery.

“It would also have provided a natural opportunity for a comprehensive review at the end of 2030, when the next phase could be developed in light of the country’s economic performance, policy direction and progress in capital market development,” he said, stressing that a 10-year plan is not inherently inappropriate.

Its effectiveness, he observed, depends on how well its implementation cycle is integrated with the national planning system.

He noted that the concern, therefore, was not the ambition of the NCMMP 2.0, but the risk of creating another planning horizon that may not adequately correspond with the policy framework upon which its success depends.

“The second issue concerns the breadth and inclusiveness of the stakeholder consultation undertaken in developing the masterplan,” he pointed out.

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

World.title: Victoria Volta Takes Cue from Onyeka Onwenu, Eyes Film Production
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Nollywood actress Victoria Volta, formerly known professionally as Victoria Nwogu, is looking to expand her involvement in filmmaking, with ambitions to move beyond acting and take on greater responsibilities in film production.

Having gained experience in front of and behind the camera, Volta hopes to work with established filmmakers and contribute more directly to the development of stories for the screen.

One of the projects that has shaped her experience is ‘Ije Awele’, in which she played the lead character, Awele, while also participating in the production. The film featured the late Nigerian entertainer Onyeka Onwenu.

Onwenu’s career spanned broadcasting, music, acting and public advocacy, establishing her as a prominent figure across different areas of Nigerian cultural life. For Volta, the opportunity to work on the same production with her was particularly inspiring.

“Onyeka represented so much to me: music, film, television, advocacy and Nigerian culture. Being on a project with her is something I will always value.

“I’ve always been interested in people. Why they behave the way they do, what shapes them and what happens beneath the surface. I think that’s part of what drew me to acting,” she said.

She studied Political and Administrative Studies before pursuing acting more deliberately and subsequently undertook film training, gaining experience in both performance and production.

“For me, acting cannot just be about looking good on camera or saying the right lines. I want to be able to enter a character’s world and make people feel something.”

Beyond acting, Volta hopes to secure more substantial roles, deepen her experience in production and work with established filmmakers. She also has ambitions to take her work to audiences beyond Nigeria.

Her career has since seen a change in branding. Her adoption of Victoria Volta as her professional name, she explained, reflects her present identity and creative direction.

“Victoria Nwogu will always be part of my story. Victoria Volta represents where I am now and where I’m going. I wanted something that felt energetic and memorable, something that reflected growth and movement. I know I’m still becoming, and I’m actually okay with that,” she concluded.

World.title: Breaking: Two Suspected Cases of Ebola Reported in North East, Says NCDC
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said two suspected cases of Ebola disease had been identified in Nigeria’s North-East region.

An update by the Centre on Saturday said both individuals had been isolated, while contact identification and listing was ongoing, and laboratory testing was being conducted.

However, being classified as suspected cases does not mean they are confirmed Ebola cases; confirmation is subject to laboratory results.

The Centre advised the general public to adhere strictly to safe practices including, maintaining good hand hygiene, enhanced sanitation and to follow guidance from public health authorities.

NCDC said further updates will be provided as verified information becomes available.

World.title: Ikogosi Marathon 2026: Plateau Athletes Set Pace in 17.5km Race, Competition Eyes Global Recognition
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Athletes from Plateau State on Saturday stamped their authority on the Ikogosi Marathon 2026 17.5km Race, emerging as the dominant force in the elite category as the competition continued its steady march towards international recognition.

The Plateau contingent produced a remarkable one-two finish, with Gyang James crossing the finish line first in 57 minutes, while his brother, Francis James, followed closely in 58 minutes to claim the second position. Rochas Sunday completed the podium after finishing third in 59 minutes.

The marathon, which began in Ilawe-Ekiti and ended at the iconic Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort in Ikogosi-Ekiti, attracted elite athletes from across Nigeria and foreign participants from Kenya and Ethiopia, with runners drawn from 28 states of the federation.

The event was attended by prominent dignitaries, including former Governor of Ekiti State, Chief Segun Oni; former presidential aide, Senator Babafemi Ojudu; Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye; Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism (NIHOTOUR), Dr Abisoye Fagade; Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Student Engagement, Sunday Asefon, among others.

Beyond the competition, the 2026 edition of the Ikogosi Marathon reflected the growing ambition of the organisers to transform the race into a globally recognised sporting platform capable of promoting athletics, tourism and youth development in Ekiti State.

In the female elite category, Teyei Davou emerged winner, followed by Tanko Nvou in second position and Vivian Obadiah in third.

For the indigenous female category, Arinde Miracle, Bako Gift and Ademisoye Adesewa took the first, second and third positions respectively, while Adeyemi Tunde, Adetiba Abiodun and Sunday Emmanuel emerged the top three finishers in the indigenous male category.

Speaking on the significance of the event, the Convener of the Ikogosi Marathon Initiative, Makinde Araoye, said the fourth edition marked a major milestone, recording about 14,000 registrations and attracting participation beyond Nigeria.

Araoye said the marathon was established not only as a sporting competition but also as a vehicle for tourism promotion, economic development and talent discovery.

He disclosed that the initiative had identified 10 promising indigenous athletes from Ekiti State who would receive financial rewards and further support aimed at preparing them for international competitions.

According to him, the elite category winners received N5 million, N4 million and N2.5 million for first, second and third positions respectively, while the indigenous category was created to encourage and nurture home-grown talents.

Araoye, however, called for greater support from corporate organisations operating in the state, urging them to embrace the competition as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR).

He expressed optimism that the 2027 edition would be upgraded into a full international marathon, attracting more foreign athletes and creating greater opportunities for Nigerian long-distance runners.

“Our vision is to position Ikogosi Marathon as an international event that will expose Nigerian athletes to global competition. We want to create a platform where talents discovered here can compete and succeed internationally,” he said.

Also speaking, Sunday Asefon described the marathon as a strategic platform for youth empowerment, talent discovery and national unity.

Asefon urged the Ekiti State Government and relevant stakeholders to invest in the indigenous athletes discovered through the competition, noting that sustained support could help them become internationally competitive.

For the champion, Gyang James, the victory was a reward for determination and improved preparation after he finished fourth in the previous edition.

James said his earlier disappointment motivated him to intensify training, adding that the Ikogosi Marathon had become an important avenue for Nigerian athletes to pursue their dreams and gain exposure.

World.title: Brown Chieftaincy House Launches N400m Trust for Widows, Indigent Students
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Abobo Brown Chieftaincy House in Finima, Bonny Local Government Area of Rivers State, has launched a N400 million humanitarian trust to sustain the philanthropic legacy of Aseme-Alabo Abinye Owen Brown and expand support for widows, indigent students and other vulnerable members of the community.

The Chief Abinye Owen Brown Excellence and Legacy Trust were unveiled during a ceremony marking the traditional leader’s birthday, with organisers describing the initiative as a deliberate effort to institutionalise his two decades of humanitarian service and ensure its sustainability for generations.

The trust will focus on education, youth empowerment and humanitarian assistance through two major programmes: the Widows Support Scheme and the Students Educational Support Scheme.

Speaking at the event, Chairman of the Planning Committee, Boma Kuronye, said the initiative was designed to immortalise Brown’s values while recognising his contributions to the welfare of the people.

“We are gathered not to mourn but to honour a living legend in his lifetime. We are gathered to institutionalise the values of a man who is still with us, still guiding us, and still serving Finima,” he said.

Kuronye described Brown as a traditional leader whose commitment to humanity transcended titles and positions.

“Aseme-Alabo Abinye Owen Brown has taught us that true greatness is not in titles but in how many burdens you lift for others. For decades, he has been a father to many, a counsellor to the House, and a quiet pillar for widows and students in Finima,” he said.

The Widows Support Scheme is also designed to improve the livelihoods of widows and restore their dignity, while the Students Educational Support Scheme will provide assistance to indigent students to ensure that financial difficulties do not deny them access to education.

According to the planning committee, the establishment of the trust marks a transition from individual acts of generosity to a structured institution capable of delivering consistent and long-term humanitarian interventions.

A citation presented in Brown’s honour described him as a respected custodian of Ibani culture and tradition, a bridge-builder and a humanist whose contributions to Finima and Grand Bonny extend beyond philanthropy.

It also acknowledged his role in promoting reconciliation, preserving the community’s history and defending its territorial integrity.

Beyond his traditional responsibilities, Brown has earned recognition for supporting widows and sponsoring indigent students, often without seeking public attention.

The citation highlighted his belief that “education is the only inheritance that cannot be stolen,” while stressing that the strength of a community could also be measured by how it treats its widows.

The ceremony attracted members of the Abobo Brown Chieftaincy House, traditional rulers, youth representatives, women’s groups, beneficiaries and other stakeholders.

The organisers said the trust was established during Brown’s lifetime to enable him to witness the impact of his humanitarian vision.

They expressed optimism that the initiative would expand educational opportunities, improve the welfare of vulnerable households and provide a sustainable framework for community development in Finima and beyond.

World.title: Edo Community Pleads with Okpebholo for Reversal of Clan Head Removal
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

Concerned Indigenes of Ikpeshi/Egbigere Clan in Akoko-Edo Local Government Area of Edo State have appealed to Governor Monday Okpebholo to reverse the removal of Regent Nicholas Saliu Odamah III and the reinstatement of Lukeman Momodu Odamah III, as the traditional ruler of the clan.

It would be recalled that Governor Okpebholo had on November 13, 2025, in a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government, Umar Musa Ikhilor, removed Lukeman Momodu and appointed Nicholas Odamah as regent pending the determination of the rightful occupant of the throne.

The state government, however, removed the regent in a statement issued by Secretary to the State Government on October 20, 2026, and reinstated Lukeman Momodu Odamah.

The government explained that the decision was taken in the interest of peace, stability and due process, and after reviewing appeals from Akoko-Edo indigenes and confirmed that the chieftaincy dispute was already before a court of competent jurisdiction.

But the group coordinator, Ms Peggy Agbo, in a news conference, made the appeal on behalf of the indigenes in Benin City.

She expressed concern that the state government’s decision could threaten the peace and stability currently enjoyed in the community

She said the community had experienced relative peace during the 11 months of Nicholas Odamah’s regency before he was removed, warning that the decision could heighten tensions if not urgently reviewed.

According to her, the group had also submitted a written objection to the governor and the State Executive Council and approached the court to maintain the status quo.

She appealed to the relevant authorities to intervene urgently and ensure that the dispute was resolved peacefully and in accordance with the law.

“We are appealing to Governor Monday Okpebholo, who is a man of peace, to suspend this action and reverse the decision contained in the statement issued by the Secretary to the State Government. We want peace, not war,” Agbo said,

Responding, Lukeman Momodu Odamah III, said the government has acted in accordance with the law and with the customary tradition of the people.

He said the case is in court and that protest cannot change the customer tradition of the people, advising the protesters to wait for the court to decide.

World.title: BREAKING | Donovan Marx farm attack: TWO arrested after ears cut off
World.content:
Two suspects have been arrested following the brutal farm attack in Ventersdorp, North West, in which farmer Donovan Marx was shot and had both ears cut off. Image: Facebook

WARNING: This article contains graphic descriptions of violence and injuries that some readers may find disturbing. Reader discretion is advised.

North West police have arrested two suspects following the brutal farm attack on cattle farmer Donovan Marx, 50, who was shot and had both ears cut off.

Police confirmed the arrests on Saturday, 31 October, three days after armed men attacked Marx on his farm in Syferfontein, near Ventersdorp.



North West police commissioner Lieutenant General Arthur Peter Adams welcomed the breakthrough and praised the investigating team for its swift efforts.

Police have not disclosed the suspects’ identities, ages or when they will appear in court.

Farmer shot during robbery

According to police, three armed men wearing balaclavas confronted a farmworker who was mowing the lawn on Wednesday, 28 October, at approximately 08:30.

The attackers allegedly threatened the worker with firearms before tying his hands and feet with cable ties.

When Marx arrived in his red Isuzu bakkie, two of the men approached and shot him.

They dragged him into the farmhouse, restrained him and allegedly stabbed and assaulted him.



The suspects stole three firearms from a safe before fleeing in Marx’s bakkie.

The farmworker managed to free himself and raise the alarm.

Marx remains in intensive care

Marx remains in a stable but serious condition at Mediclinic Potchefstroom.

His family confirmed on Saturday that surgeons could not save his ears and that he may require prosthetic reconstruction in future.

The farmer was also shot in the back, with the bullet passing through a kidney. Surgeons removed part of his large intestine following injuries sustained during the attack.

His wife, Louise, and the family have appealed for privacy and urged the public to stop spreading unverified claims about his injuries.

They also asked people not to speculate about potential suspects or investigative leads.

FF Plus condemns brutal attack

Freedom Front Plus leader Corné Mulder condemned the attack in a statement issued on Wednesday, calling on President Cyril Ramaphosa to prioritise farm murders and rural safety.

Mulder said farm attacks frequently involved extreme violence and torture and should not be dismissed as ordinary crime.

The party accused Ramaphosa of failing to give sufficient attention to farm attacks and called for stronger action against incitement to violence targeting farmers.

The FF Plus also expressed its sympathy to Marx and his family and wished him a full recovery.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp also condemned the attack, warning that violent crime in rural communities threatened farmers, farmworkers and the country’s food security.

#DoAUpdate | The Minister of Agriculture, Willie Aucamp, has strongly condemned the attack on cattle farmer Donovan Marx (50), who is still in hospital after being brutally attacked and tortured on his farm between Potchefstroom and Ventersdorp on Wednesday, 28 October 2026.… pic.twitter.com/6xmka1VFUA — National Department of Agriculture (@DOAgov_ZA) October 29, 2026

Police investigation continues

Police have not confirmed whether they are searching for a third suspect following Saturday’s arrests.

Investigators have also not disclosed whether they recovered the firearms stolen during the robbery.

Further details are expected as the investigation continues.

World.title: Two arrested at Kosi Bay for alleged rental vehicle smuggling
World.content:
Two suspects have been arrested after allegedly trying to smuggle two rental vehicles across the South African border into Mozambique.

On Thursday, 29 October 2026, the Border Management Authority (BMA) intercepted the vehicles at the Kosi Bay Port of Entry in KwaZulu-Natal.

“At approximately 12h30, BMA border guards conducting operations at Kosi Bay identified a white 2025 Ford Ranger double cab, bearing the Mpumalanga registration number, driven by a 75-year-old South African male who intended to cross into Mozambique,” the BMA explained, per a statement.



SMUGGLING AVERTED

An inspection of the vehicle and a subsequent interview with the driver followed. These led the guards to believe that the car was a rental being smuggled across the border.

Their suspicions were confirmed upon contacting the rental company. The company established it had not provided the required cross-border authorisation letter or the relevant Registration Certificate for the vehicle.

“The company further indicated that, according to its tracking records, the vehicle was stationary in Johannesburg,” the statement continues. “Upon activating its Cartrack system to verify the vehicle’s location, the company discovered that the tracking unit had been removed.”



SECOND INTERCEPTION

The two rentals were en-route to Mozambique. Image via X @TheBMA_SA

In the midst of this operation, the BMA border guards identified a second Ford Ranger. The rental company also confirmed the vehicle was one of theirs – specifically, one that was fraudulently rented out.

After alerting the senior commandment, the guards liaised with their Mozambican counterparts. By doing so, they could intercept this vehicle and its driver for further investigation.

During questioning, the driver – identified as a white male – claimed that he had borrowed the vehicle from a friend in Pretoria. However, the authorities found him to be in the alleged possession of fraudulent cross-border authorisation letters and RC1 documents.



“The car rental company,” says BMA, “was requested to provide copies of its genuine cross-border letters and registration documents to assist with verification.”

SMUGGLING STOPPED IN ITS TRACKS

The authorities arrested the suspects and charged them with possession of suspected stolen property, forgery, fraud and uttering.

They were slated to appear in court on Friday, 30 October 2026.



BMA Commissioner, Dr Michael Masiapato, lauded the efforts of the Kosi Bay border guards.

“The BMA has intensified its efforts to identify suspicious movements and continue to prevent vehicles obtained through alleged fraudulent means from being taken across our borders,” said Dr Masiapato. “Through the vigilance of our border guards and timely information-sharing with the rental company, we were able to intervene and prevent the further movement of these vehicles into another country.”

What are your thoughts about these arrests? Let us know in the comments below.
