World.title: Simple DOES it: MG3 1.5 Comfort review
World.content:
It has been a while since we last drove something like the MG3 1.5 Comfort manual. And it is worth reminding ourselves that, while classified as a compact hatchback, this Chinese-built, British-badged newcomer is anything but a small car. There is a surprising amount of space inside, with luggage capacity of 293 litres, in fact.

We suppose the exterior styling is generally attractive, particularly from the front, with its low-ish snout. From the rear, the broad stance and short overhang is very generic, and you’d be hard-pressed to say what it was with the badge covered up. Nevertheless, none of this is a deal-breaker in a car whose biggest selling point is value for money.

MG3 1.5 COMFORT MANUAL

Possibly its best angle, with requisite attention given to its front grille. Image: Ray Leathern

At just R269 900, the MG3 1.5 Comfort occupies an ever-rarer space in the South African market – a cheap compact hatchback. Something that offers a sensible mode of transport, a decent equipment list and a traditional petrol engine with a manual gearbox for simplicity. As such, under the bonnet sits a naturally aspirated 1.5-litre four-cylinder petrol engine producing 81 kW and 142 Nm. Figures that will hardly trouble the performance-car fraternity, but they are perfectly adequate for everyday commuting and general running about.



The ICE is smooth and reasonably economical, with a claimed combined consumption figure of 6.0 l/100 km. Our experience suggests that, as with any car, the actual figure will depend on traffic, driving style and how enthusiastically you depress that accelerator pedal. There is no turbocharger, so a degree of forward planning is required when overtaking or climbing a steep incline. Thankfully, the short, stubby gear lever is pleasantly slick for making snappy downshifts. Keep the engine in the right part of its rev range, which is beyond 2 000 rpm, and the MG3 1.5 Comfort happily keeps pace with traffic.

HOW’S THE CABIN?

Flat-bottom wheel and digital screens a nice touch amongst the hard plastics. Image: Ray Leathern

There is one situation in which the modest ICE output becomes more noticeable. That’s when the air-conditioning compressor is in operation during acceleration. The engine has to work that little harder, and you can feel it bogging down. So, AC in Sport mode in this instance. Nevertheless, there is something reassuring straightforward, even old-school, about this mechanical package. Just a petrol engine, manual gears and a handbrake lever, for those who still enjoy being involved in the driving process.

Beyond that, the MG3 1.5 Comfort cabin is not going to win any awards for the softness of its plastics. Fairly hard, shiny surfaces are evident throughout, but the overall presentation is modern and new. The flat-bottomed steering wheel feels good in your hands, while the digital instrumentation and seven-inch touchscreen lend the interior a more contemporary appearance. At this base spec you also get a reversing camera and keyless entry/starting. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are also part of the updated MG3 offering but it’s not wireless and you do need a cable.

IS IT COMFORT-ABLE?

Pretty practical, with 293 litres of boot capacity. And 16-inch rims don’t compromise ride quality. Image: Ray Leathern

The ride quality and general mechanical refinement is another pleasant surprise. The suspension deals with bumps and uneven surfaces with a good degree of suppleness. And 195/55 R16 tyres provide a sensible compromise between appearance and comfort. Our one criticism concerns refinement at highway speeds. Engine noise rather than road din becomes more noticeable as the pace rises, and the engine rpm sits well above 3 000 rpm at around 120 km/h.

Likewise, its assisted power steering is another area that could be improved. At higher speeds, the steering can require small, frequent corrections to maintain a straight line. It is not a deal-breaker by any means, and it’s hardly noticeable at urban speeds, but a little more directional stability would make longer journeys less tiring.

THE VERDICT

You’d be hard-pressed to pull one out of a hatchback lineup from this angle. Image: Ray Leathern

The MG3 1.5 Comfort is not perfect by any stretch. But “searching for perfection leaves a lot to ignore,” as Eddie Vedder once sang. It is spacious, sensibly equipped and easy to drive. More importantly, at R269 900, it offers a lot of car for the money. It’s standard safety equipment also deserves consideration: Four airbags, alongside features such as ABS and electronic stability control is impressive at this price point.



Moreover, we like it because it keeps things simple. A naturally aspirated engine, a proper manual gearbox and an old-fashioned handbrake lever may not sound revolutionary, but they do make for a refreshingly straightforward week of road testing.

World.title: Then vs now: The Kiffness shows rapid decline of Johannesburg [video]
World.content:
The Kiffness has shared images of the rapid decline of Johannesburg. Images via X

The Kiffness has returned to his X account to respond to a report that Johannesburg is “on the brink of a collapse”, particularly over its dire water systems

The Cape Town-born musician recently made headlines after confessing to receiving death threats over his controversial views.

THE KIFFNESS ON THE DECLINE OF JOHANNESBURG

After disabling his account for many months, The Kiffness returned to X with a video in which he describes how Johannesburg has deteriorated over the past 15 years.



The 38-year-old artist was responding to a report by Polymarket, a prediction market platform, which claimed that the city was on the “brink of a total collapse”. It referred to water shortages caused by decades of damaged infrastructure.

In a tweet, The Kiffness- real name David Scott – posted a clip of him sharing Google Street View photos of various parts of Johannesburg in 2010 and in 2026.

“As a South African, I want to show the rest of the world how a functioning city can be turned into a completely broken, derelict city in a very short time”, he said in the video.

In the pictures taken in 2010, the city appeared clean with well-maintained buildings and functioning traffic lights. The recent images revealed buildings in severe neglect, damaged roads riddled with potholes, and strewn with rubbish”

The Kiffness warned: “The decline of my hometown Jo’burg is a warning to London, Paris, New York, Amsterdam and every major city across the west. If you don’t act now, your cities will suffer the same fate”

WILL THE NEXT MAYOR SHAKE THINGS UP?

According to a trending poll by Polymarket, the Democratic Alliance’s Helen Zille has a 57% chance of becoming the next mayor of Johannesburg



During her campaign, the 75-year-old highlighted her key plan to restore the city’s functionality, focusing on basic services, infrastructure, financial management, and fighting crime and corruption.

On Wednesday, 4 November, Johannesburg voters will elect councillors to the City of Johannesburg council during the local government elections. The composition of that council will determine which party or coalition can govern the city and who ultimately becomes mayor.

World.title: Kenny Kunene vows to make Joburg a no-go zone for illegal immigrants
World.content:
Patriotic Alliance (PA) mayoral candidate for the City of Johannesburg, Kenny Kunene, says the metro will become a no-go zone for illegal immigrants if he is elected mayor.

Kunene made the remarks as political parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the local government elections on Wednesday, 4 November.

KENNY KUNENE VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION

Addressing party supporters, Kunene said that within 30 days of being elected mayor, he would establish a task team to work alongside Department of Home Affairs officials to identify and deport undocumented foreign nationals.



He said tackling illegal immigration would become a daily priority under his administration.

“We cannot have illegal immigrants being employed by big businesses at the expense of South Africans. So, we are going into Johannesburg to mass deport those who do not have the right papers.

“What I am saying is not a pipe dream. I have already raided houses in Bramley, in Kew, Sandton and in Hillbrow. I have raided flats where we arrested illegal immigrants and handed them over to the police. I have already started doing it, so I’m not talking about a dream,” he said as party supporters cheered.



Kenny Kunene says says that "WHEN" he becomes Mayor the City of Johannesburg the city will be a no go zone for illegal immigrants



"The City of Johannesburg is going to be a no go zone for illegal immigrants unapologetically so"



Kunene further adds that within his first 30 days… pic.twitter.com/wHaHgLm4pF — NOWinSA (@NowInSA) October 30, 2026

Ahead of the 2024 general elections, through its leader Gayton McKenzie and his deputy Kenny Kunene, the PA was vocal about its anti-illegal immigration stance, popularising the #Abahambe campaign while advocating for South Africans to be prioritised.

However, the party appeared to tone down this rhetoric after joining the Government of National Unity (GNU). Kunene’s latest remarks suggest that the issue is once again taking centre stage in the party’s election campaign.



“When I am the mayor, I will have more power to drive the programme of getting rid of these criminals. Our buildings are hijacked, our houses are hijacked, even in Soweto houses are being hijacked,” Kunene said.

World.title: Soweto Derby: ‘Kaizer Chiefs should’ve buried Orlando Pirates’
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando da Cruz believes his team should have buried Orlando Pirates in Saturday’s Soweto Derby at FNB Stadium.

The Buccaneers walked away with maximum points and claimed the bragging rights with a 2-1 win over the Glamour Boys.

Yanela Mbuthuma and Tshepang Moremi score for Pirates on the day while Amakhosi’s only goal of the game was scored by Pule Mmodi.



Chiefs had two golden opportunities early in the first half with Wandile Duba complicating things, blasting his effort towards Sipho Chaine who made a brilliant save.

Now, while Da Cruz admits they lost to an experienced and in-form Pirates, he still of the view that Chiefs should have easily won the match.

SOWETO DERBY: DA CRUZ SAYS KAIZER CHIEFS SHOULD HAVE BURIED ORLANDO PIRATES

“In the first half, we must have killed this game,” said Da Cruz on SuperSport TV.



“Normally, 2-0 or 3-0 because the goal of Pirates, we’ve seen that it’s offside and maybe there was [supposed to be] a red card as well.

“If we had scored two or three goals, we were going to kill this game,” added Da Cruz.

“In the second half, the last 20 minutes, with our young players we lacked experience. They didn’t create chances because we have a lack of experience, we gave them chances to score more goals.



“We know where we must improve,” concluded Da Cruz.

World.title: Pogacar 'happy to be alive' after difficult Vuelta crash recovery
World.content:
PARIS - Tadej Pogacar has revealed he suffered three fractured vertebrae in the crash that ended his season, admitting he is "just happy to be alive" after scans uncovered the full extent of injuries that also left him battling concussion-related balance problems.

The Slovenian rider had initially been diagnosed with a fracture in his neck and a broken collarbone following his Vuelta a Espana accident, but a follow-up scan in his home country uncovered further damage.

"There's actually a funny story. Two weeks ago, I was in Slovenia and I went to do another CT scan. I knew I had a C7 fracture, but then we saw I had two more broken vertebrae, the T1 and T2," Pogacar told The Athletic in an interview published Saturday.

"At that moment, I was happy I didn't do the European Championships, which had been my initial goal. When I saw I had three broken vertebrae? I'm just happy to be alive, actually, or just to be standing."

The five-time Tour de France champion said he has now returned largely to normal life, although he remains cautious as he continues to heal.

"I don't have discomfort anymore," he said. "I have to be careful not to crash on the bike, or do some heavy lifting with my left arm or with my neck. But I can do basically everything normal now."

Pogacar said the first weeks after the accident were particularly difficult. A concussion left him struggling with dizziness, nausea and poor coordination, preventing him from resuming normal activities.

"I had to be showered with the help of the team doctor. I could not shower. I was getting dizzy as soon as I stood or when I put my head down. I was just completely out of it and it was so tough," he said.

- 'Really depressed' -

The 28-year-old underwent surgery but said recovery was slower and mentally tougher than he had expected.

"It took one hour and 40 minutes, a long time, and when I got out of anesthesia the doctor was trying to make some jokes, but I was not feeling it. I was really depressed after the surgery," said Pogacar.

"For the first two weeks, I was really mentally not OK. I was really down. I was not a fun person to be around."

Pogacar said his mood improved once he resumed rehabilitation and indoor training.

"When I started to get on the home trainer, to go to physio every day, then I started to feel better -- also in the head. But it was a day-to-day fight."

Although doctors classified the neck fracture as stable, Pogacar said its potential consequences remained sobering.

"But if I crash again on the bike now, it can be very problematic. Everybody says that I was lucky, and you're always lucky after a crash where you can walk away and you're fine.

"You see it's pretty serious and not to joke around. It's a bit scary, to be honest, to think about it."

World.title: South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs in third Test to win series
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs and clinched a series victory when Australia were bowled out for 111 on the fifth day of the third Test at Newlands on Saturday.

Kagiso Rabada took two wickets in the first over and followed up with a third in a devastating opening spell which ripped out Australia's top three batsmen after they had started the day needing 288 to win.

Off-spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best six for 16 in 21.1 overs as South Africa completed their win shortly before tea.

Josh Inglis was run out to add to Australia's woes after Rabada's initial burst before Harmer took two wickets in three balls to plunge the tourists to 42 for six.

Australia were 60 for seven at lunch when Mitchell Starc was caught at short leg but in keeping with a series of multiple changes of fortune, South Africa were kept in the field for another two hours before completing their win.

South Africa, the defending World Test champions, were projected to depose Australia at the top of the International Cricket Council world Test rankings at the end of a series in which all three matches produced a result on the fifth day.

Travis Head scored a single off Rabada's second delivery but Matt Renshaw, Australia's most successful batsman in the series, was out first ball, glancing Rabada down the leg side to a diving wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton.

Three balls later the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne padded up to a ball which swung in sharply and was given out leg before wicket, with a review showing umpire's call on off stump.

Head fell to a reflex catch by Marco Jansen at gully as the left-hander flashed at Rabada and the South African players celebrated the demise of a batsman capable of playing a match-changing innings.

World.title: The Voting Booth | What coalition combinations will work for your metro?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - On Sunday 1 November at 11 am, eNCA will reveal what party supporters truly want their own parties to go into coalition with.

Having polled a thousand people each in all six of the country’s major metros in the eNCA MarkData poll, we asked supporters of every party which parties they want their parties to work with and which parties they absolutely did not want their parties to go into coalition with.

They also had the option to choose for their party to work with no other party to rather stay on the opposition benches rather than join any coalition.

The idea is to let voters be heard before politicians start bargaining for positions, the trappings of power, and the lure of huge pay cheques.

And the results we will announce are quite astounding. It will leave little room for posturing, egos, personal animosity and pettiness, if the politicians were to listen to the voters who elected them.

Don’t miss the live broadcast at 11 am on Sunday when all shall be revealed.

World.title: Six killed in truck crash in Flagstaff
World.content:
FLAGSTAFF - Six people have been killed in a truck crash in Flagstaff in the Eastern Cape.

The truck was carrying about 30 people travelling from Mswakazi in Port St Johns for a traditional ceremony. It reportedly overturned after the driver lost control on a gravel road, killing two men and four women.

Several other passengers have been hospitalised at Holy Cross Provincial Hospital.

Police said they’re still investigating the cause of the crash.

Eastern Cape Transport MEC Xolile Nqatha said the latest tragedy brings to 18 the number of people killed in the past seven days. He is urging drivers to exercise caution and ensure their vehicles are roadworthy.

World.title: Sticks are part of our culture: Ngobese-Zuma
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - March and March rejects the latest court ruling, insisting that protest restrictions threaten cultural identity and undermine the right to peaceful assembly.

A High Court ruling has permitted the group to march, but only under strict conditions.

Leader Jacinta Ngobese criticised the ban on sticks, arguing it ignores their cultural significance.

She also challenges why police need weapons at peaceful demonstrations.

"Police as well shouldn't carry weapons because they do intimidate the crowds with those same weapons that they carry as the police. Because if it is a peaceful protest and nobody's carrying sticks, as you say, then why would you need to carry guns? But on top of that, there's another issue of sticks generally being a reflection of our culture, of who we are as Zulu people. Not only just Zulu people, but as African people.

"So the courts also need to be cognizant of that, that you can't strip us away of our identity because you want to fuel a narrative that doesn't exist. For 21 months, we've marched with those sticks and there have been very few incidents of anything happening unless there were times where foreign nationals themselves provoked the situations. But those situations are never covered on the media, which is what we are complaining about.

"That nobody carries sticks because they're trying to intimidate people or scare people or beat up people. We carry those sticks because it's part of our culture and that needs to be emphasized. We can't be adopting and accepting Western ways of doing life just because of fears that the government have when they can sit down with the people and solve those problems and allow people to protest the way that they know how to."

World.title: West Indies crush Bangladesh by eight wickets in first Test
World.content:
DHAKA - Brandon King struck a career-best 81 not out as West Indies cruised to an eight-wicket win over Bangladesh in the first Test on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

King hit 10 fours and a six in his 115-ball knock to help the visitors chase down the target of 170 in 35.1 overs on the fourth day in Mirpur after Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings.

Jomel Warrican, who was named player of the match, claimed 4-63 to follow up his five-wicket haul in Bangladesh's first innings as the hosts were bowled out in 48.4 overs.

West Indies captain Roston Chase took 5-36 in the second innings, his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.

Chase said the team was determined to win the series and go up in the rankings.

"The guys were determined, even though we didn't have a good start in the first innings," Chase said.

"We lost the lead, but we were still determined to fight back and try to win the game, and that's what we did."

Bangladesh had resumed the fourth day at 79-6, holding a lead of 106, but their hopes of setting a challenging target suffered an early blow when Jaker Ali edged Warrican to slip, where Chase took the catch.

Jaker, who scored 22 off 34 balls, was the second-highest scorer for Bangladesh in the innings.

Nayeem Hasan survived two dropped catches off Chase, on 21 and 29, to keep Bangladesh going.

- 'Intention was good' -

He added 26 runs with Hasan Mahmud before Warrican trapped the latter lbw for eight.

Taijul Islam contributed eight in a 17-run partnership with Nayeem before Chase dismissed him to leave Bangladesh at 127-9.

Nayeem then reached his maiden Test half-century off 87 balls, with four boundaries, but his resistance ended when he attempted to hit Chase over long-on and was caught by Joshua Bishop.

He made 52 off 91 balls, while Shoriful Islam remained unbeaten on seven as Bangladesh were dismissed cheaply.

Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto said his team failed to execute their plans.

"All three departments didn't do well, especially in the field. These things can happen sometimes, but I believe the intention and preparation were quite good," he said.

"Going forward, we need to look at those areas and work out how we can do better in these conditions."

West Indies started confidently, with openers King and John Campbell continuing their aggressive approach to take the visitors to 64 without loss in 14.1 overs before rain interrupted play.

After a delay of around an hour, they added another 23 runs before bad light and lightning forced a further stoppage of 45 minutes.

King was dropped on 70 by substitute fielder Ebadot Hossain off Taijul after the break, but the opener made Bangladesh pay with his fine, unbeaten knock.

Campbell fell just short of a half-century, bowled by Shoriful for 49 off 55 balls, with six fours and a six.

The second Test will be played in Sylhet from November 5.

World.title: UK PM 'open' to slavery apology but not reparations
World.content:
LONDON - Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was "open" to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.

Writing in The Guardian days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in the Caribbean, and as King Charles III tours the region, the British premier argued that "we need to face up to the past".

With London under pressure to formally apologise for its pivotal part in the trade and compensate Caribbean nations, he pledged to have "difficult conversations to safeguard the Commonwealth for the future".

Burnham said he wanted to "express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today", but insisted reparations were not "the right answer".

"I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part," he wrote in the op-ed.

The transatlantic slave trade was a "brutal and barbaric violation" of enslaved people's rights, the UK leader added, offering a "structured dialogue with those affected".

"Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them."

- 'Disappointing' -

The issue has loomed large over King Charles's ongoing nine-day visit to three Caribbean countries, which will include an address to the Commonwealth heads of government summit that runs from Sunday to Wednesday.

Burnham is also set to attend the gathering in St John's, the capital of Antigua and Barbuda.

The 56-member Commonwealth, which Charles, 77, helms, is mainly composed of British ex-colonies, with the UK's central role in slavery and the treatment of its former subjects long a contentious issue within the organisation.

In the Bahamas on Tuesday, the monarch acknowledged "the great suffering of the past" during the first leg of his visit.

Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.

The country profited for centuries from colonialism and the slave trade, but argues it also led the way in the latter's abolition.

In 1833, the UK parliament passed a law to abolish slavery in most of the British Empire.

Denis O'Brien, founder of The Repair Campaign, which advocates for reparations for slavery for Caribbean nations, said the UK government "must stop obfuscating and give a full and formal apology now".

"This would be a significant and symbolic first step towards reparatory justice," he added.

O'Brien called Burnham's op-ed "disappointing", predicting it will not "quell the demand for an apology".

World.title: EFF's Mofokeng wants Joburg governance overhaul
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Infrastructure and service delivery are among the key issues facing the City of Johannesburg.

EFF mayoral candidate Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng said the city needs to rethink how it's governed.

The party also wants a bigger share of national grant funding.

The EFF is holding a rally in Soweto ahead of Wednesday's polls.

"There's a historical lag in maintaining what we already had, but there's a lack of forecasting and resource mobilization for the kind of Johannesburg that needs to emerge. Through the EFF and our leadership, we are saying we can do a few things.

"We can re-pivot, re-organize the city's council and governance, but we can also do the necessary advocacy required in parliament with national treasury to increase Joburg's budget from 10% to 15% of the grant to allow us to have climate resiliency, for example, in our housing plans for a future that's also sustainable."

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Zelensky welcomes sale of crucial US Patriot missiles but warns delivery could take years
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed US approval of a potential $2.1 billion sale of 500 vital Patriot interceptor missiles on Friday, but warned that it may take “a few years” for them to arrive.

“We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors,” he wrote on X, urging Washington to provide weapons from existing stockpiles to help Ukraine through the winter.

Kyiv uses the defensive weapons to blunt Russia’s continuous ballistic missile strikes on its territory, but Ukraine’s supply ran dry earlier this month, CNN previously reported.

The US State Department approved the potential sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE interceptors, the most advanced Patriot variant currently in service and one of the few weapons capable of shooting down incoming ballistic missiles, on Friday, according to a department release.

“We did ask our American partners to provide Ukraine with a winter support package – at a rate of 100 Patriot interceptors per month,” Zelensky said. “Five hundred missiles would be enough to protect our skies over the coming months – precisely when it is so important for Ukraine to be in a strong position in negotiations and for Russia NOT to succeed in breaking life in Ukrainian cities and communities.”

The State Department’s announcement did not specify when the interceptors would be delivered to Ukraine. CNN has asked the State Department for details about the expected delivery timeline.

The need for the inceptors is particularly acute as Ukraine heads into winter under continuing Russian bombardment. Zelensky claimed that the US and its partners “have sufficient stocks of PAC-3 interceptors in their warehouses” and urged them to release those weapons immediately.

“Providing them to Ukraine right now – in the winter of 2026–2027 – and replenishing our partners’ arsenals LATER, in THE FOLLOWING YEARS, through this production already contracted and paid for by Ukraine and our partners would be the right approach,” he said on X.

The sale nonetheless marks a significant victory for Zelensky, who has repeatedly appealed to Western leaders for more of the crucial defensive weapons. In an August interview with CNN, Zelensky argued that selling even a small portion of the US Patriot stockpile to Ukraine would be sufficient to “destroy all the Russians’ ballistic missiles.”

The purchase is not subsidized or financed by the US, according to the release. Instead, Ukraine is covering the estimated $2.1 billion purchase with funds from Canada, Germany and Norway in addition to a loan from the European Union, the State Department said.

The department said the proposed sale would support US foreign policy and national security objectives “by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe.”

Energy strikes fuel US-Ukraine tensions

The approval comes after weeks of mounting tensions between the US and Ukraine. Earlier this month, President Donald Trump announced a deal to allow Russian diesel exports to global energy markets and waived a further slate of sanctions related to Russian fossil fuel sales that had only just been signed into law.

Trump also threatened to withhold intelligence from Kyiv over its strikes on Russian refineries, and Ukraine’s access to the crucial Starshield satellite system was throttled for a period before it was restored last week.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Friday that Ukrainian drones had attacked three Russian oil refineries and a gas-chemical complex, according to Russian state news agency TASS,

The same day, Zelensky accused Moscow of continuing to target Ukraine’s infrastructure, saying Russian ballistic missiles had struck oil refining infrastructure in Kremenchuk, in the Poltava region.

“The Russians have not taken a single step toward energy de-escalation,” he said in a Telegram post. “We will also act accordingly and entirely justly.”

Friday’s sale announcement also left open whether any missile components would be produced in Ukraine as part of a so-called “offset agreement.”

The State Department said that it was “not aware” of any such arrangement between Ukraine and Lockheed Martin, the defense firm that produces the Patriot, but noted that the matter could be directly negotiated between Kyiv and Lockheed.

Trump had shocked many by announcing in July at the NATO summit in Turkey that Ukraine would receive a license to produce its own Patriot missiles, a move that could eventually alleviate pressure on US production lines amid a munitions shortage linked to the Iran war and growing international demand. But any Ukrainian interceptor factory could take years to build, and the president has seemingly backed off from the move.

This story has been updated with additional details. CNN’s Jennifer Hansler contributed to this report.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: What are the possible scenarios after Israel’s elections?
World.content:
With most votes counted, Israel’s election has produced no clear winner, setting up weeks – and possibly months – of political uncertainty. Several outcomes and scenarios may come into play.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc has lost the majority it held in the outgoing parliament. With about 53 seats projected, it falls short of the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government in the 120-seat Knesset.

Netanyahu could try to recruit one of the opposition parties to join his government, but they all ruled out cooperation with him during campaigning. Politicians who have joined him in recent years have often found themselves significantly weakened with little substantive influence over policy. Netanyahu could also try to seek individual opposition defectors, but that would require several defections to close the gap.

The opposition, on the other hand, has won a majority in the parliament, but their path to power is crossed by ideological, national and personal divisions.

Netanyahu’s main rival Gadi Eisenkot is projected to win 21 seats, but he cannot reach the 61-seat majority without the two Arab parties, Ra’am and the Joint list, who are projected to win a record 19 seats. On Wednesday, Yair Golan, the leader of the left-wing Democrats party, called on his partners to count the Arab parties as part of the bloc, rejecting what he called Netanyahu’s “racist division between Jewish and Arab votes.”

But two of Eisenkot’s right-wing allies oppose forming a government that includes the Arab parties or a minority government that relies on their outside support.

Given the apparent deadlock, another scenario is a national unity government pairing Netanyahu’s Likud and one or more parties from the opposition, an option that would replace his current hardliner government. Both Netanyahu and the opposition leaders have ruled this out during the campaign, but it may be one of the only ways to avoid another election.

World.title: Oleshky evacuees return to Ukraine under Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire
World.content:
Dmytro had not seen his wife Larisa for 1,711 days.

Waiting near the border between Ukraine and Belarus, his nervous eyes were on the horizon, looking for the bus carrying Larisa and others fleeing the occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky.

Hundreds of people – and many pets – arrived back in Ukraine on Saturday afternoon after being evacuated from the frontline city under a ceasefire that Pope Leo XIV called for and first lady Melania Trump helped to negotiate.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the arrival of the evacuees on Telegram, thanking Trump for the mediation.

“And I thank everyone in the world—all journalists, all political and civic leaders, and all concerned people—who drew global attention to the situation in Oleshky and the genuine humanitarian catastrophe in the territory of Ukraine temporarily occupied by Russia. When the world pays attention, people are saved,” he said.

Dmytro, whose last name cannot be published for security reasons, is a soldier in the Ukrainian military which made Larisa vulnerable when Russia took over Oleshky, their southern Ukrainian hometown.

The couple managed to get their daughter out, but Larisa was worried that if she tried to leave, she’d be picked up at a Russian military checkpoint during filtration – the humiliating and often violent questioning Ukrainians who found themselves under Russian occupation had to undergo before being allowed to leave for areas still under Ukrainian control.

So she stayed, hoping for a miracle. Instead, her life became a nightmare.

The town was hit by a major flood in 2023 after the nearby Nova Kakhovka Dam collapsed – most likely because of a Russian explosion. Several hundred people were reported to have died in the flooding and the town suffered major damage. The Russian-installed authorities were unable, or unwilling, to invest into repairs.

More destruction came in the subsequent years of heavy fighting in the area and the humanitarian situation has deteriorated in recent months. The town was reported by Ukrainian authorities to have ran out of food and other supplies in September, with no access to electricity, gas, medicine and other essentials. Reports from that time said people were surviving on grass and weeds.

The director of the Chernihiv Regional Hospital Andriy Zhydenko was waiting at the border with his staff to provide medical assistance to the evacuees. He told CNN the the effects of prolonged malnutrition will be a key concern, explaining that the evacuees will need to be fed carefully because they have been starving for so long that consuming too much food too quickly could be dangerous.

“There are people with injuries, stroke survivors, and those with limited mobility,” he said, adding that everyone at the hospital was overjoyed to be welcoming Ukrainian citizens home. “All of my staff wanted to come here. People have suffered greatly there. There is no humanity.”

Long way home

Some 40% of Oleshky’s prewar population of around 24,000 managed to flee to Ukraine-controlled territory when it was still possible early in the fighting, according to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), a US-based conflict observer. Thousands of others have escaped since then, but many remained, either unable or unwilling to leave.

Zhanna Ptakhova and her daughers Elizaveta and Daria Paliy were among those who made it out when it was still possible.

But Ptakhova’s husband, and Elizaveta’s and Daria’s father, stayed in Oleshky. He was going to taking care of their home until they could safely return.

But that has not happened. “The conditions were terrible. No electricity, no gas, no heat – but he’s a man with golden hands,” Ptakhova told CNN.

“He took a house that had been adapted for modern civilian life and turned it into a home suited for a primitive lifestyle; he built a stove, raised chickens to feed himself, planted a garden, and through his own hard work, he survived there,” she said.

The family was going to be reunited after three years apart.

Access routes to Oleshky have been heavily mined and littered with drone and vehicle debris and evacuation across the Dnipro River directly into Ukraine-controlled territory is not possible.

That made the journey out long and scary. Ukraine’s ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets traveled to Oleshky to personally escort the evacuees into Ukraine-controlled territory, becoming the first high-profile Ukrainian official to openly travel to occupied areas under Russian control and Russia since the start of the war.

Once a two-day demining operation was completed on Thurday, people who wanted to leave gathered on Friday and traveled through the occupied Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea to Anapa in Russia’s Krasnodar region.

The evacuees then flew from Anapa airport to Gomel, Belarus, according to the Russian Defense Ministry and Ukrainian officials.

World.title: The real question we should all be asking about AI
World.content:
The stock market is turning its back on Big Tech.

Google just had its worst day ever. Intel tumbled more than any day since the Nixon administration. Amazon and Meta both had significant declines this week, too. The Nasdaq tumbled and is just over a percentage point away from a correction (a 10 percent decline from its all-time high).

The common thread: Building the infrastructure to power AI is really, really expensive – and Big Tech profits aren’t yet justifying that massive expense. AI companies are increasingly doling out more cash for data centers than their businesses are able to generate.

But if the stock market is supposed be to delivering some kind of message, Big Tech isn’t hearing it.

Spending on AI has reached $1.6 trillion since 2023 and is expected to hit $1 trillion every single year for the next decade or so, according to JPMorgan. None of that changed this week.

That’s because the market that’s financing all of this – the bond market – is mostly shrugging its shoulders while the stock market is in the midst of a mild freakout. Lenders have been lining up to take on Big Tech’s debt to pay for the technology that’s reshaping the global economy.

That means the questions the market seems to be asking about AI – will Big Tech keep growing its spending? (it most certainly will) and will AI will turn a profit anytime soon? (doesn’t look like it) – are the wrong ones.

The real question we should be asking about AI is: How much longer will the bond market sustain the nonstop spending spree?

That will ultimately dictate whether AI turns into a success or a bust.

AI math

The way AI math works is like this: Spend a lot of money upfront on the infrastructure needed to support AI (data centers, servers, chips, power, labor, building materials, etc.). Then, once the data center is switched on, AI companies can monetize that investment … somewhere between three months to two years later, according to Goldman Sachs.

With profit arriving that far down the road, hyperscalers (the Big Tech guys like Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta) need to borrow a ton of money upfront and pay back investors down the road.

“A ton” doesn’t really do it justice. Those four hyperscalers alone have been collectively responsible for more than a third of all capital expenditures from the S&P 500 over the past 12 months, notes John Higgins, chief economic adviser at Capital Economics.

That’s why a third of Big Tech’s capital expenditures this year are expected to be financed with debt – something like $250 billion worth of bonds from hyperscalers alone, according to Goldman Sachs. That’s expected to peak next year at around 35 percent of hyperscalers’ spending.

Wires in a Trainium2 UltraServer at an Amazon Web Services lab in Austin, Texas, on February 3, 2026. Amazon had a significant decline in the stock market this week. Mark Felix/AFP/Getty Images

But bond market investors don’t have infinite money to spend. And there’s a ton of competition for lending right now – especially from US Treasuries as the government is trying to pay for Social Security, Medicare and an expensive war, all at the same time.

That raises an obvious question: Exactly how much money are investors willing to lend AI companies?

It’s more than you might think.

The hypothetical maximum amount of debt the market can absorb is unknowable, but Goldman Sachs did the math anyway and came up with $510 billion of available investment-grade (top-tier) debt for the biggest hyperscalers. That’s more than double what they’re currently expected to be borrowing by the end of the year.

In other words: The biggest AI companies have a lot of runway left to borrow.

Who’s lending to whom?

The question isn’t how much; the question is how much longer.

The answer depends on two parts: Who is paying and who is receiving.

“We are not concerned about access to capital,” said Amanda Lynam, chief credit strategist for Goldman Sachs on a recent company podcast. “We are just expecting there to be a more nuanced conversation about where to issue and at what price.”

Private investment funds, venture funds and private equity are ready to do the heavy lifting to support the AI buildout, Lynam said, with trillions more dollars of “dry powder” to finance it.

But hyperscalers aren’t the only game in town. Other companies, including neoclouds, are playing in the space too. They’re highly indebted companies that rent out computing to other businesses, and their credit situation is starting to look iffy. Their non-investment-grade bonds deliver high yields that investors willing to take on more risk are willing to gamble on, in exchange for potentially massive rewards..

That’s the market in which CoreWeave plays, with its bond yields surging to 15 percent this month as losses piled up. Elon Musk said the neocloud industry, which includes CoreWeave, is due for a massive shakeout (he called it “guppy-level death.”)

The CoreWeave AI data center is under construction on October 21, 2026, in Kenilworth, New Jersey. The company’s bond yields surged to 15 percent this month as losses piled up. Stephanie Keith/Getty Images

Every new technology has winners and losers, and Musk may be right about neoclouds. We’ll see.

Hyperscalers, by contrast, look like winners. Their cloud revenue (a stat Wall Street uses to measure AI demand) grew 50 percent in the second quarter. They have huge contract backlogs and the capacity to absorb higher borrowing costs.

Those bottlenecks can support high prices, which helped hyperscaler revenue surge 19 percent over the past 12 months, according to Higgins.

And the advent of agentic AI has sent demand exploding: requests from agents consume 15 times as many tokens as human-initiated requests, according to OpenRouter.

“The outlook for these things doesn’t look obviously bleak, given that AI is gradually being used more and more in the economy,” Higgins said.

So what’s the problem?

The concern is that the cost of borrowing could get unwieldy. And that could change the economics that are still working for AI.

Negative sentiment that’s pervasive in the stock market could start to bleed out into the bond market, sending bond yields higher and raising borrowing costs for AI companies.

The bond market works best when there’s an end in sight, Lyman noted. Every AI investor believes there’s a light at the end of the tunnel. We just have no idea how long this tunnel is.

The uncertainty about when companies will ultimately start turning a profit and making money off all their massive AI investments could give the bond market pause, she said.

In the meantime, the outlook for the technology and the big companies’ finances looks quite strong, said Stephanie Aliaga, a global market strategist with JPMorgan, in a recent note to investors.

Warning signs would include a downshift in businesses’ AI usage, cheaper pricing or fewer customer commitments.

We’re not seeing any of those yet.

World.title: Irrigation Minister: Cairo Water Week a key platform for global dialogue
World.content:
Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Hani Sewilam said Cairo Water Week has become a key international platform for dialogue, exchanging expertise and building partnerships to address water challenges.

In a statement on Friday, October 30, 2026, Sewilam thanked the international organizations, national institutions and companies that supported the ninth edition, held from October 25 to 29 under the auspices of President Abdel Fattah El Sisi and themed “Water as a Catalyst for Peace, Shared Prosperity and a Sustainable Planet.”

He said the event’s success and broad international participation highlighted the importance of partnerships in achieving sustainable water development.

He stressed the Ministry’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with international organizations, research institutions and the private sector to implement the second-generation water system (2.0), support the National Water Resources and Irrigation Strategy 2050, and promote regional and international cooperation.

Sewilam praised the European Union and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), which co-organized the event, as well as UNESCO, the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA) and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) for their contributions.

He also commended the International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), alongside other partners, including GIZ, the German Development Bank (KFW), the Dutch and British embassies, IHE Delft and the American University in Cairo.

The Minister thanked Germany’s RWTH Aachen University for supporting AI-based training and developing a presentation for the Irrigation Museum in the New Administrative Capital.

He also praised national sponsors, including the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority, the Agricultural Bank of Egypt, Gennat Agricultural Company and PepsiCo Egypt, for supporting efforts to strengthen water and food security.

The five-day event concluded on Thursday, featuring 137 technical and scientific sessions and competitions, with the participation of ministers, governors, ambassadors and international and regional organizations, including FAO, the EU, UNESCO, IWMI and the WWC.

World.title: Egyptian, Hungarian FMs discuss bilateral ties, regional developments
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held talks in Budapest on Friday, October 30, 2026, with Hungarian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Anita Orbán on bilateral relations and the latest regional developments.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of building on the Strategic Partnership Declaration signed by the two countries in 2023, describing it as an important framework for promoting bilateral relations and expanding cooperation across various fields.

In this regard, he expressed Egypt’s keenness to translate this partnership into practical projects and programs that deliver tangible benefits to the two countries’ peoples.

The top Egyptian diplomat also underscored the significance of holding regular meetings of the joint higher committee as a key mechanism for advancing bilateral collaboration.

He stressed the need for increasing trade exchange, boosting tourism cooperation, while capitalizing on promising opportunities to expand economic and investment partnerships.

The two ministers reviewed ongoing joint projects between Egypt and Hungary in a number of areas, especially in the railway.

Abdelatty emphasized the need to build on the results of cooperation achieved in this area and explore new prospects for expanding the partnership in infrastructure and transport projects, while benefiting from Hungary’s expertise and capabilities in supporting Egypt’s development efforts.

The pair also exchanged views on a number of regional and international issues of mutual concern, particularly the latest regional developments and efforts to contain ongoing crises and prevent further escalation.
