World.title: Energy expert welcomes splitting of ministries
World.content:
An energy expert, Bornface Zulu, has described the creation of the Ministry of Petroleum and Ministry of Electricity as a strategic governance reform.

Mr Zulu says the decision to split the Ministry of Energy into the two ministries reflects the growing complexity of Zambia’s energy sector and the need for specialised leadership, accountability and policy focus.

Speaking in an interview with the media Mr Zulu says Electricity and Petroleum have evolved into distinct industries with different technical demands, investment requirements and national security implications.

He said managing both under one ministry increasingly risked diluting attention and slowing critical decision-making.

Mr Zulu added that one ministry was expected to simultaneously address load shedding, generation planning, transmission investment, fuel security, storage infrastructure and international petroleum market developments which became unsustainable in the long run.

“For many years, the Ministry of Energy was responsible for electricity generation, transmission, power trading, renewable energy development, fuel procurement, petroleum storage, strategic reserves, and broader energy policy. While this structure worked historically, the rapid expansion of both subsectors created what can be described as a governance capacity challenge,” he said.

Mr Zulu further commended the decision saying it is in line with regional best practices citing Angola and South Africa.

He said Zambia is not alone in adopting specialized approaches to energy governance stating that as the energy sector becomes larger and more complex, governance structures must evolve accordingly.

“South Africa restructured aspects of its energy governance framework to provide greater attention to electricity security and power sector reforms. Angola similarly maintains separate institutional arrangements for petroleum and electricity oversight, recognizing the unique strategic importance of each sector,” Mr Zulu said.

Government recently increased the number of ministries from 24 to 30 with the Ministry of Energy among those that were split into the Ministries of Petroleum and Electricity.

World.title: Grade 12 learners in Kalumbila district urged to embrace skills development
World.content:
Grade 12 graduands at Meheba Boarding Secondary School in Kalumbila District have been urged to embrace skills development, entrepreneurship, discipline, and innovation in order to become self-reliant and contribute meaningfully to national development.

Education Standards Officer for Special Education Exildah Biemba, who represented District Education Board Secretary Thompson Lungu said education should go beyond acquiring certificates and prepare young people to identify challenges and develop solutions.

Speaking during the school’s Eighth Graduation Ceremony for the 2026 Grade 12 leavers, Ms Biemba said graduates should use the knowledge and skills acquired to create opportunities for themselves and contribute meaningfully to their communities.

The graduation ceremony was held under the theme, “Equipped to Serve, Empowered to Transform,” the ceremony celebrated the achievements of the graduating learners after years of hard work and dedication.

Ms Biemba encouraged the graduands to explore opportunities in agriculture, entrepreneurship, technology and other productive sectors rather than depending solely on formal employment.

She said government had introduced various programmes to support young people, including the National Youth Policy, Technical Education Vocational and Entrepreneurship Training (TEVET), Constituency Development Fund (CDF) skills development bursaries and empowerment initiatives.

Ms Biemba also highlighted the role of the Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board in providing financial assistance to eligible students pursuing further education at qualifying public universities.

She cautioned the graduands against drug and alcohol abuse, gambling, violence and other destructive behaviours that could jeopardise their future.

Ms Biemba further urged them to uphold discipline, integrity, humility and perseverance, saying success required more than academic qualifications.

Meanwhile, Hope Beyond Borders Initiative Secretary General Michael Matanda encouraged the graduands to remain ambitious and never allow their present circumstances to determine their future.

Mr Matanda, who is a former Meheba Boarding Secondary School pupil and a graduate of Cavendish University Zambia,shared his personal journey from struggling to read in Grade One to attaining a university degree.

He said his journey was characterised by faith, determination and hard work, adding that young people should remain focused even when faced with financial and other challenges.

Mr Matanda disclosed that Cavendish University Zambia produced 105 refugee graduates this year, more than 30 of whom came from Meheba.

He further revealed that nine of the 12 founders of Hope Beyond Borders Initiative were former pupils of Meheba Secondary School.

Mr Matanda said the organisation, which is a legally registered refugee-youth-led initiative had so far helped 25 young people secure scholarships, including four in Kenya.

He explained that the organisation supports young people through mentorship and scholarship guidance, helping them identify educational opportunities and prepare applications.

Mr Matanda also urged the graduands to acquire digital skills and embrace emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to remain relevant in a rapidly changing world.

He encouraged them to build meaningful relationships with mentors, teachers and professionals, saying guidance and networking could open doors to new opportunities.

And Meheba Boarding Secondary School Headteacher Musanya Musanya expressed gratitude to parents, teachers and other stakeholders for supporting the graduating learners throughout their five years at the institution.

Mr Musanya wished the graduands success in their examinations and urged parents to continue encouraging and supporting them as they pursue their future ambitions.

He said the graduation marked an important milestone in the learners’ academic journey and called on them to remain focused on achieving their dreams.

The ceremony brought together school administrators, parents, teachers, education officials and other stakeholders to celebrate the achievements of the Class of 2026.

The Parent-Teacher Association Chairperson Japhet Bunda Bunda thanked parents and stakeholders for their continued support towards the school’s development.

He also encouraged them to remain disciplined and focused.

World.title: Mining companies urged to uphold human rights
World.content:
Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge has urged mining companies to uphold human rights as they are a pillar of sustainable business and harmonious relations with local communities.

Ms Mibenge said mining companies should recognise that respecting human rights is not merely a legal obligation but an essential foundation for responsible business operations and long term development.

She was speaking during a Business and Human Rights engagement for mining companies in Serenje District in Central Province.

Ms Mibenge said mining firms have a responsibility to ensure that their operations respect the rights and welfare of the communities in which they operate.

She further urged mining companies to contribute to the Grow Zambia Agenda by adopting responsible business practices that promote local employment, skills development and economic opportunities for surrounding communities.

Ms Mibenge said respect for human rights, coupled with fair labour practices and meaningful community engagement, could help create an enabling environment for inclusive economic growth and sustainable livelihoods.

She also called on mining companies to strengthen their corporate social responsibility initiatives by responding to community priorities, particularly in education, health, water and sanitation, skills development and employment creation.

The District Commissioner further urged stakeholders to work closely with mining companies to monitor the social and environmental impacts of mining activities, resolve disputes and safeguard vulnerable groups within communities.

She said sustained collaboration among government, mining companies and local communities was essential to ensuring that mining activities contribute meaningfully to national development while protecting the rights and interests of affected communities.

World.title: ECZ trains election poll staff in Sioma
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has urged poll staff for the Mbeta Ward by-election in Sioma District in Western Province to uphold integrity, impartiality and professionalism as they prepare to conduct Ward by Elections on November 5, 2026.

Speaking when he officiated at the training of poll staff in Sioma district, ECZ Commissioner, McDonald Chipenzi expressed gratitude to the officers, most of whom served during the 2026 general election, for their dedication and commitment to duty.

Mr Chipenzi noted that Sioma district did not record any election petition at parliamentary or local level following the recent elections, saying this demonstrated that the team in the district did a good job.

He also commended District Election Trainers for equipping the poll staff with the essential skills, competencies and confidence required to effectively discharge their duties.

Mr Chipenzi said the Commission attaches great importance to every election it conducts, including ward by-elections, regardless of their scale or geographical scope, which necessitated the delegation of a Commission member to provide leadership, oversight and support throughout the Mbeta Ward by-election process.

He disclosed that apart from Mbeta Ward, other local government by-elections will be held on the same day, with pre-poll activities taking place simultaneously in Mukabi and Nkongwe wards in Chipili District, Lwingwishi Ward in Mansa District, Lubaleshi Ward in Kanchibiya District and Nachikufu Ward in Mpika District.

Mr Chipenzi urged the poll staff to participate actively in the training, familiarise themselves with the electoral code of conduct and their terms of reference so that they do not commit electoral offences or fall prey to intimidation.

He reminded them to remain non-partisan and impartial, saying elections are a mammoth task that calls for total dedication and sacrifice to ensure the Commission conducts credible elections.

And Provincial Election Officer, Nixon Nkwapu urged the participants to attend the training with the seriousness it deserves, saying the expectations of electorates and stakeholders are always increasing and that the exercise was not a formality.

Meanwhile, one of the poll staff, Chinyama Mufaya has thanked the Commission for the training saying it would build their capacity to conduct the by-election in a fair and transparent manner.

The Mbeta Ward by-election was necessitated after the Commission postponed the local government election for the ward to call for fresh nominations of one candidate.

The poll will be contested by Situmbeko Yuyi of the United Party for National Development (UPND) and independent candidate, Mwanamwalye Mwanamwalye.

World.title: Chadiza Police investigate defilement case involving 15 year old girl
World.content:
Police in Chadiza are investigating a case of defilement involving a 15-year-old girl of Chief Mulolo’s area in Chadiza District in Eastern Province.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer, Robertson Mweemba has confirmed the development to the media.

Mr Mweemba said the matter was reported to Chadiza Police Station on October 29, 2026 by the victim’s 65-year-old grandmother.

“Brief facts of the matter are that on October 29, 2026 around 22:00 hours, the complainant and her family were outside their house chatting when the suspect identified as Jackson Banda joined them,” he said.

He said other family members later got tired and went inside the house.

The grandmother however, later noticed that the girl was missing.

He said family members started searching for her and after some time she returned home and disclosed what had happened after being questioned.

“The matter was then reported to police, a medical report form was issued and a docket opened,” Mr Mweemba said.

“Investigations into the matter have been instituted and no arrest has been made yet,” he added.

World.title: Kaoma launches Presidential Irrigation Initiative Programme
World.content:
Kaoma Secondary School has launched the pilot Presidential Irrigation Initiative Programme in Kaoma District in Western Province, a key component of the Grow Zambia Agenda aimed at enhancing national food security.

The launch marks the beginning of a programme that will see five schools in Kaoma district each cultivate one hectare of maize.

This is part of 35 schools selected across Western Province to participate in the initiative, which is aligned with President Hakainde Hichilema’s directive to produce 10 million metric tons of maize by 2030.

Officiating at the launch held at Kaoma Secondary School, Kaoma District Commissioner, Kashina Sheba described the initiative as a game changer for both education and agriculture.

Mrs Sheba said the programme will transform schools into centres of agricultural production and climate-resilient learning, while also equipping learners with practical farming skills.

She however expressed disappointment over reports that some schools in other parts of the country had abused agricultural inputs given to them under similar programmes.

“I was disappointed to learn that some schools abused the inputs. I pray that nothing of that nature happens in Kaoma,” Mrs Sheba said.

She added that the project will provide an alternative livelihood pathway for learners who may not excel academically, enabling them to venture into agriculture to sustain their livelihoods.

Meanwhile, Kaoma District Education Board Secretary, Dickson Pola said the programme will significantly boost the schools’ feeding programme and ensure learners are well-nourished.

Mr Pola said the initiative is also in line with the new competency and performance-based curriculum which emphasizes practical skills and entrepreneurship.

And Senior Education Officer, Foster Mwanza advised learners not to view the programme as punishment, but as a patriotic contribution to the national food basket.

He said through irrigation farming, schools will be cushioned against erratic rainfall while inculcating a culture of hard work among learners.

And Kaoma Secondary School Head Girl, Tricia Kampapa commended President Hakainde Hichilema for the life changing initiative and assured the government of pupils’ commitment to taking care of the maize field.

The one-hectare per school model is expected to contribute to household and national food security while promoting self-reliance in schools.

World.title: Senior Chief Nalubamba calls for support for traditional seed
World.content:
Senior Chief Shimumbo Nalubamba of Namwala District in Southern Province has called on the Government to strengthen support for traditional seed systems and promote crop diversification to enhance food security and build resilience against climate change.

Speaking on Day Two of the Zambia Traditional Seed and Food Festival in Lusaka, Senior Chief Nalubamba said Zambia could not continue relying heavily on maize production, especially amid increasingly unpredictable rainfall patterns and the possibility of El Niño-related disruptions during the 2026/2027 farming season.

Senior Chief Nalubamba said traditional crops such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas and cassava could help households withstand climate shocks while improving nutrition and creating economic opportunities.

He said although maize remained important to national food security and household incomes, dependence on a single crop exposed farming households to unnecessary risks.

“Maize alone cannot guarantee food security, particularly under the increasingly unpredictable rainfall that we are experiencing as a country,” Senior Chief Nalubamba said.

He explained that previous generations practiced crop diversification by growing different crops in the same fields, including cowpeas, maize and traditional varieties, which helped families maintain alternative food sources when one crop failed.

Senior Chief Nalubamba said traditional seeds should not only be preserved because of their historical importance but also researched, improved, multiplied, marketed and consumed to make them economically viable.

“We must not preserve traditional seeds simply because they are traditional, we must preserve and improve them because they have a practical value for us today and they have a practical value for us tomorrow,” he said.

Senior Chief Nalubamba further called for greater investment in women farmers, noting that women played a central role in food production, seed preservation, household nutrition and agricultural marketing.

He said recognition of women’s contribution to agriculture should be accompanied by improved access to land, finance, irrigation, technology and markets.

Senior Chief Nalubamba urged traditional leaders to examine practices within their communities that could prevent women and young people from accessing productive land and participating in agricultural decision-making.

He said the 2026 International Year of the Woman Farmer should result in stronger women-led farming organisations, improved access to productive resources and the growth of rural businesses.

“A woman farmer should not only be recognised for preserving cowpea seeds. She should also have the opportunity to process, package and sell cowpeas profitably, and that is to the biggest buyer, who is Government in this case,” he said.

Senior Chief Nalubamba also called for increased investment in agroecological practices such as crop rotation, intercropping, composting, mulching, agroforestry and responsible water management to address soil degradation and environmental challenges.

He said the Government and other stakeholders should strengthen local seed systems and combine traditional farming knowledge with scientific research and modern agricultural technologies.

He further called for policies and reliable markets that would enable farmers and rural entrepreneurs to process and add value to traditional crops such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas and cassava.

He proposed supporting women’s cooperatives and young entrepreneurs to establish businesses in food processing, seed multiplication, storage, transportation and agricultural technologies.

Senior Chief Nalubamba also urged the Government to address market barriers affecting traditional crops, citing the Food Reserve Agency’s limited purchasing of certain maize varieties, including yellow and orange maize.

Meanwhile, Women farmers have called on the Government to strengthen policies that protect traditional seeds and increase investment in agroecology to promote sustainable agriculture and strengthen food security in Zambia.

Maureen Sichinga, an agroecological farmer from Lusangazi District in Eastern Province, whose farm is under Chief Nyampande’s Royal Establishment, said traditional seeds remained important in preserving the country’s agricultural heritage, improving nutrition and helping farmers adapt to climate change.

“Today I stand before you as a woman farmer, but I also stand on behalf of many women farmers across Zambia, those whose hands work the soil, whose knowledge preserves our traditional seeds and whose determination keeps food on our tables,” Mrs Sichinga said.

She said traditional farming knowledge has helped communities survive difficult seasons because women understood which crops performed well in their soils and which seeds could withstand challenging weather conditions.

Mrs Sichinga noted that the 2023/2024 drought had exposed the vulnerability of households that depended heavily on maize and synthetic agricultural inputs.

She encouraged farmers to diversify their crops by growing traditional varieties such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas, cassava and sweet potatoes, alongside indigenous fruits and vegetables.

“Traditional seeds are not seeds of the past. They are seeds for our future,” she said.

Mrs Sichinga said women are already adopting sustainable agricultural practices such as intercropping, composting, mulching, water conservation, rainwater harvesting and agroforestry.

She added that women farmers are also preserving traditional seeds through farmer-managed seed systems and community seed banks to reduce dependence on expensive external agricultural inputs.

“For us, agroecology is not simply a concept discussed at meetings. It is about how we grow our food, care for the land, protect our seeds and sustain our families,” she said.

Mrs Sichinga outlined key messages for Government and other stakeholders, including the protection of farmers’ rights, increased investment in agroecology, improved access to productive resources for women farmers and greater participation of farmers in agricultural decision-making.

She further called for policies that would allow farmers to conserve, use, exchange and sell traditional seeds alongside conventional seed systems.

She urged Government to invest in soil restoration, water harvesting, small-scale irrigation, integrated pest and disease management, farmer-to-farmer learning, community seed banks and agricultural research that responds to the needs of smallholder farmers.

Mrs Sichinga also called for a ban on highly hazardous pesticides, herbicides and other chemicals, citing concerns over their effects on human health and the environment.

She welcomed the development of Zambia’s National Agroecology Strategy and called for its validation and effective implementation, with farmers meaningfully involved at every stage.

She further stressed the need to improve women’s access to land, finance, appropriate technologies, agricultural extension services and markets.

World.title: November 5 by election ballot papers not yet in- ECZ
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has announced that the consignment of ballot papers for the November 5th, 2026 by-elections have not arrived in the country, as scheduled.

ECZ Chief Electoral Officer, Brown Kasaro says the ballot papers were expected to arrive at 14:30 hours on Friday, October 30, 2026, aboard an Emirates flight.

Mr Kasaro explained that ECZ was, however, informed that the consignment was not aboard the expected flight, contrary to the information contained in the Air Waybill earlier shared.

In a statement Issued to ZANIS in Lusaka, Mr Kasaro assured that the Commission is currently engaging the printer, Al Ghurair Printing and Publishing, and Emirates Airline to establish what transpired and ascertain the status and expected arrival of the consignment.

Mr Kasaro also stressed that the Commission is treating the matter with urgency and will provide further updates as soon as verified information becomes available.

He further announced that the verification exercise which was earlier scheduled for today, Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 09:00 hours at ECZ Head Office will be subject to confirmation following clarification of the consignment’s arrival.

“The Commission appreciates the patience and understanding of all stakeholders,’’ Mr Kasaro said.

MINES and Mining Development Deputy minister Fred Moyo has called for a baseline study across Zimbabwe’s mining sector to establish whether mines have adequate ventilation personnel and whether the profession is given sufficient priority in organisational structures.

Moyo said the proposed study should cover different classes of mines and establish where ventilation departments are positioned within their management structures.

“I have demanded that they go in and do the baseline study.

Zimbabwe’s manufacturing capacity utilisation rose to 63.2% by the end of the third quarter of 2026, up from 57% in 2025, Industry and Commerce minister Mangaliso Ndlovu has said.

Ndlovu said capacity utilisation had increased to 61.

World.content:
AS Zimbabwe advances towards its Vision 2030 goal of becoming an empowered upper-middle-income economy, human capital development and industrial modernisation remain critical national priorities.

The Presidential Programme for Professionals (PP4P) is mobilising professional expertise to support these objectives by strengthening leadership, building capacity and bridging the gap between policy and implementation.

Through strategic cooperation with China, PP4P is advancing knowledge exchange in governance, vocational education, technical skills development and industrial transformation.

World.title: D-Day for Hwange, Chinhoyi illegal traders
World.content:
THE Hwange Local Board and the Municipality of Chinhoyi have given illegal traders operating in the two local authorities to cease operations and demolish their structures by Friday or face heavy penalties.

The impending blitz is aimed at restoring order and cleanliness across in urban areas, targets widespread illegal developments, roadside businesses, and vending stalls that have mushroomed at undesignated sites.

The operation is also targeting motor vehicle mechanics operating on public spaces, illegally- parked vehicles, abandoned vehicle shells, and buildings erected without approved municipal plans.

World.title: Government orders councils to prioritise workers’ welfare, service delivery
World.content:
Government has ordered all local authorities with outstanding salary arrears to prioritise settling their obligations to employees, or risk restrictions on foreign travel, workshops outside their jurisdictions, and purchase of vehicles for personal use.

The directive, contained in Local Authorities Circular Number 9 of 2026, dated October 20, underscores growing concern over the accumulation of salary arrears running into several months at some local authorities.

Issued by the Ministry of Local Government and Public Works, the circular describes the situation as unacceptable, citing its negative impact on employees’ welfare and livelihoods, staff morale, productivity and the capacity of councils to deliver essential services.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi
World.content:
Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi.

A source said, "They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted."

He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026.

A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, "I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety."

He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay.

Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group.

"What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. Many people were killed in the attacks. Prior to the attacks, those who saw them moving along the River Niger banks had raised an alarm calling on residents of the communities along the area to vacate. Some left, but many others stayed behind," he said.

Daily Trust gathered that a few days before the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi attacks, suspected members of the Lakurawa group also attacked Lafagu and other communities in Boya area of Kaoje, killing the village head, Alhaji Saidu Mujeli, and six others before leaving the area through the River Niger bank to attack other communities in Besse and Shanga.

It was gathered that despite the establishment of an army battalion in Kaoje to curtail the activities of terrorists, attacks have continued.

Police confirm attacks

Speaking to our correspondent, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said "it's true that the attack happened but it did not happen in one day and not in one community. It started from the 22nd of this month. The casualties recorded was not in a single attack. They attacked many of the communities in the riverine area and that's why the figure of those killed rose to 12. A police inspector and 11 others were killed in the attacks."

He said members of the Lakurawa terrorists group had earlier attacked communities along the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi axis on 22nd of October, but security operatives repelled them. He said they later carried out attacks on the communities of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi on October 26 and 28.

"Although the joint security teams repelled the attacks, seven people unfortunately lost their lives, including a police inspector," he said.

He added that earlier, members of the Yan Sakai, had invaded Samanaji Market and killed Fulani traders.

"Our police tactical teams deployed by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Besse, responded promptly to restore peace and prevent further carnage. However, three Fulani people lost their lives, while a police inspector sustained injuries in the line of duty," he said.

The state police spokesman said a tactical team of the police had been deployed to the troubled communities and normalcy is gradually returning to the area.

"The police have launched investigation into the attack and is following up on the attackers," he said.

'Attacks sign of frustration'

A security expert, who retired as a Captain in the Nigerian Army, Shehu Abubakar, told our correspondent that the attacks carried out by suspected members of the Lakurawa group in some communities of Kebbi, is a sign of frustration.

"You should understand that a battalion of the Nigerian Army was recently established at Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government to curtail activities of the bandits and Lakurawa, operating in the area. The Lakurawa must leave the area to find a convenient place as base to carry out their attacks. They carried out their attack on the communities along the River Niger bank while migrating to another area to avenge the presence of the army base at Kaoje.

"They can no longer stay close to the area where the battalion is located. They migrated from Kaoje, through the bank of the River Niger, moving through communities of Samanaji, Dutsinmari, Zaria Kalakala, to where they started their attacks at Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi. Now that they seem to have been displaced, the security agencies operating in the state should follow them up in every move they make so that they don't get a convenient place to settle. That way, they may be frustrated to move out of the state," he said.

Military bases in Kebbi

In the last two years, six Forward Operation Bases were established in Sakaba,Zuru,Yauri, Augie and Kaoje. The Battalion in Birnin Kebbi was upgraded to an Armoured Brigade, just as there is a battalion in Zuru.There are also army units in parts of Kaoje and other areas to strengthen military operations in the troubled communities of Augie, Danko Wasagu, Mahuta, Argungu, Arewa, Bagudo and Dandi, but the spate of killings occasioned by bandits and Lakurawa attacks remain a growing concern among residents.

Close 

Kebbi's killing fields

On Wednesday of last week, a large number of bandits invaded Dirin -Daji in Sakara Local Government Area of the state. It took the combined efforts of the security agencies in the area to disperse the attackers.

A week before the Kaoje district attack, three people were killed at Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of the state. The community was attacked by the bandits in the early hours of the day when people were preparing to go about their daily activities. A resident, Aminu Usman, said their attackers came in large number to invade the community and that they killed three people while many others escaped through the bush.

A few days before the attack at Kasabo, suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorists group attacked the site of the construction company handling the Badagry-Ilela Supper Highway project at Gubba in Maiyama Local Government Area of the state, killing two soldiers and a Chinese national. The attackers were said to have crossed into Kebbi from Kebbe area of Sokoto, to carry out the attack, it was gathered.

Efforts to get comments from the state government proved abortive, but a top government official who does not want his name in print told our corespondent that the state government was working closely with security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attacks.

He said, "Governor Nasir Idris has been up and doing on issues of security on the state. No fewer than 109 armoured vehicles and other logistics have been procured for security agencies to fight insecurity in the state."

World.title: Trump prosecutions under Biden set precedent for DOJ’s Alaska ‘Decoy Dan’ probe, ex-FEC chair says
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Justice Department is investigating allegations that Democratic operatives recruited Alaska Senate candidate Daniel J. Sullivan, dubbed "Decoy Dan," to siphon votes from Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan—prompting liberal-leaning election-law experts to accuse the Trump administration of federal overreach.

But former Federal Election Commission member Hans von Spakovsky argued that the Biden-era Justice Department’s prosecution of Donald Trump over alleged efforts to overturn the 2020 election laid the groundwork for the Alaska probe.

"The Justice Department has talked about a potential conspiracy to defraud the voters of Alaska and people are saying, 'Oh, he's got no case. That's a weak case,'" Spakovsky, senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom, told Fox News Digital. "Well, I suggest you do a Google search and pull up the indictment that Jack Smith got against Donald Trump in the District of Columbia. He set a precedent for this."

Joined by FBI officials and Alaska State Troopers, Alaska U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman announced at a Friday press conference that the Justice Department has been investigating whether Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired school teacher who will appear on the ballot without a party affiliation, was colluding with Democratic operatives tied to Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign.

The Justice Department previously sued Alaska election officials, seeking to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses re-election by fewer votes than those cast for Daniel J. Sullivan. The lawsuit was amended Friday to include reporting by The New York Times that the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and senior aides of Peltola's campaign allegedly worked to recruit candidates who could pull votes away from Sen. Sulllivan. Heyman mentioned the Times reporting repeatedly in the press conference.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

"We are taking that extremely seriously," Hetman said.

Sources at the Justice Department told Fox News Thursday that the Trump administration had issued more than 30 subpoeanas in a span of 24 hours as part of its criminal investigation into the alleged collusion, but Heyman did not say at the press conference what criminal charges are being pursued.

"I'm not making any assumptions on whether a crime has been committed or not," Heyman said. "That's why we are conducting that thorough investigation."

Von Spakovsky, a former Federal Election Commission commissioner, said potential indictments of Democratic operatives in the Alaska Senate race could rely on federal statutes similar to those Smith, the former special counsel, used in his 2023 indictment of Trump over alleged efforts to overturn the election.

Spakovsky pointed to charges of conspiracy to defraud the United States and conspiracy against rights. In Trump’s case, prosecutors alleged that he used fraud and deceit to obstruct the federal government’s process for certifying the 2020 election and conspired to deprive voters of having their lawful votes counted and honored.

Spakovsky said prosecutors could potentially apply similar theories in Alaska if they determine that Democratic operatives knowingly recruited Daniel J. Sullivan to confuse voters and divert votes from Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

ALASKA'S GOVERNOR ORDERS INVESTIGATION AFTER NYT REPORT ON ALLEGED DEM-LINKED SENATE ELECTION SCHEME

Smith's "indictment is basically along exactly those same lines, claiming that that Donald Trump was trying to defraud U.S. voters from fair and honest elections. So Jack Smith and Democrats, they set the precedent for the kind of investigation Justice Department is doing now."

Aubrey Wieber, executive director of 907 Initiative, a progressive advocacy group running critical ads against Sen. Sullivan, told Alaska Public Media that the press conference announcing the investigation "on the eve of the election" may be stemming from ulterior motives.

"One could say it appears that they are trying to interfere in an election and put their thumb on the scale," Wieber said.

The Justice Department's lawsuit was filed on Oct. 22, prompting a parade of condemnations from those who argued the federal government had "no authority" to intervene, with many pointing to the Alaska Supreme Court rejecting the state's push to disqualify Daniel J. Sullivan from appearing on the ballot.

GOVERNOR PROBING 'DECOY DAN' SULLIVAN ELECTION SCANDAL WARNS SYSTEM FLAW HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

"DOJ's theory: two candidates named Sullivan might confuse voters. The Alaska Supreme Court settled that in June and the ballot labels the incumbent. DOJ has no role in state election law," Omar Noureldin, senior vice president of policy and litigation at Common Cause of Common Cause, a self-described no-partisan watchdog organization.

Spakovsky called recruiting a candidate with the same name as a political opponent a "dirty trick," but said the recruitment itself was not necessarily a criminal violation. He said the legal analysis could change if operatives paid the candidate or provided services to help organize his campaign.

"The place you run into potential issues is not only if you just recruit a candidate, but you’re being paid to recruit that candidate, and you then provide services to help him run his campaign and organize it," Spakovsky said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Providing campaign assistance outside of being a volunteer is an in-kind contribution subject to federal reporting and contribution rules. Spakovsky said any failure to properly report such contributions could create a separate campaign-finance violation.

World.title: Maine school official raises Muslim religious objections to classroom dogs as district weighs policy changes
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Maine public school administrator raised concerns about allowing dogs in classrooms because of Islamic religious beliefs about the animals, as the district considers changes to its classroom pet policy following a teacher's request to foster puppies.

Dr. Abdullahi Ahmed, Portland Public Schools' assistant superintendent for student, family and community partnerships, discussed the concerns during an Oct. 14 policy committee meeting, explaining that some Islamic traditions consider dog saliva impure. Ahmed said he had consulted local Muslim religious leaders who opposed keeping dogs as classroom pets, according to a report by The National News Desk.

The debate began after a teacher at Ocean Avenue Elementary School sought permission to foster puppies in her classroom, giving students an opportunity to interact with the animals during reading and playtime. Ahmed suggested that accommodations could include keeping dogs in a separate room to respect students and families with religious objections.

ABDUL EL-SAYED'S ALLEGED FAMILY TIES TO MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD SURFACE AFTER DENYING ANY LINK DURING NBC INTERVIEW

Ahmed said that Muslim community members are not opposed to animals, saying, "in Islamic tradition, there is always the love for animals and living things and compassion for animals."

He went on to say that some Islamic traditions consider dogs unclean.

"So, with that being said, there are some ritual kind of a purity or in that Islamic traditions ... So, for example, the dog saliva is considered impure," Ahmed said. "And also some people had some experiences with dogs, which were negative actually in the past."

NEW YORK TIMES ACCUSED OF FRAMING MUSLIMS AS TRUE VICTIMS OF 9/11 IN ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE

Ahmed, who was born and raised in Somalia, speaks Somali, Arabic, English and Urdu, according to his district biography. He also said the imams he spoke with did not want dogs kept as pets in classrooms.

Committee members discussed whether any revised policy should apply only to dogs or extend to other classroom animals, along with potential opt-in and opt-out accommodations. The committee did not vote on policy changes during the Oct. 14 meeting.

World.title: Heidi Klum leads celebs with over-the-top couples' Halloween costumes through the years
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Couples' costumes on Halloween are always fan favorites, and even more so when it's a celebrity couple.

Heidi Klum and her husband look unrecognizable on the red carpet every year in head-to-toe prosthetics, while Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. have referenced iconic movies from the '80s in the past.

Here are some of the best couples' Halloween costumes from over the years.

Heidi Klum and Tom Kaulitz

The official Queen of Halloween always goes above and beyond for her annual Halloween party, and her husband, Tom Kaulitz, plays along each year.

At her party in 2025, the couple looked unrecognizable as they posed for photos on the red carpet. Klum dressed as the Greek mythological character, Medusa, while Kaulitz dressed as a warrior she had turned into stone.

The costume consisted of a full green prosthetic bodysuit with scales and a tail following behind her, with fake teeth and a crown of snakes on top of her head, which actually moved.

"I love for people to see this and think whatever they want to think for the first time when I go on the red carpet," she told Fox News Digital in 2024. "I never like to share it before, because then people are gonna be like, ‘Oh, it wasn’t as good as I thought it was gonna be.'"

In 2024, Klum and Kaulitz arrived to the annual Halloween party dressed as different versions of E.T. from the hit '80s movie, "E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial."

Kaulitz dressed as the more traditional version of E.T., while Klum dressed as the version of the character from when the kids in the movie try to disguise him, donning a black hat, blonde wig and red shawl.

"As a 9-year-old in Germany, E.T. introduced me to the idea that there’s life outside planet earth," she said on Instagram. "I know E.T. wanted to go home, but I hope that if the movie took place in 2024, that my favorite extra terrestrial would come to my party instead."

Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco

Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco were late for a very important date as they followed the white rabbit down the rabbit hole and into Wonderland for Halloween in 2024.

The couple dressed as Alice in Wonderland and the Mad Hatter, with Gomez wearing a whimsical blue dress with white socks and a blonde wig. Blanco wore black pants with a brown jacket and multicolored undershirt, paired with a big top hat and an orange wig, as he got into character with white face makeup.

"Curiouser and curiouser.." Gomez captioned the Instagram post.

Paris Hilton and Carter Reum

Paris Hilton channeled her inner Britney Spears when she dressed as the singer in her music video for "Toxic."

The 45-year-old media personality posed for photos at the Casamigos Halloween Party in 2023 in a futuristic blue flight attendant uniform, which she paired with metallic silver-heeled boots and sunglasses.

Reum was all smiles as he stood next to her donning an airline pilot uniform.

Kourtney Kardashian and Travis Barker

"I’m the ghost with the most, babe," Kourtney Kardashian captioned a 2023 Instagram post featuring her and Travis Barker in their ghoulish Halloween costumes.

The celebrity couple dressed up as Beetlejuice and Lydia Deetz at their wedding. Barker wore white makeup on his face with dark circles around his eyes, paired with green hair and a burgundy red suit, perfectly capturing the essence of the spirit.

Kardashian embodied his blushing bride in a red dress with a lace neckline and sleeves, and wore her hair in an intricate updo as she posed for the photo with a serious expression and holding a bouquet of roses.

Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber

Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber embraced their inner rock stars when they dressed as David Bowie and Debbie Harry at their Halloween party in 2018.

Gerber's costume consisted of black pants and a black shirt, which he paired with a Union Jack flag coat, a red and white scarf tied around his neck and a spiky orange mullet wig. He also painted a red lightning bolt over one of his eyes to emulate Bowie's alter ego, Ziggy Stardust.

Crawford, on the other hand, wore a yellow T-shirt dress over ripped-up black tights and knee-high heeled boots with a black belt around her waist and a red handbag. She styled her hair in a big blonde wig and wore heavy eye makeup.

Lisa Rinna and Harry Hamlin

One of reality TV's most iconic characters dressed up as one of TV's most legendary icons, when Lisa Rinna and her husband Harry Hamlin cosplayed Lucy and Ricky Ricardo from "I Love Lucy."

Rinna channeled the comedy legend with a red wig, over-the-top makeup, a blue dress with white polka dots and a white apron. She posed for photos by pursing her lips and putting her finger up to her mouth, mimicking Lucy's classic expression.

Hamlin stood next to her wearing a suit, and raised one eyebrow as he gave the camera a serious look.

Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.

After decades together, Freddie Prinze Jr. and Sarah Michelle Gellar have had some pretty iconic couples costumes.

In 2019, the couple dressed up as Doc Brown and Marty McFly from the hit 80s movie, "Back to the Future." They shared the costume on Instagram, captioning the post, "Great Scott!!!"

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The "She's All That" star wore a white jumpsuit, yellow hazmat gloves, a messy white wig with lab goggles as he posed next to Gellar, who wore jeans, a button-up shirt with denim sleeves and a red puffer vest. She accessorized with a skateboard to perfect the Marty McFly look.

The couple also recreated an iconic scene from the 1987 movie, "Dirty Dancing," choosing to dress up as characters Frances "Baby" Houseman and Johnny Castle.

In the photo, Gellar is wearing a cropped white button-up and capri denim shorts, as well as a curly short wig, as she crawled on her hands and knees towards Prinze, who was dressed as dance teacher Johnny Castle in black pants and a black tank top.

"Nobody puts baby in the corner #happyhalloween from Baby Houseman and Johnny Castle #dirtydancing #loverboy," she captioned the post.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Kelsea Ballerini and Chase Stokes

Former couple Kelsea Ballerini and Chase Stokes were hopelessly devoted to one another when they posed for photos together at Heidi Klum's Halloween party dressed as Danny Zuko and Sandy Olsson from the movie "Grease."

The country singer's take on the iconic character included tight leather pants, an off-the-shoulder black shirt and a leather jacket, which she paired with red high heels. She styled her hair in curls and a deep side part, and got into character with red lipstick.

Stokes played the part of a greaser effortlessly in an all-black outfit, including a leather jacket with "T-Birds" written across the back. He styled his hair with a curl in the front, and accessorized with a cigarette in his mouth.

World.title: How candy corn became a Halloween tradition, and why Americans still love to hate it
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Chances are high that candy corn is ending up in quite a few trick-or-treating baskets this Halloween, but the controversial confection has not always been associated with the spooky holiday.

The colorful treat has been around for more than 100 years.

It was invented in the 1880s in Philadelphia by George Renninger, an employee at Wunderle Candy Company, according to the National Confectioners Association in Washington, D.C.

HALLOWEEN CANDY FAVORITES COULD LEAVE ADULTS WITH CRACKED TEETH AND FAR WORSE, SAYS DENTIST

In keeping with a trend popular among confectioneries to make treats inspired by nature, candy corn was made to look like corn kernels.

It was initially marketed as faux chicken feed, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Candy corn’s unique layered tricolor design combined with a lack of automated machinery made for a difficult production process.

The treat became a seasonal item, with production beginning in late August and running through the fall, according to the National Confectioners Association.

CLICK HERE TO 

Around the turn of the 20th century, another candy company, Goelitz Confectionery (now Jelly Belly Candy Company) started selling candy corn.

Although the company didn’t invent the treat, it’s widely credited for producing the candy on a larger scale and marketing it as a Halloween product.

About 35 million pounds of candy corn are produced annually, according to Farmers’ Almanac, but it’s a notoriously polarizing item.

"It's the only other candy I would hope for aside from Reese's pieces if I was trick-or-treating," a candy corn fan said on Reddit.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Another person mentioned liking the treat, but said he or she "can only have a handful at most before the sweetness is overwhelming."

Another person on Reddit was fully against candy corn, saying, "It’s disgusting. Tastes like nothing or chalk and never sweet. Don’t like the texture. Don’t like the color."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Expanding beyond the grocery store aisle, earlier this fall Brach’s, a large producer of candy corn, released a non-edible variation of the treat.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The brand debuted a limited-edition perfume, called Ode to Candy Corn, which "smells just like the iconic treat tastes," per parent company Ferrara’s website.

World.title: Pizza delivery worker's heartbreaking reaction to cruel prank sparks $680K in donations
World.content:

A video of a Red Baron pizza worker who was confronted by a prankster while on the job has gone viral, sparking a huge outpouring of support for the man from strangers and his employer alike — with the company telling Fox News Digital it stands behind its employee.

A video that circulated online shows the worker, identified in a GoFundMe fundraiser as Walt Z., stocking frozen Red Baron pizzas in a Meijer grocery store in White Lake, Michigan, according to reports.

The prankster is shown coming up to Walt and asking him for the time.

Then, as Walt takes out his phone to check, the person plays a sound resembling an Apple Pay transaction and claims to have stolen $10 from him, thanking him and telling him he needs to buy something.

MAN SAYS TEXAS ROADHOUSE SERVED HIM $20 STEAK INSTEAD OF PRICIER FILET MULTIPLE TIMES

Walt initially says he plans to report the prankster and becomes increasingly upset as the person insists it was just a joke.

"My life is hard enough as it is," Walt tells the prankster.

He explains that he was already an hour late getting home, his children had already gone to bed without him and he would have to get up at 5 a.m. the next day for work.

He also mentions that he is struggling to pay his mortgage.

APPLEBEE'S CUSTOMER PUSHES BACK ON SUGGESTED TIP AFTER CHECKING THE MATH

"I don't need this in my life," he exclaims as others try to step in.

The footage went viral on social media this week as people bashed the prankster and rallied behind the struggling father of four for pushing back on the cruel joke.

"There’s a guy like him in every grocery store in America, grinding through the shift nobody sees," one X user wrote.

"Turning one of them into the punchline isn’t edgy. It’s lazy."

"God bless the working man," another commenter wrote.

CLICK HERE TO 

Fox News Digital attempted to reach Walt Z. and also reached out Red Baron.

As of Saturday, Oct. 31, a GoFundMe campaign had raised more than $679,000 from over 19,000 donations.

The fundraiser says donations will be sent directly to Walt.

Red Baron also publicly backed its employee after the video circulated.

The company posted on X, "He’s still here. He’s got a fan club. Including us," alongside a graphic announcing that "employee of the month nominations are closed. You know why" — suggesting that Walt might be selected for the honor.

Red Baron told Fox News Digital the incident took place in August and involved a member of its Direct Store Delivery team.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The company said it had checked on the employee’s well-being, continues to offer support and is working with retail partners to help maintain a safe and respectful workplace.

While internet users feared Walt could lose his job over his reaction to the incident, the company said, "We are pleased to share that he is doing well and remains a valued member of our team."

Red Baron added that Walt is grateful for the support but has requested privacy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

In an update posted to the fundraiser, Walt thanked those who donated, shared the campaign or sent messages of support.

He said he and his family are doing well and also asked that their privacy be respected.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I wanted to take a moment to personally thank everyone who has donated, shared this fundraiser, or left a kind message," Walt Z. wrote on the fundraiser page.

"The kindness and encouragement you've shown me and my family have meant more than I can put into words."

World.title: Tatum O'Neal steps out with family ahead of 63rd birthday years after near-fatal stroke
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Tatum O'Neal was recently spotted enjoying a day out with her family in Los Angeles.

The "Little Darlings" star was photographed at a fan convention with her family, wearing a black dress paired with a coat, glasses and layered necklaces. She styled her hair in an updo and walked outside the convention with the assistance of a cane.

O'Neal was accompanied by her daughter Emily McEnroe and son-in-law Tim Massarelli.

The sighting comes ahead of the actress' 63rd birthday on Nov. 5 and more than six years after she had a near-fatal stroke in May 2020 following an overdose on morphine, opiates and pain medication.

'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET 'DROPPED' AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES

In a July 2023 interview with People, O'Neal and her son, Kevin McEnroe, opened up about the health scare, with her son telling the outlet there were moments when he and his siblings, Sean and Emily "didn't think she was going to survive."

McEnroe shared that in addition to the stroke, O'Neal had multiple seizures and went into cardiac arrest. She spent six weeks in a coma.

O'Neal has struggled with drug addiction for decades, with McEnroe saying she "had become very isolated" during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, and had begun abusing medications, including some prescribed to her to treat neck and back pain and rheumatoid arthritis.

"She had become very isolated," he told People. "With the addition of morphine and heavier pharmaceuticals, it was getting scary. COVID, chronic pain, all these things led to a place of isolation. In that place, I don't think, for her, there was much hope."

O'Neal made her feature film debut in the 1973 movie, "Paper Moon," which she starred in alongside her famous father, Ryan O'Neal, at nine years old.

She went on to make history for her role in the film, as the youngest winner of a competitive Academy Award, when she took home the award for best supporting actress at the 46th Academy Awards in 1974, when she was 10 years old.

"All I really want to thank is my director Peter Bogdanovich and my father. Thank you," she said in her acceptance speech.

While she thanked her father in her speech, the two went on to have a turbulent relationship. In her 2004 autobiography, "A Paper Life," Tatum shared that their relationship first became rocky after making "Paper Moon," because he was jealous of her success.

In the book, she also alleged he physically and emotionally abused her, and said he was addicted to drugs.

Ryan O'Neal died in December 2023 at the age of 82 from congestive heart failure, and in a February 2025 interview with Variety, Tatum shared her reaction to being left out of his will, noting she only learned of the decision following his death.

"Keep it, motherf-----," she said. "The first book that I wrote was just a f---ing honest book. And that’s what got him."
