World.title: Bulgaria’s Presidential Race Heads to Runoff as Russia Divides the Two Candidates
World.content:
On Sunday, Bulgarian voters head to the polls again for the second round of geopolitically charged presidential elections.

In the first round on October 25, current acting President Iliana Iotova won 34.7 per cent to opposition candidate and former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov’s 31.9 per cent.

The elections were marked by record low turnout. The Central Election Committee reported that only 22.98 per cent of eligible voters cast a ballot.

Iotova and Gyurov are both running as independents, but they are supported by opposing factions and represent opposing foreign policy approaches and political alignments.

Iotova has been endorsed by the ruling party Progressive Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Socialist Party (which she is a former member of) and the nationalist party VMRO. Her potential victory would represent a consolidation of power by Progressive Bulgaria and Prime Minister Rumen Radev, whom Iotova served as vice president when he was president from 2017 to early 2026.

Gyurov has been supported by the pro-EU opposition parties Democratic Bulgaria and We Continue the Change, of which he was formerly a member. However, his campaign has tried to present him as independent of party dynamics.

During a TV debate on October 29, Iotova positioned herself as the candidate who can guarantee peace in the region and maintain more balanced diplomatic relations with Russia.

Among her criticisms of her opponent is that as interim Prime Minister, Gyurov signed a 10-year agreement with Ukrainian President Zelensky. She also disapproves of his past association with the party We Continue the Change, particularly the party’s work on gas diversification in 2022 after Russia’s Gazprom cut off supplies to Bulgaria.

The opposition has recently criticised Iotova for pardoning five people sentenced for drug dealing since 2022, at least one of whom was later arrested again for the same crime.

For both candidates 2026 brought major changes. Iotova became acting president after Rumen Radev stepped down and ran successfully in the April snap elections with his Progressive Bulgaria party. Before Radev took over as prime minister, Gyurov led the caretaker cabinet.

The presidential campaign coincided with increased drone attacks in the Black Sea which stoked public debate and divisions over the government’s reluctance to name Russia as the aggressor. Both Radev and Iotova remain elusive about Russia’s potential role in the security risks in the Black Sea region.

Shortly after the first round, the government was criticised for using official communication channels to promote Iotova and for domineering language directed at journalists who cover the elections. On October 30, the government issued a statement saying that the Central Election Committee found no wrongdoing but has deleted the Iotova-related posts if Gyurov’s team is “so sure this would help them in their campaign”, in an atypically ironic tone for an official statement.

Opposition figures have also accused Radev’s government of meddling with social media. Three popular satirical social media pages – often targeting political figures through memes and jokes but occasionally appearing supportive of Gyurov and the pro-EU opposition parties – were taken down and restored repeatedly.

World.title: Mourning Day Declared in Bosnia’s Brcko Following Deadly EUFOR Helicopter Crash
World.content:
The mayor of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s semi-autonomous administrative unit Brcko District, Sinisa Milic, declared a day of mourning on Friday following the deaths of four EUFOR personnel from the Italian armed forces.

The deaths occurred when a helicopter operated by the European Union Force in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR, crashed on Thursday during a routine operation near Brcko in northeastern Bosnia.

Milic said the victims were members of the force deployed to maintain peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

“This is a symbolic way of expressing solidarity with the victims’ families and the entire Italian people,” Milic said.

He emphasised that special recognition should go to the helicopter pilots, who tried to keep the aircraft airborne and prevent it from crashing into populated areas, thereby avoiding civilian casualties.

EUFOR confirmed on Thursday night that two of the four people killed in the helicopter crash were members of the Italian armed forces, while the other two belonged to the Italian Red Cross Military Corps.

Another 11 people were injured, all of whom are in stable condition, according to EUFOR. Two were transferred to the Tuzla Clinical Centre for treatment, while the remaining nine are receiving medical care in Brcko.

“EUFOR is deeply saddened by this tragic loss of life and extends its deepest condolences to the friends and family of those who lost their lives in the service of peace,” a EUFOR statement said.

Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto announced on Thursday that those killed in the crash were Sergeants Simone Ruggia and Claudio Marchesi of the Italian armed forces, and Lieutenant Franco Adriano Zecchillo and Sergeant Laura Procacci of the Italian Red Cross Volunteer Military Corps.

EUFOR reiterated its appeal to the public not to spread disinformation or speculate about the circumstances of the crash, urging the public to rely exclusively on official sources for information.

They reported that no civilian infrastructure, property or vehicles were damaged in the incident and that no civilians were injured, adding that the investigation into the accident is currently ongoing.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her condolences, saying the news had caused deep sorrow.

“The news of the tragic crash of an Italian EUFOR helicopter in Bosnia and Herzegovina is a cause of deep sorrow. My thoughts are with the victims, their families and everyone involved in the mission to maintain peace and stability in the region who are now going through hours of uncertainty,” Meloni said.

The European Union Force in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR Althea, is an EU-led military operation established in 2004 to help maintain a safe and secure environment in the country.

Operating under a United Nations mandate, EUFOR supports the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement and is headquartered at Camp Butmir in Sarajevo. A total of 24 countries take part in the mission, including some non-EU countries, with the commanding structure rotating on an annual basis.

World.title: Moldova Steps Up Border Security Amid ‘Unprecedented’ Threats
World.content:
From airspace violations to cyber attacks, Russia’s war in Ukraine has confronted Moldova with “unprecedented” threats, forcing the country to upgrade its defences with new surveillance systems, drones and anti-drone technology, border police chief Ruslan Galusca has told BIRN.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Moldova has registered more than 100 drone incursions, 65 of which occurred this year.

In recent weeks, Russia has targeted border crossings between Ukraine and Moldova that it claims are being used to resupply the Ukrainian military despite Moldovan denials.

On October 5, one of Galusca’s officers was wounded in Russian drone strikes near the Palanca-Maiaki-Udobnoe crossing.

“The risk is real,” Galusca said in an interview.

World.title: New Ultra-Fast Chargers Put Into Operation on Croatian Motorways
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – New ultra-fast electric vehicle chargers have been put into operation on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, with some having power as strong as 400 kW.

Petrol has put into operation 18 new ultra-fast charging points for electric vehicles on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, among which are six charging points with a power of 400 kW intended for heavy electric trucks. Poslovni reports that the new connections have been installed at the Janjče west, Dragalić south, Dragalić north and Desinec north rest areas, the company announced. This therefore expands the network of charging stations on important transport routes towards the Adriatic and on the motorway that connects Slavonia with Zagreb.

there are now 70+ ultra-fast connections across croatia

During the summer, Petrol already opened new ultra-fast charging stations at the Vrata Jadrana north and south and Dragalić north rest areas, and the latest investment also includes infrastructure for electric freight vehicles. The company now has more than 300 charging points for electric vehicles dotted all over Croatia, of which more than 70 are ultra-fast. At the regional level its network covers approximately 1,300 connections. Particularly significant is the installation of 400 kW charging points for electric trucks, which due to the large capacity of their batteries require more powerful infrastructure than passenger cars.

Nevertheless, the actual charging speed depends on the capabilities of the vehicle, the state of charge of the battery and other conditions, so the nominal power of the charger does not mean that every vehicle will be able to charge the battery at a power of 400 kW.

eu cash helped to expand the network

The new charging stations are part of Petrol’s OneCharge network and the European CROSS-E project, which is co-financed with European Union funds through the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF). The project includes the development of infrastructure for ultra-fast charging of passenger cars and electric trucks on important transport routes in Croatia and in neighbouring Slovenia. Within the scope of this particular project, Petrol plans to install a total of 98 charging points at 22 locations in the two countries. Part of the infrastructure will be intended for electric freight vehicles.

These considerable investments are also linked to the European Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), with which the European Union is gradually introducing requirements for the availability of charging stations on the main transport corridors. The overarching goal is to facilitate travel by electric cars on longer routes, reduce the need for detours for charging and enable the development of electric freight traffic.

World.title: Croatian Railway Projects Totalling €1.7 Billion Are Now Underway
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Croatian railway projects totalling €1.7 billion are currently underway as part of a major investment cycle.

The Croatian railway network is currently in the middle of a major investment cycle. Index reports that large projects worth €1.7 billion are underway, and by 2035 additional investments of around six billion euros are planned. The goal of the modernisation is to ensure faster, safer and more reliable transport of passengers and freight and to strengthen the competitiveness of Croatian ports.

State Secretary in the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Žarko Tušek, member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić and professor from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences Mladen Nikšić spoke on HRT about the current projects, traffic safety and the deadlines for the first results. State Secretary Žarko Tušek emphasised that the modernisation of the railway is a continuation of major investments in transport infrastructure, after road, maritime and air transport. “It is the turn of the railway, without which there is no development of the economy, port capacities, logistics, rural areas and regional transport,” Tušek said.

a lowland railway to rijeka

He noted that projects worth more than a billion euros have been completed, and almost 700 million euros have been invested in the maintenance of the sector in the last eight years alone. “The value of active, contracted projects currently amounts to €1.7 billion,” he said. Among the largest projects are the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth 900 million euros, and the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section of 350 million euros. Investments are also being made in the Podravina and Istrian railways and the Zadar – Knin railway, while the Vukovar – Vinkovci section has been completed. Long-term plans envisage investment of another around six billion euros by 2035, and the modernisation of the entire 2,600-kilometre network will continue after that as well. As a key future project Tušek singled out the lowland railway towards Rijeka, estimated at around five billion euros.

the dugo selo-novska railway is becoming double-track

“Just yesterday we selected international consultants who will accompany us in the negotiation procedure so that within a year we can reach the conclusion of an Alliance contract for the construction of that major project,” he announced. Member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić said that the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth almost 900 million euros, will bring a significant step forward in the development of transport. “That section is the only one on the former tenth international corridor that has remained single-track. With the completion of the works we will have a double-track electrified railway from the border with Slovenia to the border with Serbia, with speeds of up to 160 kilometres per hour,” Ćužić explained. He compared the importance of the second track with road traffic, where an additional lane increases throughput. He emphasised that this will enable Croatia to reach the standards of modern European railways and ensure faster and safer travel.

croatia will need to wait a decade before it notices a difference

Professor Mladen Nikšić from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences believes that the current investments will bring significant improvements, especially after the completion of all projects. “I believe that we will have higher-quality railway traffic, shorter journey times and greater track capacity for the transport of passengers and freight. This will also make our ports more prominent,” Nikšić said. He assessed that the modernisation should significantly shorten journeys. “I believe that when those projects are completed, we will be able to reach Slavonski Brod or Vinkovci in two to two and a half hours, and we will travel faster towards Rijeka and the Adriatic cities as well.

That takes time, but I think the full effects will be visible in about ten years,” he said. Nikšić added that investments in infrastructure must be accompanied by better quality of transport, especially the punctuality and reliability of trains. “Work needs to be done on the quality of transport, punctuality and reliability. We also have new vehicles, and all of that together with a quality timetable must form a complete whole,” he said.

Professor Nikšić also commented on recent railway accidents in Croatia. He pointed out that the causes can be divided into two groups: non-compliance with procedures and problems in communication, and shortcomings in vehicle maintenance. “The number of freight train accidents on the Rijeka railway is particularly worrying.

With the liberalisation of freight traffic the state has lost part of its influence on the maintenance and control of vehicles,” he warned. He believes that the Railway Traffic Safety Agency should intensify extraordinary and unannounced inspections, and that for the prevention of human errors the key are the education of employees and compliance with procedures. “Administratively everything can be in order, but vehicles can be better or worse maintained. Work must certainly be done on that,” he emphasised. Marijan Ćužić from HŽ Infrastructure said that preliminary checks of recent accidents have not shown irregularities on the infrastructure, but that investigations are still ongoing.

the rijeka railway can’t deal with all the freight

“Our first preliminary investigations have shown that there was no error on the infrastructure. The railway systems, including tracks and switches, are correct,” Ćužić said. He added that the education and communication of all participants in railway traffic need to be improved in order to reduce the risk of accidents. Žarko Tušek emphasised that investments in the railway have a key role in strengthening the competitiveness of Croatian ports. As an example he cited Rijeka, whose traffic is growing, but the existing railway cannot accept all the freight, so it ends up on the roads. Marijan Ćužić continued and explained that the construction of the second track will enable significantly greater freight transport. “We calculate that with the new railway we will be able to transport to Europe all the additional quantities of freight that the Port of Rijeka plans in the next ten years or so,” he stated.

could rijeka become a bigger logistics centre than trieste and koper?

Mladen Nikšić believes that along with Rijeka it is also necessary to develop the Dalmatian ports, modernise the Lika railway and better connect Zadar, Šibenik and Split. He also warned that the future lowland railway towards Rijeka will require additional port capacities.

“When the lowland railway is built, its capacity will be 30 million tonnes, which Rijeka alone will not be able to generate. That is why we already need to think about a new port on Krk, a railway connection and a new bridge that would connect the island with the mainland,” Nikšić said. Tušek confirmed that the lowland railway, a new terminal on Krk and a large freight centre in Zagreb are part of the Government’s strategic plans. “Krk is not any fantasy, but a project that needs to start being elaborated urgently. Its potential is such that Rijeka could become a stronger logistics centre than Koper and Trieste together,” Tušek concluded.

When asked when the general public and the economy will feel concrete benefits, Marijan Ćužić replied that the first results will be visible in two to three years, and that the Croatian railway in the next decade should reach the European level. “The first advances will be seen on the section from Zagreb to the Hungarian border, but also on the railways in Istria, in the Knin and Zadar area and on the Podravina main line. Already in a relatively short time our users will be able to use the advantages of a modern railway,” he concluded.

World.title: Meet The Croatian City With a Monument Not to a King, But to a Frog
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – There’s a central Croatian city which was once home to a monument dedicated not to a nobleman or a king, but to a frog.

Rulers and historical warriors are the most common monuments you’ll see dotted all over Croatia. A contemplative artist, statesman, writer or philosopher is also not a rarity. Nor is the one and only Nikola Tesla. Women are also found across the country, including the legendary Mila Gojsalić high in the mountains above Omiš. As Lana Mindoljevic writes for Putni kofer, however, you won’t often notice monuments to animals. That is, of course, unless they’re being ridden by some hero into battle. In Karlovac, one of the best-known monuments was for a long time the one dedicated not to a brave horse or dog, but to a frog. The small bronze resident of the city on four rivers stood for years at the entrance to the city’s so-called Promenade.

croatia’s only frog monument

The frog monument was unveiled in March 2008 and until 2024 stood at the intersection of Stjepan Radić Street and Dr. Franjo Tuđman Promenade, better known as the Promenade. Until 2022 it was the only frog monument in Croatia, but then one was also placed in Zmijavci near Imotski. Unfortunately, you cannot see the Karlovac frog anymore. It was removed during the renovation of Radić Street, when it was taken for safekeeping to the warehouse of the Public Fire Brigade of Karlovac. It never returned to its old location. When relocating it, the city announced that it would find a new location for it, because the old one had proved non-functional; it obstructed, they say, the passage and the organisation of events on that Promenade. But the works have been completed, and the Karlovac frog has still not received a new place.

The monument to the frog was unveiled on the 31st of March 2008, and it was made by the academic sculptor Stjepan Gračan. It was donated to Karlovac by the City of Zagreb on the initiative of Zvonimir Bešker, a Karlovac native who worked in the Zagreb city administration. It arrived in the city two years before it was placed, and in the meantime the best place for it was being sought; even placement on the wall of the city magistrate was considered. In the end a location accessible to passers-by and children was chosen, for whom it was believed they would rejoice most in the new attraction.

a monument to the frog catchers of karlovac

The Karlovac frog was chosen because of the old nickname of the people of Karlovac: the inhabitants of the city on four rivers were once, namely, called frog-catchers (žabari). What was once a pejorative name, some of the inhabitants over time accepted as part of their identity. While the frog was still standing in its place, a story also appeared that it brings luck: one was supposed to, allegedly, rub it behind the left eye and make a wish. Whether the firefighters today whisper their wishes to the frog or have already become so used to it that they don’t even notice it, we don’t know, but we believe that many more people would rejoice in it on some public surface.

World.title: Tourism Minister Welcomes Advent Price Caps Across Croatia
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Tourism Minister Tonči Glavina has stated that he more than welcomes advent price caps announced across Croatia, hoping for higher winter visitor figures.

The tourism minister stated that ” for any Advent to be successful, its most important component in terms of the structure of guests, in terms of revenue, in terms of hospitality and so on, is precisely domestic consumption,”

Index reports that he added that this type of consumption depends most on the citizens who live in the municipalities and cities that organise Advent fairs. He recalled that Poreč, Pula and Split have introduced price limitations for part of the Advent offer. He pointed out that the Split model provides for the determination of part of the prices already in the public call that regulates the relations between the city and the tenants of the Advent stalls. At the same time, prices are limited only for a smaller part of the hospitality offer.

“In this way, they’ve very clearly ensured the conditions that Advent and the hospitality offer at Advent are absolutely accessible to everyone,” Glavina said.

split caps its advent prices for the first time ever

It’s worth noting that this year, Split has introduced limitations on the prices of part of the food and drinks at Advent stalls for the very first time. According to the public call published by the city company Žnjan, a portion of fritule of at least 150 grams may cost a maximum of four euros, while a hot dog and sausage of at least 80 grams may cost a maximum of three euros. Mulled wine and hot chocolate, in a quantity of at least two decilitres, may cost a maximum of three euros. For the same quantity of tea hospitality providers will be able to charge a maximum of €2.50, while half a litre of water must not be more expensive than two euros.

The limitations apply to the seven listed products, and not to the entire offer. A novelty is also that the City of Split will for the first time, when selecting tenants, score the quality of their hospitality offer, and not only the offered rent. This year’s Advent in Split will last from the 27th of November to the 6th of January, and Advent stalls will be set up on the Riva, Prokurative, in Đardin and Stobreč.

pula also caps its advent prices

A similar decision was made by Pula, where fritule, pancakes and Christmas cookies may cost a maximum of three euros per portion. For mulled wine, hot chocolate and cocoa the maximum price will be three euros, and for a hot dog, hamburger and bakalar five euros. Tea and water will be able to cost a maximum of two euros. Nevertheless, the limitations do not mean that all products at Pula’s Advent stalls will have prescribed prices. Hospitality providers will have to offer at least one product at a limited price, depending on the type of offer, while they will be able to determine the prices of other products independently.

Such a model has already been applied for years in Poreč, and things will be no different throughout the upcoming festive period, either.

Glavina emphasised that Advent as a tourist product is very important for the development of year-round tourism and tourist results in the months of December and January. He stressed that this year the Croatian National Tourist Board is for the first time conducting a national campaign with all key domestic Advent destinations, directed towards the main markets from which tourists come to Croatia.

“We’re making that transition towards year-round tourism and it is very important for us to have good content and programmes, and I am sure, because of the good prices, that the number of visitors at Advent will perhaps be higher than ever before,” he concluded.

World.title: Advent in Split Caps Prices Ahead of Christmas Festivities
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Advent in Split has capped the prices of what it will sell during the upcoming Christmas festivities.

Ahead of the Christmas period and the different advent celebrations across Croatia, a new trend among local politicians is limiting prices for hospitality providers. The new city that has joined the wave is Split. Split hospitality providers who can apply for the tender for Advent stalls have been met with a limitation on the prices of food and drinks.

Poslovni reports that this new wave of price capping appeared after ever-increasing prices at Advent events across Croatia often caused dissatisfaction among visitors and locals alike. Split has therefore become the third city overall that has decided to introduce an upper limit on the prices of certain products. A hot-dog sold at Advent in Split will now cost a maximum of three euros, which is two euros less than up in Pula, which has also limited its own advent prices this year. Mulled wine in both of these cities will be available for a maximum of three euros, while fritule sold in Split will still be one euro more expensive than in Pula.

Poreč has otherwise been applying this model of price limitation for several years. The general public’s opinions on prices at festive events up and down Croatia are divided. While some believe that the offer often does not justify the amounts they have to pay, others point out that the entire Christmas period is an opportunity to enjoy the festive atmosphere, which is why prices are not always their primary concern.

World.title: How Much Do Tourists Spend in Croatia? Data Reveals Changing Habits
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – How much do tourists from abroad actually spend when they come to Croatia? The latest data on precisely this reveals just how much habits have altered.

The results of the national survey entitled “Attitudes and Expenditure of Tourists in Croatia – TOMAS Croatia 2025/2026” were presented at the Croatian National Tourist Board recently. Morski reports that this took place with the participation of the Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina, the director of the Croatian National Tourist Board Kristjan Staničić, the director of the Institute for Tourism Damir Krešić, members of the Tourist Council of the CNTB and various representatives of professional associations in tourism.

guests spend 15% more than they did in 2022

The research, conducted by the Institute for Tourism, covered 14,770 tourists across the whole of Croatia, and the results provide insight into the characteristics of tourist demand, expenditure, motives for arrival and guest satisfaction. One of the most important results is the growth in the average daily expenditure of tourists. On the Adriatic it reached €162 per person, which is 15 percent more than back in 2022, while in continental Croatia it amounts to €164, with a growth of 21 percent. At the same time, on the Adriatic an increase was also recorded in the share of expenditure on additional destination services, such as sports, cultural and entertainment content as well as excursions and local transport, which confirms the importance of a diverse offer in creating additional value of the tourist stay.

“Such research is important for understanding the profile of our guests, their expectations, expenditure and satisfaction with the tourist offer. Comparison with the previous research shows how tourists’ habits are changing and where we have the opportunity to further strengthen the competitiveness of Croatian tourism. This year’s results confirm to us that Croatia attracts guests who on average spend more, but also that their habits are changing. Our task is not only to increase tourist traffic, but to create greater value from every tourist arrival. That means strengthening the quality of the offer, encouraging longer stays, developing year-round tourism and better connecting accommodation with gastronomy, culture, sport and other content,” Glavina stated.

guests with deeper pockets are growing on the coast

A positive trend has also been recorded in the structure of Croatia’s guests. On the Adriatic the share of guests with higher purchasing power is growing, with 74 percent of tourists stating monthly household income higher than €4,000. At the same time, the share of foreign guests visiting Croatia for the first time increased from 14 percent in 2022 to 22 percent in 2025, while 60 percent of foreign guests have visited Croatia at least three times, which confirms a combination of the destination’s attractiveness to new guests and the loyalty of existing visitors.

“The results of the TOMAS research are an important basis for the further improvement of Croatian tourism and the quality direction of our promotional activities. In order to build competitive and sustainable tourism, it is important to understand who our guests are, what motivates them to come and what kind of experiences they are looking for. Exactly such research enables us to base our activities on concrete indicators and the real experiences of visitors. Our goal is to continue positioning Croatia as a safe, authentic and year-round destination that builds its competitiveness on the diversity of the offer, natural and cultural riches, hospitality and the quality of the overall experience,” Staničić said.

croatia still stands out

The results further show how Croatia stands out with the quality of the experience and an offer that attracts different profiles of guests. Among the elements with very high satisfaction ratings on the Adriatic, the beauty of the place and nature, personal safety, atmosphere and ambience stand out, while guests of continental Croatia particularly highly rate personal safety, the hospitality of the local population, the overall stay and the cultural and artistic offer. As many as 69 percent of guests of continental Croatia would almost certainly recommend the destination they visited, and on the Adriatic that share amounts to 58 percent.

World.title: Air Montenegro Introduces Zagreb Flights Three Times a Week
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Air Montenegro is planning to introduce Zagreb flights which will operate three times a week as of next month.

Air Montenegro plans to operate on the route between Podgorica and Zagreb within the framework of the Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme in Montenegro. According to information Croatian Aviation received, the planned flights are currently scheduled from the 24th of November this year with three rotations per week.

Air Montenegro has otherwise been given the opportunity to operate flights on several international routes within the Montenegrin Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme, and among them is the route that will connect Podgorica and Zagreb. The very first rotation is currently planned, as stated, for the 24th of November this year. The flights are scheduled on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays, which means a total of three weekly rotations until the end of the winter timetable. The airline is also expected to continue operating the flights in the summer timetable period next year, which is the period from the end of March to the end of October 2027.

The arrival of the aircraft from Podgorica at Zagreb Airport has been planned for early in the morning, just after 08:00, while departure of the aircraft from Zagreb towards Podgorica is planned at 08:50. Embraer E195 aircraft with a capacity of 118 seats in the carrier’s fleet are planned for operating the flights on this route. This means that Air Montenegro will offer a total of 12,508 seats between Podgorica and Zagreb this winter on the 53 announced rotations.

The introduction of this route within the PSO programme is otherwise important in scope for the connectivity of the two capitals and opens up an additional travel option for passengers between Croatia and Montenegro, between which there is currently no direct air route. Zagreb and Podgorica have potential for travel by different categories of passengers, from business and institutional to tourist and those travelling to visit family and friends.

Details about ticket sales, exact times of return flights and the final implementation of the schedule depend on the carrier’s announcement and official information for the winter timetable 2026/2027. It is expected that the carrier will release tickets for sale soon, and in the event of administrative difficulties, a postponement of the date of the first rotation is possible, but there is no doubt that the route will soon be in operation.

Previously, Ryanair operated on the route between Podgorica and Zagreb. The route was introduced back in September 2021, operated mainly twice a week, on Thursdays and Saturdays, with A320 aircraft with a capacity of up to 180 seats. The route was discontinued at the end of October 2023, and Ryanair justified that move by the increase in airport fees in the capital of Montenegro. Croatia Airlines also previously operated on this route, in the period from the end of June 2008 to the beginning of the summer timetable 2013, three times a week with Dash Q400 aircraft with a capacity of 76 seats. After more than three years without flights, Air Montenegro will soon reconnect the two capital cities.

World.title: Croatia Might See Some Snow Next Week as a Weather Change Looms
World.content:
October the 30th, 2026 – Croatia may see some snow next week as a dramatic weather change looms, bringing far colder temperatures and plenty of rain.

Over the next few days across Croatia, the weather will be predominantly cloudy and markedly cooler temperatures will prevail, with occasional rain. Index reports that on the Adriatic coast and the islands there will be more sunshine, but also very strong bura. According to the latest forecast issued by the Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ), a further deterioration of the weather is expected at the beginning of next week, and the first snow could fall in the highlands.

Over the weekend, the weather will be changeable, mostly cloudy inland, and in places rain will fall, especially in eastern and mountainous areas of Croatia. A weak to moderate northeasterly wind will blow, and on the Adriatic a moderate to strong bura, under Velebit with gale-force, in places even hurricane-force gusts. The highest daily temperature will range from 10 to 14 degrees inland and from 17 to 21 degrees on the Adriatic coast and the islands, DHMZ states. Inland, it will be predominantly cloudy, in places with a little rain, primarily in the east of the country and in mountainous Croatia. On the Adriatic it will be partly sunny, but still windy, with a moderate to strong bora, and under Velebit a gale-force bura wind. Morning temperatures will range from 4 to 8 degrees, and on the Adriatic from 10 to 15. During the day, 9 to 13 degrees are expected inland and 16 to 20 by the sea.

No major change in the weather is expected on Saturday. Inland clouds will prevail, and in places there will also be rain, especially in mountainous Croatia and in the east of the country. On the coast, there will be more sunny periods, but the bura will continue to blow, particularly strongly under Velebit. On Sunday, the 1st of November, more rain is expected in other parts of the interior as well. It will be cloudy and cooler, with a northerly and northeasterly wind that will occasionally be strong. The change in the weather will also affect Dalmatia, where along with more clouds local rain and showers are expected. Temperatures will gradually fall, and the highest daily values inland will be around 10 degrees. In the highland areas, snow is also possible on Sunday.

According to the DHMZ forecast, unstable and colder weather continues at the beginning of next week. On Monday, the 2nd of November, rain is expected in a large part of the interior, and temperatures will fall even further. DHMZ maps also show the possibility of snow in the higher areas of mountainous Croatia, especially on Monday and Tuesday. In some more mountainous areas a snow cover could also form, but this is a forecast several days ahead that can still change.

On Tuesday, cold and predominantly cloudy weather will continue, with occasional rain, while snow is still possible in the highlands. According to current forecasts, from Wednesday, the 4th of November, a gradual calming of the weather is expected. There will be less precipitation, and in places sunny periods will appear. Nevertheless, temperatures will remain relatively low and feel far colder, especially inland.

World.title: Prime minister: I will not remain silent about Russia
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said Russia is killing women and children and he will not hold back when speaking about the Russian threat, after reports that U.S. officials had asked the Baltics to tone down their statements.

Reuters news agency reported on Friday, citing several anonymous sources, that the US had asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia and reduce their emphasis on the threat posed by Russia in public statements

Michal said no requests have reached him.

"No such complaints have come directly to me. The last time we were together with Trump was in Ankara in the summer at the NATO summit, and the message from the Americans has rather been that European countries must take their own defense against the Russian threat seriously and put more money into defense, and Estonia is certainly doing that. We are rather a strong contributor to security and a security partner for the United States," he told ERR on Friday.

Estonia will continue to raise awareness about Russia's aggression and its crimes in Ukraine, the prime minister said.

"Even before Russia's full-scale aggression against Ukraine began, we warned about the plans and wishes of Russian dictator Putin. And we have continued to do so, and I will continue to do the same. I do not intend to hold back, because pleasing dictators or remaining silent is certainly not the solution. Rather, we must continue the pressure and support Ukraine – that is the only way to force Putin to change his objectives," Michal told ERR.

"Ahead of this winter, on Putin's orders, electricity infrastructure and heating infrastructure are currently being destroyed and bombed. Now the Russians have targeted water supplies and sewage systems. They are killing women and children. What words can European leaders even use to describe this? All words are too mild for this. The reason Putin is currently being portrayed as cornered is that there is no real progress on the battlefield, and therefore Putin is carrying out various hybrid attacks and essentially behaving like a terrorist. We certainly cannot, and I certainly do not intend to, soften my tone or remain silent about Russia," he continued.

"Who else, if not Estonia's leaders – the prime minister in public appearances or private conversations, or Estonian defense and security officials in various appearances or discussions – should directly describe what Russia is doing? As John McCain once said when he was a US presidential candidate, Russia is a gas station pretending to be a country, and today it is led by a dictator who kills women and children. And in my opinion, all words are indeed too mild to describe this," Michal added.

World.title: Police catch teenagers who deliberately left scooters on 70 km/h road
World.content:
Police have identified several young men who deliberately left electric scooters on a 70 km/h stretch of road near Keila, endangering people's lives. The company that owns the vehicles has temporarily suspended operations in the area.

Officers received a report in late September that an electric scooter was lying on the road near the Mudaaugu bus stop on Paldiski Highway, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) said on Saturday.

According to Hisko Vares, head of the investigation unit at Lääne-Harju Police Station, several reports of similar incidents were received over the course of the month. "Police have been informed on 10 occasions that an electric scooter had been left on the road. In one case, a car hit a scooter, but fortunately no one was injured," he said.

The head of the investigation unit said police officers gathered additional information from residents, but the investigation was complicated by the lack of surveillance cameras in the area. There were also no eyewitnesses, as far as police are aware.

"After extensive work, the perpetrators were identified as three young men aged 17, 18 and 24," Vares said.

He stress that deliberately leaving objects on the road is extremely dangerous. "The speed limit on this stretch of road is 70 km/h, and hitting an electric scooter in the dark at that speed could end extremely badly. The young men endangered other people through their actions, and it is only fortunate that no one was injured," Vares said.

The PPA has launched misdemeanor proceedings, during which all the precise circumstances will be established.

Company suspends scooter parking in the area

Hoog Mobility, the company that owns the electric scooters, told ERR it is aware of the incidents, is cooperating with police and has temporarily removed its electric scooters from the area.

"Yes, we are aware of these incidents and take them very seriously. These are not incorrectly parked scooters. The scooters were in a parking area and locked, but someone deliberately carried them from there onto the highway. This is vandalism that endangers the lives and health of drivers. Nothing like this has happened to us before, and the incidents have been confined to one area," said Drevor Rudnevs, Hoog Mobility management board member.

Several of the company's scooters have been damaged as a result of the incidents, but he did not say how extensive the damage was. "Scooters can be repaired or replaced, but a person's health cannot," Rudnevs added.

The board member said police are aware of the incidents and proceedings are ongoing: "As a precautionary measure, we have temporarily removed the parking areas in this region. We are grateful to local residents who have informed us of their observations"

World.title: Estonia faces a shortage of competent car repair specialists
World.content:
Car dealers are complaining that it is difficult to find good and knowledgeable specialists for repair workshops, and vocational school graduates do not fill the gaps.

Business owners say it is not easy to find competent employees for car repair workshops. While technicians and painters can still be found, the situation is much more complicated when it comes to good auto body repair specialists.

For example, in Pärnu there are five professional auto body repair specialists whom car repair workshops lure away from one another with higher pay.

"Those who have already trained and are specialists in this field really have to be searched for high and low. The young guys aren't there yet. Some are very skilled and learn the job very quickly, while for others it is exactly the opposite – somehow the profession just doesn't suit them," said Kristjan Lagern, head of Eurostauto's Pärnu dealership.

Every year, around 20 young prospective technicians start studying at Pärnu Vocational Education Center and recieve their education both in the garage and the classroom. They also learn about electric cars.

"Technology is constantly developing and everything is evolving, but the basics remain the same – a wheel is a wheel, a bearing is a bearing and an engine is an engine. It's just that more and more additional features and control systems are constantly being added. You have to be capable of learning or be diligent, because here we only learn the basics in three to four years, but you have to keep learning all the time," said Priit Auväärt, lead teacher of automotive studies at Pärnu Vocational Education Center (PARK).

But not every student has a passion for the automotive industry. Some are studying only because their parents tell them to.

Car sales company Amserv has spent years ensuring its workshops have a steady supply of enthusiastic specialists. The company supports automotive technology students at Pärnu Vocational Education Center with a scholarship. This year, the €750 scholarship was awarded for the seventh time.

"On the one hand, we certainly want to develop a new generation of employees for ourselves. On the other hand, we ourselves started out young, and this is a good opportunity to now give young people opportunities," said Ahti Aasala, head of aftersales at Amserv Group.

This time, the scholarship and an internship position went to Robin Mitt, a second-year automotive technician student, who has been interested in cars since childhood.

"With friends, there was already this kind of tinkering around with cars, and then I developed a desire and interest in it at home as well. Nowadays, all these cars are becoming full of electronics, and there are countless different electrical devices in them. You definitely need knowledge of the electrical side," Mitt said.

A modern automotive technician must be able to work under the hood, understand electronic devices and, ideally, know how to use TikTok to post informative clips for customers about problems with their cars.

World.title: Estonian border guards could be given additional powers to stop migrants
World.content:
Estonian border guards could be given additional powers to stop border violators, Minister of Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) has said, after meeting with his Latvian counterpart.

At a press conference at Estonia's Piusa border guard station on Friday, the ministers said measures need to be found to stop the Belarusian government from organizing illegal migration into the Baltic states.

The pressure is expected to fall over the winter, but is likely to pick up again next spring.

"One possibility is for all these countries to close their border crossing points with Belarus for a while, because Belarus is interested in maintaining this traffic, so perhaps that would get the message across, because in Poland's case it certainly worked," Taro said.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200). Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Latvian Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava said Latvia has amended its legislation so that border guards can respond more effectively to both border violations and damage to infrastructure.

"I think that if some of them reconsider the possibility of entering Latvian territory, we have given our border guards more opportunities to use weapons against those who illegally cross the border and attempt various actions against our technological infrastructure. So I think this also works as a preventive measure," he said.

Taro said Estonian border guards also need to be given additional powers.

"We should take into account that if people are operating in the border zone and it is not clear that they are our own people, then they are probably enemies, and in that case a border guard must have complete confidence that they can use all means to stop that hostile activity there, up to and including weapons, up to and including lethal force. We are currently analyzing how our legal framework deals with this, how much room for interpretation we have and whether anything needs to be changed," the Estonian minister said.

World.title: Estonian raw milk producer buys Latvia's largest dairy company
World.content:
As part of the transaction, Agrone Group, through its parent company, acquired a 100 percent stake in Food Union Management, which holds majority stakes in both Latvian dairy companies. The stake was purchased from the previous owner, Food Union Luxembourg Holdings II S.à r.l.

The transaction was completed following approval from the Estonian and Latvian competition authorities and was financed by SEB. The price will not be disclosed by agreement between the parties.

Agrone CEO Raul Jeets said the transaction was historic for the dairy industries of both countries.

"Rīgas piena kombināts is a company with almost a century of history, a strong market position and well-known and beloved brands throughout the Baltics, such as Kārums and Lakto. By combining Agrone's experience in raw milk production with Rīgas piena kombināts' expertise in milk processing, product development and sales, we will have a good foundation for increasing the entire group's business volumes, improving efficiency and strengthening competitiveness," he said.

Jeets said Agrone has been working for years to expand its operations from milk production into milk processing and new export markets.

Artūrs Čirjevskis, chairman of the management board of AS Rīgas piena kombināts, said the company's goal is to continue offering customers and consumers high-quality and tasty dairy products.

"We are pleased that the transaction has been completed. From now on, we are part of a strong Baltic dairy group that covers the entire dairy value chain. This has been our long-term ambition," he said.

Joosep Kadak, head of corporate banking at SEB, which financed the transaction, said that Agrone is a good example of how an agricultural company that has grown on Estonian capital is taking the next step toward becoming an integrated Baltic company.

The change of ownership will not initially bring any changes to the day-to-day operations of Rīgas piena kombināts or Valmieras piens, or to their relationships with employees, customers, raw milk suppliers and other partners.

Production and deliveries will continue as usual. As a next step, the management teams of Agrone and the Latvian companies will jointly develop a strategy for further development.

World.title: Young boys confess to vandalizing over 100 graves in Saaremaa
World.content:
Two young boys aged eight and 10 are responsible for vandalizing more than 100 graves at a cemetery on the island of Saaremaa over the weekend, newspaper Saarte Hääl reported .

One of the boy's parents shared a handwritten letter in the Kihelkonna community Facebook group in which the child apologizes for damaging the cemetery.

"I'm sorry for damaging the cemetery. And I regret it and I promise that I will never do it again," Saarte Hääl quoted the boy's letter as saying.

The children's parents and grandparents also addressed the community in the same group.

"As parents and grandparents, we are deeply sorry that our child has caused irreparable damage and heartache to the Kihelkonna community through his actions," they wrote.

The Prosecutor's Office, which is conducting a criminal investigation, confirmed to ERR that two boys under the age of 14 have been questioned in connection with the Kihelkonna Cemetery incident and that prosecutors believe they are involved in the incident.

A vandalized gravestone in Kihelkonna cemetery in Saaremaa. Autor/allikas: ERR

Rein Rand, head of the investigation group at Kuressaare Police Station, told ERR on Friday afternoon that criminal proceedings had been launched under the section of the Penal Code concerning desecration of the memory of the deceased.

Margus Saar, who has worked as a cemetery caretaker for 21 years, told "Aktuaalne kaamera" on Tuesday that this was the first time vandalism of this scale has occurred.

"Police have now established that 105 graves were affected. Gravestones have been broken – pushed over and then shattered. Expensive grave lanterns made of granite have had their glass smashed, and flowers have been damaged. I'm inclined to think that Sunday was the day it happened, and that it was young people. There are footprints suggesting that," Saar said.

Minna Raun, head of the district policing group at Kuressaare Police Station, said vandalism on this scale had not occurred before.

"The prescribed punishment for this is a fine or imprisonment. If minors are involved, the type of punishment remains exactly the same. Vandalism on this scale is indeed taking place for the first time," said Minna Raun, head of the district policing group at Kuressaare Police Station.

World.title: Is Estonia about to have a surplus of IT specialists?
World.content:
For years, Estonia has talked about a shortage of programmers and IT workers, but after a huge wave of layoffs this week, is there about to be a surplus instead?

One of Estonia's success stories, Pipedrive, announced on Thursday that most of the people working at the company would lose their jobs. However, the changes brought about by artificial intelligence in the labor market are only just beginning.

Microsoft recently offered voluntary severance packages to around 60,000 employees to cover the costs of AI and data centers. Amazon has cut around 30,000 office jobs in a year, while social media giant Meta has laid off 10 percent of its employees. The International Monetary Fund warned that AI would affect around 40 percent of jobs.

Telia, located next door to Pipedrive, recently announced the elimination of 100 jobs. Business is changing and AI is doing more and more.

"If I had to be an oracle, I would rather think that we will be able to do the same work with increasingly fewer people," said Telia CEO Andre Visse.

Young people have been hit hardest by the change. In Estonia, employment among under-25s working in IT has fallen by nearly a quarter in three years.

"Obviously, we are seeing these changes here, and it is considerably more difficult for young people to enter the labor market today than it perhaps was three years ago," said Urve Mets, head of research at OSKA.

However, Sergei Anikin, who years ago grew Pipedrive's engineering department from 10 people to more than 400, believes that young people are flexible and adopt new ways of working more quickly.

"If I compare young people who had no baggage with someone who, for example, has a stable job, a family and a mortgage, and then suddenly realizes that their skills are no longer actually needed because there is a machine that can do their work better and hundreds of times faster, then I think those people will find it considerably harder to cope with this situation," Anikin said.

Could Estonia soon find itself in a situation where there is no longer a shortage of programmers, but rather a surplus?

"If around 400-500 people are laid off from the sector at once, then that will certainly have an impact on the structure of the workforce, and unemployed people will appear on the market for some time. But I think that will correct itself quite quickly," Visse said.

One distinctive feature of Estonia is that IT specialists are concentrated narrowly in the IT sector, Visse said. AI could change that.

"There is actually quite considerable room for development in bringing more technologically knowledgeable, IT-savvy workers into other sectors and helping us digitalize the entire economy and automate these processes more quickly," Visse said.

There will also be high demand for technology skills in the future, but simply writing code will no longer be enough, Mets said.

"IT knowledge alone is not enough, meaning that every young person could think a little about whether, for example, they see their future work as being more connected to technology in the medical field or perhaps in the industrial sector," Mets said.

Whereas good ideas previously went unrealized because there were not enough people to implement them, AI has eliminated that bottleneck, Anikin said.

"We joke here that no stupid idea will go unrealized, so what will actually become important is the ability to distinguish stupid ideas from good ones," Anikin said.

World.title: 8 migrants detained in Tallinn's Mustamäe
World.content:
Police apprehended eight illegal immigrants in Tallinn's Mustamäe district on Friday. Two men were taken to hospital, while the remaining six were taken directly to a detention center.

Almost 400 migrants have been detained by the police since July in Estonia after a surge in illegal crossings at the Latvian-Belarusian border. Estonia is used as a transit country to get to Scandinavia rather than as a final destination. The migrants caught by police are detained and then sent back to Latvia in groups.

On Friday at around 3:30 p.m., a citizen informed police that eight dark-skinned men had exited a vehicle on J. Sütiste tee in Mustamäe, attracting attention.

After the men got out, the vehicle left the scene and the men began moving around the area.

Silver Hanikat, operations manager of the North Prefecture, said every additional pair of eyes is a great help to police in apprehending illegal immigrants.

"Thanks to the promptly provided information, police officers were able to respond quickly and detained the group of eight near an apartment building. Two men required medical assistance and were taken to hospital for further examination," he explained.

According to preliminary information, seven of those detained are from Somalia and one is from Algeria.

"All the detained men were in Estonia illegally and did not have any documents with them," the operations manager added.

World.title: US dollar edges down in Baghdad, holds steady in Erbil at 167,900 IQD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down slightly across Baghdad’s main currency exchanges on Saturday, October 31, 2026, while holding steady in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, at the opening of the weekly trading cycle.

According to market data, wholesale rates at Baghdad’s central Al-Kifah and Al-Harithiya exchanges slipped to 167,900 dinars per $100, marking a slight decline from 168,000 dinars recorded at the close of trading on Thursday.

Retail exchange desks across local markets in Baghdad saw retail selling rates stabilize at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, parallel trading counters maintained flat levels, quoting selling prices at 167,750 dinars alongside purchase bids of 167,650 dinars per $100.

World.title: Iraqi government denies 16 trillion dinar foreign loan reports to cover deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi federal government denied reports on Friday, October 30, 2026, alleging that Baghdad intends to borrow 16 trillion Iraqi dinars from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, China, Germany, and France to plug the sovereign budget deficit, confirming that state fiscal strategy relies on deploying domestic revenues to sustain public expenditures.

In statements delivered to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Government Spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi stated that widely circulated claims regarding foreign borrowing arrangements to offset budget shortfalls are entirely unfounded.

Al-Aboudi affirmed that there is no fiscal necessity for external borrowing, citing sustained crude export performance and favorable revenue flow.

Al-Aboudi explained that the executive administration adheres to a disciplined economic policy centered on optimizing state revenues to fund public commitments and sovereign operational requirements.

He noted that elevated crude export ceilings have bolstered treasury inflows, enabling the government to maximize available financial resources and fulfill state obligations without turning to foreign debt.

World.title: Health Minister highlights global partnerships at 6th Iraq International Health Expo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Health, Abdul-Hussein Aziz Al-Mousawi, underscored on Friday, October 30, 2026, the imperative of expanding international healthcare partnerships, transferring advanced medical technologies, and upgrading clinical healthcare delivery across the country.

Speaking during his inspection tour on the third day of the 6th Iraq International Health Exhibition and Conference, Al-Mousawi highlighted the exhibition’s role as a platform for exchanging technical expertise, acquiring advanced healthcare systems, and driving modernization across state and private healthcare infrastructure, according to a ministerial statement reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The minister commended the wide international turnout at this year’s edition, which brought together 375 healthcare corporations representing 24 countries.

Al-Mousawi noted that the significant global participation reflects growing commercial confidence in Iraq’s healthcare sector and opens viable investment pathways with international pharmaceutical and biomedical institutions.

During the walkthrough, Al-Mousawi inspected newly introduced medical diagnostic devices, surgical machinery, and specialized pharmaceutical supplies, engaging with company representatives and technical specialists on modern clinical solutions, hospital management technologies, and localized healthcare supply-chain integration.

World.title: Iraq to sign transit deals in Doha routing European internet traffic
World.content:
The Iraqi Ministry of Communications announced on Friday evening, October 30, 2026, that it will sign official agreements in Doha, Qatar, with three major nations to transit internet capacities through Iraqi territory to Europe.

The formal signing ceremony will take place on November 9, 2026, on the sidelines of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference and elections.

According to a ministerial statement, the strategic initiative is designed to solidify Iraq’s role as an international data transit bridge and a pivotal regional telecommunications hub linking the Middle East and Asia directly to European digital networks.

The ministry highlighted that this expansion will position Iraq as a global leader in the growth of terrestrial transit capacity volumes routed across sovereign territory over the preceding four months, advancing Baghdad’s broader strategy to monetize its geographic advantage as an alternative overland fiber corridor to undersea maritime routes.

World.title: Iraqi pharmacy sets Guinness World Record with 79,069 hydration pledges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has achieved a Guinness World Records title after Haya Pharmacy’s “Ghaith” hydration awareness campaign collected 79,069 pledges in one month, encouraging people across the country to adopt healthier water-drinking habits.

The initiative, which broke the record in Baghdad on October 5, 2026, got the highest pledges for a hydration awareness campaign in a single month.

The campaign, which was created in partnership with the Ebers marketing team, integrated community participation and public health awareness efforts to encourage regular water intake.

The campaign was strategically driven from Dubai, with teams from Ebers and Haya Pharmacy overseeing its execution on the ground in Iraq.

The success marks a significant milestone for Haya Pharmacy’s public health programs, demonstrating the effectiveness of national awareness campaigns in promoting better lives and community engagement.

World.title: Iraq signs agreement with Swiss pharma giant Roche
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Swiss pharmaceutical manufacturer Roche has inked a strategic partnership deal with Iraq’s Ministry of Health to strengthen healthcare services, with a focus on ophthalmology and hemophilia A.

In Baghdad, Swiss Ambassador Peter Nelson and officials from Roche and the Iraqi Health Ministry attended the signing of the agreement.

The partnership’s goal is to enhance patient care by strengthening diagnostic capacities, introducing sophisticated medical technology, and providing specialized training for Iraqi healthcare personnel.

Roche also reiterated its long-standing commitment to Iraq’s healthcare sector, emphasizing the necessity of working with government institutions to provide access to breakthrough therapies and medical knowledge.

The company thanked Iraqi Health Minister Dr. Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi for his support of foreign pharmaceutical companies and recognition of the significance of intellectual property protection in promoting medical innovation.

The arrangement is part of an attempt to modernize Iraq’s healthcare system and provide access to specialized medical services.

World.title: Maserati expands Iraq presence with new automotive partner
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Italian luxury carmaker Maserati has appointed Tiraz Automotive and Service Group as its new official partner in Iraq, aiming to strengthen its presence and expand customer access to the brand.

The deal was inked on September 18 in Modena, Italy, during a meeting between Maserati personnel and a Tiraz team headed by Kambiz Fathibitaraf.

Maserati hopes that the relationship would allow it to grow its operations in Iraq and provide consumers with a more personalized ownership experience, including access to its Fuoriserie customization program.

Customers may personalize their automobiles with various colors, materials, and design features that suit their specific interests.

The appointment is part of Maserati’s strategy to expand its presence in the Iraqi luxury automobile market and increase its local customer base.

World.title: Iraq signs gas capture agreement with US firm Morgan Hughes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US-based Morgan Hughes Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Iraq’s General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE) to develop projects aimed at capturing and utilizing associated gas currently flared at oil production sites across Iraq.

The agreement was signed in Baghdad by Morgan Hughes Energy Managing Director Gregory Bloom and GCCE, under the patronage of Iraq’s Minister of Environment, Sarwa Abdulwahid, and in the presence of US Chargé d’Affaires Steven Fagin.

The proposed partnership will focus on recovering low-pressure associated gas and using it to generate electricity for oil production facilities, reducing gas flaring and reliance on Iraq’s national electricity grid.

The initiative also aims to develop carbon credit projects using internationally recognized monitoring and verification standards, creating potential revenue opportunities through carbon markets while supporting Iraq’s emissions reduction targets.

Morgan Hughes Energy said it plans to bring American expertise and technology to the projects, supporting Iraq’s energy security and hydrocarbon development.

The company operates in the upstream and midstream oil and gas sectors, with interests across the Middle East, including offshore gas production, pipeline infrastructure, and gas storage facilities.

The MoU represents an initial step towards a broader strategic partnership between the two companies, with specific projects still subject to further development.

Nepal PM Balen Shah is expected to seek Indian aid for flood reconstruction, fresh hydropower investment and faster progress on stalled infrastructure projects during his proposed visit later this month

World.title: Authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions: Justice Bhuyan
World.content:
âShun the binary of âusâ & âtheyâ; adopt âweâ for unity in diversity,â said Justice Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At a time when the opposition has branded the NDA govt authoritarian, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan Saturday said authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions, and stressed people must shed the binary of 'us' and 'they' and adopt the core constitutional philosophy of 'we' to preserve the country's unity in diversity.Speaking at the convocation ceremony of University of Science and Technology Meghalaya, the SC judge said, "A society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism. A society that treats tradition as beyond scrutiny may fail to reform unjust practices."Highlighting Article 51A of the Constitution that casts a duty on every citizen to develop a scientific temperament, Justice Bhuyan said, "It does not merely ask us to acquire scientific knowledge. It asks us to cultivate a temperament which is based on reason. It tells us to inquire, to question, to examine and, where necessary, to reform."He said, "I believe, scientific temperament lays the foundation for the rule of law. This is because arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear and unexamined belief. A society that accepts claims without evidence is susceptible to superstitious beliefs and becomes vulnerable to misinformation."Attaching great importance to debate, he said those who ask questions must also be willing to listen to a different point of view. "Willingness to reason together through a meaningful debate alone can make a society stronger," he said, adding that questions followed by meaningful and healthy debates can happen only when people have access to information.Inspired by Nobel laureate Amartya Sen's 'The Idea of Justice', which he quoted extensively during the speech, Justice Bhuyan elaborated on the difference between 'institutional democracy' and 'functional democracy' and said that a functional democracy requires public questioning and scrutiny. "Circulation of information and scrutiny by public reasoning thus becomes part of the due process by which a democratic society resonates with justice. "He said preservation of diversity demands shunning false narratives and the binary of 'us' and 'they'."For a more just and humane society, it is important that we move away from the destructive binary of 'us' and 'they' and embrace the idea of oneness," he said."Not for nothing, the Preamble to the Constitution starts with the expression - 'We, the People of India'. The Constitution... speaks to all citizens of India as equal members of the constitutional order. Therefore, 'we' represents a larger idea of belonging in which our individual identities or group identities do not diminish our shared constitutional unity," he said.In what could be construed as indirect opposition to Uniform Civil Code, he said, "It does not require that our individual identities should get subsumed in the larger whole. Diversity, therefore, is not an impediment to the constitutional project; rather, it infuses substance and meaning to it."

World.title: NC faces revolt as 25 MLAs seek removal of ministers, Omar aide
World.content:
SRINAGAR: J&K CM

faces a growing revolt within National Conference (NC), with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy CM, within 15 days and removal of his close aide and political adviser Nasir Aslam Wani.

At a meeting at NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Loneâs home Friday evening, legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated. Around 18 MLAs attended in person and seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present. NC has 41 MLAs in 90-member assembly and runs a coalition govt with six Congress, six independent and one CPM legislator.

âSo far there is no next step. The first step was a big step to bring democracy within the party,â the legislator said. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the âlarger good of the partyâ.

NC provincial president for Kashmir Showkat Mir confirmed the meeting but played down its significance, saying it was not directed against the party. He said some senior legislators wanted an appointment with NC president Farooq Abdullah.





âEveryone wants to become a minister but the CM can appoint only eight in UT set up,â Mir said, adding that 24 legislators could be accommodated in the cabinet if statehood was restored.

Omar, 56, and his father Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi, where the CM celebrated his wedding with journalist Nidhi Razdan. Sharing a photograph on social media, Omar wrote: âA new journey began yesterday.â On July 31, Supreme Court granted Omar a divorce after being informed that he and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah had settled their matrimonial dispute through mediation.

The NC turmoil came as party MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi prepared to quit the party and surrender his Lok Sabha seat on Nov 3, accusing Omar and his ministers of betraying the partyâs promises on restoration of Article 370 and protection of J&Kâs rights.

âThe crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family,â Mehdi wrote on X. He accused NC of seeking votes on promises to restore Article 370 and release prisoners, only to abandon them after assuming office.

Mehdi will address people at Budgam on Nov 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, a Congress politician and prominent Shiite cleric assassinated in a terrorist attack on Nov 3, 2000. Mehdi has been among Omarâs sharpest critics, accusing him of abandoning NCâs manifesto.
